Still 'tis His hand that leadeth me.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Lord, I would clasp Thy hand in mine,
Since 'tis my God that leadeth me.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: And when my task on earth is done,
When, by Thy grace, the vict'ry's won
E'en death's cold wave I will not flee
If God through Jordan leadeth me.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: He leadeth me! He leadeth me!
By His own hand He leadeth me.

title: He lives—the great Redeemer lives;
author: Anne Steele (1760)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: What joy the blest assurance gives!
And now before His Father, God,
Pleads the full merit of His blood.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: On Thee do all our hopes depend:
Our cause can never, never fail,
For Thou dost plead, and must prevail.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: When sin and Satan join their power,
Let this blest truth repel each dart,
That Thou dost bear us on Thy heart.

title: Here o'er the earth as a stranger I roam
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Here o'er the earth as a stranger I roam,
Here is no rest—is no rest;
Here as a pilgrim I wander alone,
Yet I am blest—I am blest.
For I look forward to that glorious day
When sin and sorrow shall vanish away;
My heart doth leap while I hear Jesus say,
There, there is rest—there is rest.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Here are afflictions and trials severe,
Here is no rest—is no rest;
Here I must part with the friends I hold dear,
Yet I am blest—I am blest.
Sweet is the promise I read in Thy Word;
Blessed are they who have died in the Lord;
They have been called to receive their reward;
There, there is rest—there is rest.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: This world of care is a wilderness state,
Here is no rest—is no rest;
But I must bear from the world all its hate,
Yet I am blest—I am blest.
Soon shall I be from the wicked released;
Soon shall the weary for ever be blest;
Soon shall I lean upon Jesus' breast;
There, there is rest—there is rest.

title: He sitteth o'er the waterfloods
author: Richard Whateley

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: And He is strong to save;

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Though loud around the vessel's prow
The waves may toss and break;
Yet at His word they sink to rest

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: As in the days of old,
When o'er the Saviour's sinless head

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Yea, all the billows passed o'er Him;
For us He met th' o'erwhelming storm,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Then doubt and fear no more,
For He who passed through all the storms

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Will soon be moored in harbour calm,

title: Holy Saviour! We adore Thee
author: Samuel Prideaux Tregelles (1838)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Seated on the throne of God;
While the heavenly hosts before Thee
We are ransomed by Thy blood.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Saviour! Though the world despised Thee,
Yet the Father's glory raised Thee,
We shall live, for Thou hast died.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: And though here on earth rejected,
Than like Thee our Lord to be?
Thou from earth hast set us free.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Haste the day of Thy returning
With Thy ransomed Church to reign;
Then shall end our days of mourning,
We shall sing with rapture then:

title: Hope of our hearts, O Lord, appear!
author: Sir Edward Denny

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Hope of our hearts, O Lord, appear!
Shine forth, and chase the dreary night!

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: No resting-place we seek on earth,
Our eye is on the royal crown,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: What is it to the brighter hope

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: What to the joy, the deeper joy,
Of union with our living Head,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: This joy e'en now on earth is ours'
Our hearts, without a pang, shall know

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: There, near Thy heart, upon the throne,
What grace was in the bleeding Lamb,
Who died to make us free.

title: How bright that blessed hope!
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Let us our heads lift up,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Let us the cross take up
Shame, for His sake, to share,
Since we the crown shall wear

title: How firm a foundation, ye saints of the Lord
author: Rippon's Selection & Richard Keen (1787) (1787)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: How firm a foundation, ye saints of the Lord,
Is laid for your faith in His excellent Word!
What more can He say than to you He hath said,
You who to the Saviour for refuge have fled?

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Fear not, He is with thee; oh, be not dismayed!
He—He is thy God, and will still give thee aid;
He'll strengthen thee, help thee, and cause thee to stand,
Upheld by His righteous, omnipotent hand.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: The soul that on Jesus has leaned for repose,
He will not, He cannot desert to its foes;
That soul, though all hell should endeavor to shake,

title: How good is the God we adore
author: Joseph Hart (1759)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: How good is the God we adore,
Whose love is as great as His power,
And knows neither measure nor end.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: 'Tis Jesus, the First and the Last,
Whose Spirit shall guide us safe home;
We'll praise Him for all that is past,
And trust Him for all that's to come.

title: How sweet the Name of Jesus sounds
author: John Newton (1779)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: How sweet the Name of Jesus sounds
It soothes his sorrows, heals his wounds,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: It makes the wounded spirit whole,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Dear Name! The Rock on which we build;

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Our Lord, our Life, our Way, our End,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Weak is the effort of our heart,
But when we see Thee as Thou art
We'll praise Thee as we ought.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Till then we would Thy love proclaim
And triumph in that blessed Name
Which quells the power of death.

title: I'm but a stranger here;
author: Thomas Rawson Taylor (1836)

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I shall reach home at last;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: There with the good and blest,
Those I've loved most and best,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: There at my Lord's right hand;

title: I am waiting for the dawning
author: Samuel Trevor Francis

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I am waiting for the dawning
Of the bright and blessed day,
When the darksome night of sorrow
When for ever with the Saviour,
Far beyond this vale of tears,
I shall swell the song of worship

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I am looking at the brightness,
Of the clear and joyous beaming
Of the Bright and Morning Star.
Through the dark grey mist of morning
Do I see its glorious light;
Of this sad and weary night.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: I am waiting for the coming
Of the Lord who died for me;
O His words have thrilled my spirit,
I will come again for thee,
I can almost hear His footfall
On the threshold of the door,
And my heart, my heart is longing

title: I am a stranger here
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: No home, no rest I see;
Not all men count most dear
Should win a sigh from me:

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Home, O how soft and sweet,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: And when the world looks cold,
I can look up and smile:

title: I'm a pilgrim and stranger
author: Mary Dana

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Rough and thorny is the road,
Often in the midst of danger,
Clouds and darkness oft distress me,
Great and many are my foes;
Anxious cares and thoughts oppress me:

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: O how sweet is this assurance
Home in prospect still can cheer me;
Yes, and give me sweet repose,
While I feel His presence near me:

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Yes, He sees and knows me daily;
Sends me help when foes assail me,
Soon my journey will be ended,
Life is drawing to a close;
I shall then be well attended:

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: I shall then with joy behold Him,
Face to face my Saviour see;
Fall with rapture and adore Him
Nothing more shall then distress me
In the land of sweet repose;
Jesus stands engaged to bless me:

title: I'm waiting for Thee, Lord
author: Hannah Kilham Burlingham

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I'm waiting for Thee, for Thy coming again.
Thy home I shall share at Thy coming again.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The day must be near of Thy coming again
But glory so fair at thy coming again.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O hasten the day of Thy coming again!
This is not my rest, Lord;
I wait to be blest at Thy coming again.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: I'll meet them once more at Thy coming again.
The blood was the sign, Lord,
That marked them as Thine, Lord,
And brightly they'll shine at Thy coming again.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: E'en now let my ways, Lord,
Be bright with Thy praise, Lord,
For brief are the days ere Thy coming again.
No triumph for me like Thy coming again.

title: I am watching for the morning
author: Boethia Thompson

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I am watching for the morning,
I am looking for the dawning
I am watching for the morning
I am waiting for the meeting,
I am longing for the greeting;
I am waiting for the meeting

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I am gazing up for Thee, Lord,
Until Thy face I see, Lord;
I am gazing up for Thee, Lord,
Of that great and full salvation;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: How I long to see Thy smile, Lord,
When has passed the little while, Lord;
How I long to see Thy smile, Lord,
O to see the beam of gladness
On that face once marred with sadness;
O to see the beam of gladness

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O to see the morning breaking,
O the joy of such awaking;
O to see the morning breaking
To be caught up, Lord, for ever,
To be parted, Lord, no never;
To be with Thee, Lord, for ever

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: With the Lord to be for ever,
With the saints to be together;
With the Lord to be for ever

title: I bless the Christ of God;
author: Horatius Bonar (1861)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I bless the Christ of God;
And with unfalt'ring lip and heart

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Each thought of unbelief and fear,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: I praise the God of grace,
I trust His truth and might;
He calls me His, I call Him mine,
My God, my joy, my light.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: In me is only ill; My ill

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: I love because He loveth me,

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: My life with Him is hid,
My clouds have melted into light,

title: I bow me to Thy will, O God
author: Frederick William Faber

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I bow me to Thy will, O God,
And every day I live I'd seek
To please Thee more and more.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Why should I care, O blessed Lord?
Since all my cares are Thine;
Why not in triumph live, since Thou

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Faith's pilgrim sons behind Thee seek
The road that Thou hast gone.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: He always wins who sides with God,
To him no chance is lost;
God's will is sweetest to him when

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Ill that God blesses is our good,
And all is right that seems most wrong,
If it be His sweet will.

title: I have been at the altar and witnessed the Lamb
author: Amelia Matilda Hull

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I have been at the altar and witnessed the Lamb
Burnt wholly to ashes for me;
And watched its sweet savour ascending on high,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: And lo, while I gazed at the glorious sight,
A voice from above reached mine ears:
By this thine iniquity's taken away,
And no trace of it on thee appears.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: An end of thy sin has been made for thee here
By Him who its penalty bore;
With blood it is blotted eternally out,
And I will not remember it more.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O Lord, I believe it with wonder and joy;
While daily I learn that I am in myself
Of sinners the vilest and chief.

title: I have a home above
author: Henry Bennett

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: He passed through death's dark raging flood

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: He leads me onward to the home

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: I soon shall greet them on that shore

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: But more than all, I long
Whose smile fills all the radiant throng

stanzas.label: Verse 7
lines: Shall cheer me through the little while

stanzas.label: Verse 8
lines: My joy and strength shall be,
Till Thou shalt speak the gladd'ning word
That bids me rise to Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 9
lines: In happier, holier strains I'll praise
The grace that made me Thine.

title: I heard the voice of Jesus say
author: Horatius Bonar (1846)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I heard the voice of Jesus say,
Lay down, thou weary one, lay down

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I came to Jesus as I was,
I found in Him a resting-place,
And He has made me glad.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: I heard the voice of Jesus say.
Stoop down, and drink, and live.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: I came to Jesus, and I drank
My thirst was quenched, my soul revived,
And now I live in Him.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: I heard the voice of Jesus say,
I am this dark world's Light:
Look unto Me, thy morn shall rise,
And all thy day be bright.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: I looked to Jesus, and I found
In Him my Star, my Sun;
And in that light of life I'll walk

title: I hear the words of love
author: Horatius Bonar (1846)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I hear the words of love,
And I have peace with God.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: The clouds may go and come,
And storms may sweep my sky;

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: My joy still ebbs and flows,
But peace with Him remains the same,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: His love, not mine, the resting-place,
His truth, not mine, the tie.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Though heaven is now His home;
The mighty stone is rolled away,

stanzas.label: Verse 7
lines: The grave of all my woes!
I know the Son of God has come,
I know He died and rose.

stanzas.label: Verse 8
lines: I know the throne on which He sits,
I know His truth and love.

title: I journey through a desert drear and wild
author: Mary Jane Deck Walker

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I journey through a desert drear and wild,
Yet is my heart by such sweet thoughts beguiled
Of Him on whom I lean, my Strength, my Stay.
I can forget the sorrows of the way.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thoughts of His love—the root of ev'ry grace
Which finds in this poor heart a dwelling-place;
The sunshine of my soul, than day more bright,
And my calm pillow of repose by night.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thoughts of His sojourn in this vale of tears;
The tale of love unfolded in those years
Of sinless suffering and patient grace,
I love again and yet again to trace.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Thoughts of His glory—on the Cross I gaze,
And there behold its sad yet healing rays;
Beacon of hope which, lifted up on high,
Illumes with heavenly light the tear-dimmed eye.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Thoughts of His coming; for that joyful day
In patient hope I watch, and wait, and pray;
The dawn draws nigh, the midnight shadows flee,
O what a sunrise will that advent be!

title: I hear the accuser roar
author: Samuel Whitlock Gandy

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Of ills that I have done;
I know them well, and thousands more;

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Let but my risen Lord appear,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: To fight and force me from my ground

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: I meet them face to face
March in the triumph of His grace

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: There, in His book I bear

stanzas.label: Verse 7
lines: He won the meed and crown;
Trod all our foes beneath His feet

stanzas.label: Verse 8
lines: He hell in hell laid low;
Bowed to the grave, destroyed it so,

stanzas.label: Verse 9
lines: Who lived, who died, who lives again,
For thee, His Church, for thee.

title: I left it all with Jesus long ago;
author: Ellen H. Willis (1876)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I left it all with Jesus long ago;
All my sins I brought Him, and my woe:
When by faith I saw Him on the tree,
Heard His still, small whisper, Tis for thee,
From my heart the burden rolled away:
From my heart the burden rolled away:

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I leave it all with Jesus, for He knows
How to steal the bitter from life's woes;
How to gild the tear-drop with His smile,
Make the desert garden bloom awhile:
When my weakness leaneth on His might
When my weakness leaneth on His might

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: I leave it all with Jesus day by day;
Faith can firmly trust Him, come what may:
Hope has dropped her anchor, found her rest
In the calm, sure haven of His breast;
Love esteems it heaven to abide
Love esteems it heaven to abide

title: I need Thee, precious Saviour!
author: Frederick Whitfield

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Thou art all to me;
The blood of Christ most precious,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I need Thy love, Lord Jesus!
To cheer me on my way,
To be my strength and stay.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: I need a friend like Thee;
A friend to soothe and comfort,
A friend to care for me.
I need Thy heart, Lord Jesus!

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: I need Thy light, Lord Jesus!
To guide me safe to glory
Where I shall see my God.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: I need Thee day by day
To fill me with Thy fullness,
To lead me on my way.
To teach me what I am,
To show me more of Jesus,
To point me to the Lamb.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: And hope to see Thee soon,
To sing Thy praise, Lord Jesus,

title: I once was a stranger to grace and to God;
author: Robert Murray McCheyne (1837)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I once was a stranger to grace and to God;
I knew not my danger, I felt not my load;
Though friends spoke in rapture of Christ on the tree,
JEHOVAH TSIDKENU was nothing to me.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Like tears from the daughters of Zion that roll,
I wept when the waters went over His soul;
Yet thought not that my sins had nailed to the tree

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: When free grace awoke me by light from on high,
Then legal fears shook me, I trembled to die;
No refuge, no safety in self could I see,
JEHOVAH TSIDKENU my Saviour must be.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: My terrors all vanished before the sweet Name;
My guilty fears banished, with boldness I came
To drink at the fountain, life-giving and free;
JEHOVAH TSIDKENU is all things to me.

title: I saw the Cross of Jesus
author: George Müller & Frederick Whitfield (1875)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I saw the Cross of Jesus
I sought the Cross of Jesus
I brought my sins to Jesus,
He cleansed them in His blood;
And in the Cross of Jesus
I found my peace with God.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I love the Cross of Jesus;
It tells me what I am:
Yet in the Cross I glory,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Sweet is the Cross of Jesus;
And then in strains of glory
And death is known no more.

title: I thirst, but not as once I did
author: William Cowper

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I thirst, but not as once I did,
The vain delights of earth to share;
That I should seek my pleasure there.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: It was the sight of Thy dear Cross
First weaned my soul from earthly things,
And taught me to esteem as dross
The mirth of fools and pomp of kings.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: No longer sink below the brim;
But overflow, and pour me down

title: In seasons of grief to my God I'll repair
author: John Price

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: In seasons of grief to my God I'll repair
When my heart is o'erwhelmed with sorrow and care;
From the ends of the earth to Thee will I cry,
Lead me to the Rock that is higher than I.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: When Satan, my foe, shall come in like a flood
To drive my poor soul from the Fountain of good,
I'll pray to the Saviour who meekly did die;
Lead me to the Rock that is higher than I.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: And while as a stranger I sojourn below,
Thy covenant blessing, Lord, freely bestow;
In affliction's dark night to Thy throne let me fly,
Lead me to the Rock that is higher than I.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: And when the last trumpet shall sound through the skies,
And the dead in Christ Jesus immortal shall rise,
With the ransomed I'll praise Him above yonder sky,
Built firm on the Rock that is higher than I.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Higher than I, higher than I,
Lead me to the Rock that is higher than I.

title: I would commune with Thee, my God;
author: Goerge Burden Bubier

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I would commune with Thee, my God;
E'en to Thy seat I come;
I leave my joys, I leave my sins,
And seek in Thee my home.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I stand upon the mount of God
I hear the storms in vales beneath;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: But I am calm with Thee, my God,
And to the height on which I stand
Nor storms nor clouds can rise.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O this is life! O this is joy!
My God, to find Thee so;
Thy face to see, Thy voice to hear,
And all Thy love to know.

title: It passeth knowledge, that dear love of Thine
author: Mary Shekleton (1863)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: It passeth knowledge, that dear love of Thine,
Lord Jesus, Saviour; yet this soul of mine
Would of Thy love, in all its breadth and length,
Its height and depth, its everlasting strength

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: It passeth telling, that dear love of Thine,
Lord Jesus Saviour; yet these lips of mine
Would fain proclaim to sinners, far and near,
A love which can remove all guilt and fear,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: It passeth praises, that dear love of Thine,
Lord Jesus, Saviour; yet this heart of mine
Would sing that love, so full, so rich, so free,
Which brings a rebel sinner, even me,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: But though I cannot sing, or tell, or know
The fullness of Thy love while here below,
My empty vessel I may freely bring;
O Thou, who art of love the living spring,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Then fill me, O my Saviour, with Thy love!
Lead, lead me to the living fount above;
Thither may I in simple faith draw nigh,
And never to another fountain fly,

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: And when, Lord Jesus, Thine own face I see,
When at Thy lofty throne I bow the knee,
Then of Thy love, in all its breadth and length,
Its height and depth, its everlasting strength,

title: I will sing of my Redeemer
author: Philip Paul Bliss (1876)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I will sing of my Redeemer,
And His wondrous love to me;
On the cruel Cross He suffered,
From the curse to set me free.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I will tell the wondrous story,
How my lost estate to save,
In His boundless love and mercy

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: I will praise my dear Redeemer,
Over sin, and death, and Hell.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: I will sing of my Redeemer,
And His heav'nly love to me;
He from death to life hath brought me,
Son of God, with him to be.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Sing, O sing of my Redeemer!
With His blood He purchased me!
On the Cross He sealed my pardon,
Paid the debt and made me free.

title: I've found a Friend; O such a Friend!
author: James Grindlay Small (1863)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I've found a Friend; O such a Friend!
He loved me ere I knew Him;
He drew me with the cords of love,
And thus He bound me to Him.
And round my heart still closely twine
Those ties which nought can sever,
For I am Christ's and He is mine,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I've found a Friend; O such a Friend!
He bled, He died to save me;
And not alone the gift of life,
But His own self He gave me.
Nought that I have, mine own I'll call,
I'll hold it for the Giver:
My heart, my strength, my life, my all,
Are His, and His for ever.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: I've found a Friend; O such a Friend!
All power to Him is given
To guard me on my onward course
And bring me safe to heaven.
So now to watch! To work! To war!
And then to rest for ever.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: I've found a Friend; O such a Friend!
So kind, and true, and tender,
So wise a Counsellor and Guide,
From Him, who loves me now so well,
What power my soul can sever?
Shall life? Or death? shall earth? or hell?
No! I am His for ever.

title: I've found a joy in sorrow
author: Jane Fox Crewdson (1864)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I've found a joy in sorrow,
I've found a branch of healing

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I've found the Rock of Ages

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: So near! yet out of sight.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: I have the joy, the balm,

title: I was a wand'ring sheep
author: Horatius Bonar (1843)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I did not love the fold;
I did not love my Shepherd's voice,
I did not love my home;
I did not love my Father's voice

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: And followed me o'er vale and hill,
Yea, found me nigh to death,
And bound me with the bands of love,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: 'Twas He that cleansed me by His blood,
'Twas He that brought me to the fold,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: I love my tender Shepherd's voice,
I seek no more to roam;
I love my heav'nly Father's voice,
I love, I love His home.

title: It may be at morn
author: H.L. Turner (1878)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: To receive from the world His own.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: In the blaze of His glory

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: How long—ere we shout the glad song?

title: I've found the precious Christ of God
author: John Mason

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I've found the precious Christ of God,
My heart doth sing for joy;
And sing I must, for Christ I have,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Christ Jesus is the Lord of lords,
He is the King of kings;
He is the Sun of Righteousness

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Christ is my meat, Christ is my drink,
My peace, my strength, my joy, my crown,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Christ is my Shepherd and my Friend,
My Head, my Hope, my Counsellor,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Christ Jesus is the heaven of heaven;
My Christ what shall I call?
Christ is the First, Christ is the Last,
And Christ is all in all.

title: Jehovah is our strength
author: Samuel Bernard

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: And He shall be our song;
In vain then Satan doth oppose,
For God is stronger than His foes.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Since He hath made us His
For God is stronger than His foes.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: What can we wish for more?
As long as we are His
In vain do earth and hell oppose,
For God is stronger than His foes.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: And since we now are His,
His care our souls will feed:
In vain do sin and death oppose
For God is stronger than His foes.

title: Jesus is our Shepherd, wiping ev'ry tear
author: Hugh Stowell

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus is our Shepherd, wiping ev'ry tear,
Folded in His bosom what have we to fear?
Only let us follow whither He doth lead,
To the thirsty desert, or the dewy mead.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Jesus is our Shepherd, well we know His voice!
How its gentlest whisper makes our hearts rejoice:
Even when He chideth, tender is his tone;
None but He shall guide us; we are His alone.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Jesus is our Shepherd; for the sheep He bled;
Ev'ry lamb is sprinkled with the blood He shed;
Then on each He setteth His own secret sign.
They that have My Spirit, these, saith He, are Mine.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Jesus is our Shepherd; guarded by His arm,
Though the wolves may ravin none can do us harm;
If we tread death's valley, dark with fearful gloom,
We shall fear no evil, victors o'er the tomb.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Jesus is our Shepherd; with His goodness now,
And His tender mercy, He doth us endow.
Let us sing His praises with a gladsome heart
Till in heaven we meet Him, nevermore to part.

title: Jesus Christ, Thou King of Glory
author: Hannah Kilham Burlingham

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus Christ, Thou King of Glory,
Singing of Thy grace the story,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thou the bands of death didst sever,
God is for us now and ever;
We joy in Thee. We are Thine,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thou the ransom price hast given,
Thou art Lord of earth and heaven;
Through Thy blood we stand forgiven,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Sweet and full our song shall be;
Thou hast read our spirits' yearning,

title: Jesus, in His heav'nly temple
author: Robert Cleaver Chapman

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Sits with God upon the throne;
Now no more to be forsaken,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Smite the Shepherd with the sword;
Set at nought our glorious Lord.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Jesus fills all heav'n with incense

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: On His heart our names are graven;
On His shoulders we are borne;
Of our God beloved in Jesus
We can love Him in return.

title: Jesus is coming! Sing the glad word!
author: Edwin Hutch & Daniel Webster Whittle

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus is coming! Sing the glad word!
Coming for those He redeemed by His blood,
Coming to reign as the glorified Lord!

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Jesus is coming! The dead shall arise,
Loved ones shall meet in a joyful surprise,
Caught up together to Him in the skies:

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Jesus is coming! His saints to release;
Coming to give to the warring earth peace;
Sinning, and sighing, and sorrow, shall cease:

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Jesus is coming! The promise is true;
Who are the chosen, the faithful, the few
Waiting and watching, prepared for review?

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Jesus is coming, is coming again!
Shout the glad tidings o'er mountain and plain,

title: Jesus, Lord, I'm never weary
author: Boethia Thompson

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Looking on Thy Cross and shame;
Gazing there I seem so near Thee,
Dear to me each throb of pain.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Little cared I for the anguish
Left alone, Lord, there to languish,
None to share Thy parting sigh.
Left alone, O Lord, to die.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Jesus, Saviour, I have found Thee
In Thyself, Lord, Thou hast found me
From my soul by love inspired.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: All my sins were laid upon Thee,
All my guilt was on Thee laid,
And the blood of Thine atonement
All my utmost debt has paid.
I believe, for Thou hast said.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Thine almighty arms are round me,
And my head is on Thy breast,
For my weary soul has found Thee
Now I know that I am blest.

title: Jesus, Lord, we know Thee present
author: Boethia Thompson

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus, Lord, we know Thee present
From all fear and doubt set free;
Here to rest, so sweetly able,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Of Thy precious blood once shed.
Lord, we take each simple token
And Thy blood shed on the tree.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O what joy it is to see Thee
In the bread and wine of blessing,
Bread to strengthen, wine to cheer.
Thus to take the cup of blessing,
Thus to share the broken bread.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Lord, we know how true Thy promise
To be with us where we meet,
When in Thy loved Name we gather
That we soon will be with Thee, Lord
And for ever where Thou art.

title: Jesus! Source of life eternal
author: Ernst Christoph Homburg tr/ad by Hannah Kilham Burlingham

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: By defeat and shame and death.
Deigned to pass for our salvation:

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thou, O Son of God, wert bearing
Thou, the King of Glory, wearing,
For our sake, the crown of thorn;
From the chains of sin for ever:

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: All the shame men heaped upon Thee,
Not the pains of death too bitter

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Saviour, thus to Thee we give;
For Thy death, whereby we live.
All the grief Thou wert enduring,
All the bliss Thou wert securing:

title: Jesus! O Name of power divine
author: Frederick Whitfield

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus! O Name of power divine

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Each bitter grief, each anxious care,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Here, love may meet a kindred heart,
But not a heart like Thine;
Lord, from Thy love I cannot part,
Nor canst Thou part with mine.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: With Thee I cannot feel alone,
Though friends are changing one by one,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: My future path, I know, may be
But love has planned that path for me,
That love in which I share.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: And is it not, O Lord, enough
Till Thou shalt call Thy Bride above,
To meet Thee in the air?

stanzas.label: Verse 7
lines: It is enough; Thy tender smile,
Shall cheer me through the little while

title: Joy! joy! joy! there is joy in heav'n with angels
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Joy! joy! joy! there is joy in heav'n with angels,
Joy! joy! joy! for the prodigal's return;
He has come, he has come
To his Father's house at last;
He was lost, he is found,
And the night of gloom is past.
Blessed hour of joy and communion sweet,
For his heart is full and his love complete;
His Father sees him and hastes to meet,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Joy! joy! joy! in the courts of heav'n resounding;
Joy! joy! joy! o'er the prodigal's return;
Hark, the song! hark, the song!
While his eye is dim with the falling tears
Of repented grief, over wasted years
The pard'ning voice of his Father cheers,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Joy! joy! joy! in the radiant fields of glory,
Joy! joy! joy! when wand'ring soul returns;
Let us haste, let us haste
While the morning sun is bright;
To a land of love and light:
We will journey on till our pilgrim feet
Shall be found at last in the golden street:
Our glorious Saviour will smile to greet,

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Joy! joy! joy! there is joy in heaven with the angels;
Joy! joy! joy! for the prodigal's return.

title: Just as Thou art, how wondrous fair
author: Joseph Denham Smith

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Just as Thou art, how wondrous fair,
Lord Jesus, all Thy members are:
A life divine to them is given,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Just as I was I came to Thee,
An heir of wrath and misery;
Just as Thou art before the throne,
I stand in righteousness Thine own.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Just as Thou art, how wondrous free:
Loosed by the sorrows of the tree:
Saviour! the curse, the wrath were Thine,
To give Thy saints this life divine.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Just as Thou art, nor doubt, nor fear
O timeless love! as Thee, I'm seen
The righteousness of God in Him.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Just as Thou art, Thou Lamb divine!
Life, light, and holiness are Thine:
Thyself their endless source I see,
And they, the life of God, in me.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Just as Thou art, O blissful ray
That turned my darkness into day!
That woke me from my death in sin
To know my perfectness in Him.

stanzas.label: Verse 7
lines: O teach me, Lord, this grace to own,
That self and sin no more are known:
That love, Thy love, in wondrous right,
Hath placed me in its spotless light.

stanzas.label: Verse 8
lines: Soon, soon, 'mid joys on joys untold,
Thou wilt this grace and love unfold,
Till worlds on worlds and adoring see
The part Thy members have in Thee.

title: Jesus, Lover of my soul
author: Charles Wesley (1740)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Let me to Thy bosom fly
While the billows near me roll,
While the tempest still is high:
Hide me, O my Saviour, hide
Till the storm of life is past;
O receive my soul at last.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Hangs my helpless soul on Thee;
Leave, ah! leave me not alone,
All my hope on Thee is stayed,
All my help from Thee I bring;
With the shadow of Thy wing.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Plenteous grace with Thee is found,
Grace to pardon all my sin;
Make and keep me pure within.
Thou of life the fountain art;
Freely let me take of Thee;
Spring Thou up within my heart

title: Jesus, the Lord our Righteousness!
author: Nikolaus Ludwig von ZinzendorfTranslated by John WesleyAlternate first line: God's Christ, who is my righteousness

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Our beauty Thou, our glorious dress;
With joy shall we lift up our head.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Bold shall we stand in that great day,
For who aught to our charge shall lay?
While by Thy blood absolved we are
From sin's tremendous curse and fear.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thus Abraham, the friend of God,
Thus all the saints redeemed by blood,
And all their boast is in Thy Name.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Till we behold Thee on Thy throne,
In Thee we boast, in Thee alone;
Our beauty this, our glorious dress,

title: Kept, safely kept;
author: William Blane

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: In weakness to my God I cling,
Though foes be strong I calmly sing,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The strength of God's almighty arm
Doth shield my soul from every harm,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Unshaken on my God I lean,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: His mighty love ne'er cold shall wax,
Nor shall His pow'rful grasp relax,

title: Lamb of God! our souls adore Thee
author: James George Deck (1841)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lamb of God! our souls adore Thee
While upon Thy face we gaze;
There the Father's love and glory
Shine in all their brightest rays.
Heaven and earth alike confess Thee
As the ever great I AM.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Lamb of God! Thy Father's bosom
One with Him in power and grace:
O what wondrous love and mercy!
Thou didst lay Thy glory by
And for us didst come from heaven,
As the Lamb of God, to die.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Lamb of God! when we behold Thee
In the world Thy hands had made;
When we see Thee in the garden
At Thy grace we are confounded,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: When we see Thee, as the Victim,
For our guilt and folly stricken,
All our judgment borne by Thee.
Lord, we own, with hearts adoring,
Thou hast loved us unto blood;
Be to Thee, Thou Lamb of God!

title: Lamb of God! Thou now art seated
author: James George Deck (1841)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lamb of God! Thou now art seated
Every knee in heaven is bending
To the Lamb for sinners slain;
Every voice and harp is swelling,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Lord, in all Thy pow'r and glory,
Still Thy thoughts and eyes are here,
To Thy gracious heart so dear.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Lamb of God! Thou soon in glory
Wilt to this sad earth return;
All Thy foes shall quake before Thee,
All that now despise Thee mourn;
Then Thy saints all gathered to Thee
With Thee in Thy kingdom reign;
Thine the praise, and Thine the glory
Lamb of God, for sinners slain.

title: Let us love and sing and wonder!
author: John Newton (1774)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Let us love and sing and wonder!
Let us praise the Saviour's Name!
He has hushed the law's loud thunder,
He has quenched mount Sinai's flame;
He has washed us in His blood,
He has brought us nigh to God.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Let us love the Lord that bought us,
Called us by His grace, and taught us
Where our joys and blessings are;
He has washed us in His blood,
He presents our souls to God.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Let us sing, though fierce temptation
Threaten hard to bear us down;
For the Lord, our strong salvation,
Holds in view the conq'ror's crown;
He who washed us in His blood,
Has secured our way to God.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Let us wonder; grace and justice
Join, and point to mercy's store;
When through grace in Christ our trust is
Justice smiles, and asks no more;
He who washed us in His blood
Soon will bring us home to God.

title: Let us rejoice in Christ the Lord
author: John Newton (1774)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Let us rejoice in Christ the Lord
Who claims us for His own;
The hope established on His Word

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Though many foes beset us round,
Our life is hid with Christ in God

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Weak as we are, we shall not faint
Jesus, the strength of every saint,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Though now He's unperceived by sense
Our guide, our glory, our defence.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: So surely those that trust His Name

title: Lord, accept our feeble song;
author: Thomas Kelly

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Power and praise to Thee belong;
We would all Thy grace record,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Rich in glory, Thou didst stoop,
Thence is all Thy people's hope;
Thou wast poor, that we might be
Rich in glory, Lord, with Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: When we think of love like this,
Joy and shame our hearts possess;
Joy, that Thou couldst pity thus;
Shame for such returns from us.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Yet we soon the day shall see
When we shall from sin be free;
When, to Thee in glory brought,
We shall serve Thee as we ought.

title: Look, ye saints, the sight is glorious;
author: Thomas Kelly

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Look, ye saints, the sight is glorious;
See the Man of Sorrows now;
Every knee to Him shall bow:

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Crown the Saviour, angels crown Him;
In the seat of power enthrone Him,
While the vault of heaven rings;
Crown the Saviour, King of kings.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Saints and angels crowd around Him,
Own His title, praise His Name:

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O what joy the sight affords!
King of kings, and Lord of lords.

title: Lord Jesus, are we one with Thee?
author: James George Deck (1837)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lord Jesus, are we one with Thee?
O height, O depth of love!
Once slain for us upon the tree,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Our sins, our guilt, in love divine,
The gall, the curse, the wrath were Thine,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Still one with us Thou art;
Nor life, nor death, nor depth, nor height
Thy saints and Thee can part!

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O teach us, Lord, to know and own
That Thou with us art truly one,
And we are one with Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Soon, soon shall come that glorious day,
Thou shalt to wond'ring worlds display
That Thou with us art one.

title: Lord Jesus Christ we seek Thy face
author: Alexander Stewart

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lord Jesus Christ we seek Thy face,
Within the veil we bow the knee;
O let Thy glory fill the place,
And bless us while we wait on Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: We thank Thee for the precious blood
That purged our sins and brought us nigh,
All cleansed and sanctified, to God,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Shut in with Thee, far, far above
The restless world that wars below,
We seek to learn and prove Thy love,
Thy wisdom and Thy grace to know.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: The brow that once with thorns was bound,
Thy hands, Thy side, we fain would see;
And bless us while we wait on Thee.

title: Lord Jesus, come!
author: George Jekell (1856)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Afar from Thee, and that bright place
Where we shall see Thee face to face.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: No joy we know apart from Thee,
No sorrow in Thy presence see.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: And claim us as Thine own;
Our weary feet would wander o'er
This dark and sinful world no more.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: That all Thy flock, so scattered here,
With Thee in glory may appear.

title: Lord Jesus, Friend unfailing!
author: Samuel G. Kuster

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: How dear Thou art to me!
I find my strength in Thee:
Why should my feet grow weary
Rough though the path and dreary,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Nought, nought I count as pleasure,
Earned peace and joy for me.
I love to own, Lord Jesus,
Bought with Thy blood most precious
Whose can I be but Thine?

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: What fills my heart with gladness?
Where can I look in sadness,
Thy love can ne'er grow cold;

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Why should I droop in sorrow?
If I my cross have taken,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Your charms are spread in vain;
There shall I gaze on Jesus,
There shall I dwell with God.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: How dear Thou art to me.

title: Lord, dismiss us with Thy blessing
author: John Fawcett & Godfrey Thring & William Walter Shirley (1773)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lord, dismiss us with Thy blessing
Fill our hearts with joy and peace;
Let us each, Thy love possessing,
O refresh us, O refresh us

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: May the fruits of Thy salvation
In our hearts and lives abound;
To the truth may we be found.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Us from earth to call away,
Upward borne by Thee to heaven,
We shall ever, We shall ever
Reign with Thee in endless day.

title: Lord Jesus, my Saviour!
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: How vast Thy love to me!
I'll bathe in its full ocean
This all my song shall be,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: O depths of grace and mercy!
To those dear wounds I flee;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: The Father will not punish me,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: I'll tune my harp, and with the saints
And as I strike the golden strings
This all my song shall be,

title: Lord Jesus, I love Thee, I know Thou art mine
author: William Ralph Featherstone & Adoniram J Gordon

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lord Jesus, I love Thee, I know Thou art mine,
My rock and my fortress, my Surety divine;
My gracious Redeemer, my song shall be now,
'Tis Thou who art worthy, Lord Jesus, 'tis Thou!

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I love Thee because Thou hast first loved me,
And purchased my pardon on Calvary's tree;
I love Thee for wearing the thorns on Thy brow;
'Tis Thou who art worthy, Lord Jesus, 'tis Thou!

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: I would love Thee in life, I would love Thee in death,
And praise Thee as long as Thou lendest me breath,
And sing, should the death-dew lie cold on my brow,
'Tis Thou who art worthy, Lord Jesus, 'tis Thou!

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: And when the bright morn of Thy glory shall come,
And the children ascend to the Father's glad home,
I'll shout, with Thy likeness impressed on my brow,
'Tis Thou who art worthy, Lord Jesus, 'tis Thou!

title: Lord Jesus, in Thy Name alone
author: Mary Bowly Peters

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lord Jesus, in Thy Name alone
We soon shall meet around the throne;
With this sole claim, on this sole ground,
Thy table here we now surround;
What can we mention to our God
Except Thine own most precious blood?

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: O Jesus, Lord! there is, indeed
Enough in Thee to meet our need,
Enough in Thee to make us glad!
Why should Thy ransomed ones be sad?
This hope have we before our God,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: What joy it is to walk with Thee!
But O what joy Thy face to see!
And when our bliss is all complete,
We still shall worship at Thy feet,
And mention nothing to our God
But that same ever precious blood.

title: Lord Jesus, let Thy favour rest
author: John Withy

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lord Jesus, let Thy favour rest
May it be bound in heaven, and blest

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thy ways, Thou heavenly Bridegroom, be
Their constant springs be found in Thee,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: As fellow-heirs of life in Thee,
Their mutual faith and love still be

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: And when the day of light shall shine,
Thou then with joy wilt own as Thine,

title: Lord Jesus Christ, the thought of Thee
author: Bernard of Clairvaux

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lord Jesus Christ, the thought of Thee
But sweeter far Thy face to see,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Nor voice can sing, nor heart can frame,
A sweeter sound than Thy blest Name,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O hope of every contrite heart,
O joy of all the meek,
To those who fall, how kind Thou art;
How good to those who seek.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: But what to those who find? Ah, this
Nor tongue, nor pen can show;
The love of Jesus! what it is
None but His loved ones know.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Saviour, our only joy be Thou
As Thou our crown wilt be;
Be Thou, O Lord, our glory now.

title: Lord Jesus, Thine;
author: Albert Midlane

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: No more this heart of mine
Shall seek its joy apart from Thee;
The world is crucified to me,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: My joy, my hope, my crown;
Now earthly things may fade and die,
They charm my soul no more for I

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: On love eternal, fixed and sure;
Yes, I am Thine for evermore,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: To Thy dear Name, my precious Lord;

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: And bear me to Thy home,
For ever freed from earthly care,

title: Lord! to Thee my heart ascending
author: Elizabeth Harris Codner

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lord! to Thee my heart ascending
For Thy mercy full and free,
Even me. Grace vouchsafed to sinful me.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thou didst give Thy Son for me,
Even me. Thou didst give Thy Son for me.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Though so long a wand'ring sinner
Even me. Thou hast kindly welcomed me.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: But I'm lost in joyful wond'ring,
And I say, O can it be
That there will be no more sund'ring
Even me. 'Twixt my blessed Lord and me.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Can it be that I, an alien,
Now a child shall ever be?
Can it be that, all forgiven,
Even me. Glory is prepared for me.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: And His blood hath made me free;
From His love no foe can sever,
For He gave Himself for me,
Even me. For He gave Himself for me.

stanzas.label: Verse 7
lines: Lord! I thank Thee for salvation,
Grace so mighty and so free;
Even me. Glorify Thyself in me.

title: Lord Jesus, Thou who only art
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lord Jesus, Thou who only art
The endless source of purest joy,
O come and fill this longing heart;
May nought but Thee my thoughts employ
Teach me on Thee to fix my eye,
For none but Thee can satisfy.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The joys of earth can never fill
The heart that's tasted of Thy love;
No portion would I seek until
I reign with Thee, my Lord above,
When I shall gaze upon Thy face,
And know more fully all Thy grace.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: When from Thy radiant throne on high
Thou didst my fall and ruin see,
Thou cam'st on earth for me to die
That I might share that throne with Thee.
My hopes, my joys are all above.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O what is all that earth can give?
I'm called to share in God's own joy;
Dead to the world, in Thee I live,
In Thee I've bliss without alloy:
Well may I earthly joys resign;
All things are mine, and I am Thine!

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Till Thou shalt come to take me home
Be this my one ambition, Lord,
Self, sin, the world, to overcome,
Fast clinging to Thy faithful Word;
More of Thyself each day to know,
And more into Thine image grow.

title: Lord Jesus, Thy great love to me
author: John Wesley

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lord Jesus, Thy great love to me
No thought can reach, no tongue declare:
O bend my wayward heart to Thee
And reign without a rival there;
Thine, wholly Thine, alone I'd live,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: O Lord, how gracious is Thy way,
All fear before Thy presence flies;
Lord Jesus, nothing may I see,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: In suff'ring be Thy love my peace,
In weakness be Thine arm my strength;
And when the storms of life shall cease
And Thou from heaven wilt come at length,
Lord Jesus, then this heart shall be

title: Lord Jesus, to tell of Thy love
author: Thomas Haweis

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lord Jesus, to tell of Thy love
Our souls shall for ever delight,
And join with the blessed above
In praises by day and by night.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: That love which was stronger than death
Flow out without limit, and free.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: With men Thy delight was to dwell;
By dying to save us from hell.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Enduring the grief and the shame,
And bearing our sins on the Cross,
O who would not boast of Thy love,
And count the world's glory but dross.

title: Lord, we are Thine: our God Thou art
author: James George Deck (1841)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lord, we are Thine: our God Thou art,
Fashioned and made we are by Thee;
These curious frames! in every part
Thy wisdom, power, and love we see;
Each breath we draw, each pulse that beats,
Each organ formed by skill divine,
Great God, that we are only Thine.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Lord, we are Thine: in Thee we live,
Thou dost each hourly mercy give;
Thine earth we tread, we breathe Thine air;
Raiment and food Thou dost supply;
Thy sun's bright rays around us shine:
We own that we are only Thine.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Lord, we are Thine: bought by Thy blood:
Once the poor guilty slaves of sin;
Thou didst redeem us to our God,
And made Thy Spirit dwell within.
Thou hast our sinful wand'rings borne
With love and patience all divine:
As brands, then, from the burning torn
We own that we are only Thine.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Lord, we are Thine: Thy claims we own,
Ourselves to Thee we humbly give;
Reign Thou within our hearts alone,
And make us to Thy glory live.
Here let us each Thy mind display,
In all Thy brilliant virtues shine;
When Thou shalt own that we are Thine.

title: Lord Jesus we believing
author: Samuel Prideaux Tregelles

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: In Thee have peace with God,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thy grace hath given us rest;
Thy stripes have given us healing,
Thy love doth make us blest.
In Thee the Father sees us
Thy blood, from sin which frees us,

title: May the grace of Christ our Saviour
author: John Newton (1779)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: May the grace of Christ our Saviour,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thus may we abide in union
With each other and the Lord,
Joys which earth can ne'er afford.

title: Lord Jesus, who didst once appear
author: John Berridge

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lord Jesus, who didst once appear
We now beseech Thy presence here

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: With grace the bride and bridegroom speed;
May heart with heart be true indeed,
As knit, O Lord, in Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: With gifts of grace their hearts endow
Their substance bless, and peace bestow,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: In purest love their souls unite
May make each other's burdens light

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: And looking to their heavenly home
O may they dwell each day
As heirs of life till Thou shalt come

title: Man of Sorrows! what a name
author: Philip Paul Bliss (1875)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Man of Sorrows! what a name
For the Son of God, who came

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: In my place condemned He stood;
Sealed my pardon with His blood:

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Spotless Lamb of God was He:

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Lifted up was He to die,
It is finished, was His cry;

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: When He comes, our glorious King,
All His ransomed home to bring,
Then anew this song we'll sing:

title: Lord, we would ne'er forget Thy love
author: James George Deck (1841)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lord, we would ne'er forget Thy love,
Who hast redeemed us by Thy blood;
And now, as our High Priest above.
Dost intercede for us with God.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Lord, we would not forget the pain,
The blood-like sweat, the shameful tree,
The wrath Thy soul did once sustain
From sin and death to set us free.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: We would remember we are one
With every saint that loves Thy Name;
United to Thee on the throne,
Our life, our hope, our Lord the same.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Here, in the broken bread and wine,
We hear Thee say, Remember Me!
I gave My life to ransom thine,
I bore the wrath to set thee free.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Lord, we are Thine, we praise Thy love,
One with Thy saints, all one in Thee;
We would, until we meet above,
In all our ways remember Thee.

title: Meeting in the Saviour's Name
author: Thomas Kelly

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: To the world we thus proclaim
On what ground we hope to stand,
When the Lord shall come with clouds,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: From the Cross our hope we draw
What a joyful truth is this!
O how full of hope it is!

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Yes, He rose, He lives to reign;
He will vanquish all His foes
When to earth He comes again;
His the triumph and the crown,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Sing we, then, of Him who died,
Sing of Him who rose again;
And with Him we hope to reign:
Yes, we look to see our Lord,
And to share His bright reward.

title: Mid the splendours of the glory
author: William Watkins Reid (1863)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Mid the splendours of the glory
Which we hope ere long to share,
Christ, our Head, and we, His members,
When we meet Him in the air.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: He has loved us without cause;
And for all His blood-bought myriads,
His is love that knows no pause;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O what gifts shall yet be granted,
Palms and crowns, and robes of white,
When the hope for which we panted
Makes us glorious through His might.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Bright the prospect soon that greets us
When our heavenly Bridegroom meets us
Bride and Bridegroom reign for aye.

title: My days are gliding swiftly by
author: David Nelson (1835)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: My days are gliding swiftly by,
Would not detain them as they fly,
These hours of toil and danger.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: We'll gird our loins, my brethren dear,
Our absent Lord has left us word,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Should coming days be cold and dark,
We need not cease our singing;
That perfect rest nought can molest,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Each cord on earth to sever;
Our Lord says, Come, and there's our home

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: For O we stand on Jordan's strand,
And just before, the shining shore

title: My chains are snapt, the bonds of sin are broken
author: Margaret L. Carson

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: My chains are snapt, the bonds of sin are broken,
O let the triumphs of His grace be spoken,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: O death! O grave! I do not dread your power,
On Jesus, in that dark and dreadful hour,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Yes, Jesus bore it, bore, in love unbounded,
He passed through death and gloriously confounded

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: And now He's risen, proclaim the joyful story,
And we in Him are raised to endless glory,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: We wait to see the Morning Star appearing
This blessed hope illumes, with beams most cheering,

title: My God, I am Thine;
author: Charles Wesley

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: At the sound of His Name.

title: My God! what cords of love are Thine
author: Philip Doddridge

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: My God! what cords of love are Thine,
Thy truth and grace their power combine

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The guilt of twice ten thousand sins
And when the fight of faith begins
Our strength is as our day.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Comfort, through all this vale of tears,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Drawn by such cords we'll onward move
Till round the throne we meet,
And, captives in the chain of love,

title: Midst the darkness, storm and sorrow
author: Paul Gerhardt tr/ad by Emma Frances Shuttleworth Bevan (1898)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Midst the darkness, storm and sorrow,
Well I know the blessed morrow
'Midst the light, and peace, and glory
Christ for me is waiting, watching,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Long the blessed Guide has led me
Now I see the golden towers,
There, amidst the love and glory,
On His hand a name is graven

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: There, amidst the songs of heaven,
Is the footfall through the desert
There, made ready are the mansions
But the Bride the Father gave Him

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Who is this who comes to meet me
He it is who came to win me
In His glory well I know Him

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: O the blessed joy of meeting
O the wondrous words of greeting

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Where no shade nor stain can enter,
Glory of God's grace for ever

stanzas.label: Verse 7
lines: He, who in the hour of sorrow
I, who through the lonely desert
He and I in that bright glory
Mine to be forever with Him,

title: My Shepherd is the Lamb
author: John Beaumont's Psalms

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: With all things good I ever am

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: And leads me where the rivers roll

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: His love so full, so free!
Fruit of His grief and toil.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: When faith and hope shall cease,
I then shall see Him face to face,
And know as I am known.

title: My God, I have found
author: Joseph Denham Smith & John Gambold

title: The Solid Rock
author: Edward Mote (c.18)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: My hope is built on nothing less
I dare not trust the sweetest frame,
But wholly lean on Jesus' Name.
On Christ, the solid Rock, I stand;
All other ground is sinking sand.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: When darkness seems to veil His face
I rest on His unchanging grace;
In every high and stormy gale
My anchor holds within the veil.
On Christ, the solid Rock, I stand;
All other ground is sinking sand.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: His oath, His covenant and blood,
Support me in the whelming flood;
When all around my soul gives way
He then is all my hope and stay.
On Christ, the solid Rock, I stand;
All other ground is sinking sand.

title: My Redeemer! O what beauties
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: None but Jesus, in His glories,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Sunk in ruin, sin, and misery,
Plucked me as a brand from hell.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Mine by covenant, mine for ever,
Mine by oath, and mine by blood,
Mine—nor time the bond shall sever,
Oh how sweet to call Thee mine!

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: When in heaven I see Thy glory,
When before Thy throne I bow,
Perfected I shall be like Thee,
Then shall hear me shout His praise.

title: My rest is in heaven, my rest is not here
author: Henry Francis Lyte

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: My rest is in heaven, my rest is not here,
Then why should I murmur when trials are near?
Be hushed my sad spirit, the worst that can come
But shortens the journey and hastens me home.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: It is not for me to be seeking my bliss,
And building my hopes in a region like this;
I look for a city which hands have not piled;
I pant for a country by sin undefiled.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: The winds of affliction around me may blow,
And dash my lone barque as I'm sailing below;
I smile at the storm as I lean on His breast,
And soon I shall land in the haven of rest.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Let trial and danger my progress oppose,
They only make heaven more sweet at the close;
Come joy or come sorrow, whate'er may befall,
A home with my God will make up for it all.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: With Christ in my heart, and His Word in my hand,
I travel in haste through an enemy's land;
The road may be rough, but it cannot be long,
So I journey on singing the conqueror's song.

title: My Saviour, whom absent, I love
author: William Cowper

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: My Saviour, whom absent, I love,
Whom, not having seen, I adore;

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Dissolve Thou the bonds that detain
My soul from her portion in Thee;
Ah! strike off the adamant chain

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: When arrayed in Thy glories I shine,
Nor grieve any more by my sins
The bosom on which I recline.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O then shall the veil be removed
And round me Thy brightness be poured!
I shall meet Him whom absent I loved,
I shall see whom unseen I adored.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: And then, nevermore shall the fears,
Which darken the valley of tears,

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: They'll be but new signs of Thy love,
New themes for my wonder and praise.

stanzas.label: Verse 7
lines: Thus the stroke which from sin and from pain
Will but strengthen and rivet the chain
Which binds me, my Saviour, to Thee.

title: "No condemnation!" O my soul
author: Robert Cleaver Chapman

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: In heaven His blood for ever speaks
His saints as jewels on His heart

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thy sins were all on Jesus laid,
His stripes have made thee whole.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Teach us, O God, to fix our eyes
So shall we love Thy gracious will

title: My tongue shall spread the Saviour's fame
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: My tongue shall spread the Saviour's fame
For since my soul has known His Name

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: When walking in the paths of sin.
I far from Him would rove,
By sweet constraint He drew me in,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: He spread the banquet, made me eat,
Yea, o'er my guilty, rebel head

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: When, weary of His rich repast
He has recalled His faithless guest

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Through Him the vict'ry I obtain,

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: And when He calls me home ere long

title: My soul amid this stormy world
author: Robert Cleaver Chapman

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: My soul amid this stormy world,
And fain would be as swift of wing
And flee to Him I love.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The cords that bound my heart to earth
Before His Cross I now am left

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: That visage marred, those sorrows deep,
The thorns, the scourge, the gall,
These were the golden chains of love

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Fain would I, Saviour, know Thy love,
Would search the depths of all Thy wounds

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Fain would I strike the golden harp
And at Thy feet, while bending low,
Would sing what grace has done.

title: My God, my Father, while I stray
author: Charlotte Elliott (1834)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: My God, my Father, while I stray
Far from my home in life's rough way,
O teach me from my heart to say,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: If dark my path and hard my lot,
May I be still and murmur not;
But breathe the prayer divinely taught

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: If Thou shouldst call me to resign
What most I prize—it ne'er was mine,
I only yield Thee what is Thine:

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: My Father! help me still to say,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Control my will from day to day,
Blend it with Thine, and take away
All that now makes it hard to say,

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: And when on earth I breathe no more
The prayer oft mixed with tears before,
I'll sing on heaven's blissful shore,

title: My sins were laid on Jesus
author: Horatius Bonar (1845)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: My sins were laid on Jesus
He bore them all and freed me
My guilt was borne by Jesus;
In his own blood most precious,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I tell my wants to Jesus,
I lay my griefs on Jesus,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: I rest my soul on Jesus,
I love the Name of Jesus,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: I long to be like Jesus,
I long to be like Jesus,
I long to be with Jesus
To sing with saints His praises,

title: No bone of Thee was broken
author: Robert Cleaver Chapman

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: No bone of Thee was broken
Of life and peace a token
To us who know Thy Name;
The Head, for all the members,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: What Thou didst sow in tears;
This feast which we are keeping
The face of God from Thee;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thy death of shame and sorrow

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: We watch the dawn of day.
We eat and drink with gladness

title: Now I have found a Friend
author: Henry J. M. Hope (1852)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Now I have found a Friend,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Though I grow poor and old,

title: Now, in a song of grateful praise
author: Samuel Medley (1776)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Now, in a song of grateful praise,
To Christ my Lord my voice I'll raise;
With all His saints I'll join to tell,
My Jesus has done all things well.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: All worlds His glorious power confess
His wisdom all His works express;
But O, His love what tongue can tell?
My Jesus has done all things well.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Has been His love to sinful me!
He plucked me from the jaws of hell;
My Jesus has done all things well.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: I spurned His grace, I broke His laws,
And yet He undertook my cause,
To save me, though I did rebel;
My Jesus has done all things well.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Though many a fiery, flaming dart
The tempter levels at my heart,
With this I all his rage repel;
My Jesus has done all things well.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: And when to that bright world I rise,
And join the anthems in the skies,
Above the rest this note shall swell,
My Jesus has done all things well.

title: Not all the blood of beasts
author: Isaac Watts (1709)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Not all the blood of beasts
Could give the guilty conscience peace,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: By faith we lay our hand
On that dear head of Thine;
With broken, contrite hearts we stand,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: We now look back to see
When hanging on the accursed tree,
And know our guilt was there.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: We bless the Lamb with cheerful voice,

title: No blood, no altar now
author: Horatius Bonar (1845)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: No flame, no smoke ascends on high,
The lamb is slain no more;
But richer blood has flowed from nobler veins
To purge the soul from guilt, and cleanse the reddest stains.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: We thank Thee for the blood,
The blood of Christ, Thy Son,
The blood by which our peace is made,
Great victory o'er hell and sin and woe,
That needs no second fight and leaves no second foe.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: We thank Thee for the grace
Love of the Father's everlasting Son,
Love of the Holy Ghost, Jehovah, Three in One.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: We thank Thee for the hope,
So glad and sure and clear;
It holds the drooping spirit up
Fair hope! with what a sunshine does it cheer
Our roughest path on earth, our dreariest desert here.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: We thank Thee for the crown
'Tis no poor with'ring wreath of earth,
The kingdom of our God and His incarnate Son.

title: O blessed Saviour! is Thy love
author: Joseph Stennett

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O blessed Saviour! is Thy love
So great, so full, so free?
Fain would we give our hearts, our minds,
Our lives, our all, to Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: We love Thee for the glorious worth
We love Thee for the shameful Cross

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: No man of greater love can boast
Than for his friend to die;
Thou for Thine enemies wast slain!
What love with Thine can vie?

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Though in the very form of God,
Thou didst partake of human flesh,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Thou wouldst like sinful man be made
That we as like Thee might become,

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Like Thee in faith, in meekness, love,
More of Thine image daily gain

stanzas.label: Verse 7
lines: O Lord! we treasure in our souls
And ever may Thy Name to us

title: O blessed Lord, what hast Thou done!
author: Mary Bowly Peters

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O blessed Lord, what hast Thou done!

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The Father, in His willing love,
Could spare Thee from His side;
And Thou couldst stoop, to bear above,
At such a cost, Thy Bride.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: While our full hearts in faith repose
Peace in a steady current flows,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: What boundless joy will fill each heart,
When we behold Thee as Thou art,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Unseen we love Thee, dear Thy Name!
The half hath not been told.

title: O blessed Saviour! Who but Thou
author: Sir Edward Denny

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O blessed Saviour! Who but Thou,
May claim from all our willing hearts

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: We love the brethren, Lord, 'tis true,
Sweet traces of Thy blessed self,
For they are one with Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: And one with us, but O, 'twas Thine,
With life and all that love could give,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Thus, heirs of endless bliss with Thee,
And ask Thee still for greater grace,
To love Thee more and more.

title: O Christ! we rest in Thee
author: James George Deck (1841)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Christ! we rest in Thee,
'Tis on Thy meek and lowly breast
Our weary souls alone can rest.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: And in the savour of that blood
The curse is gone—through Thee we're blest;
God rests in Thee—in Thee we rest.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: The rest of God, shall come;
Sorrow and sin shall pass away,
And we shall reach our home;
Then, of the promised land possessed,
Our souls shall know eternal rest.

title: O Christ, what burdens bowed Thy head!
author: Anne Ross Cundell Cousin

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Christ, what burdens bowed Thy head!
Our load was laid on Thee;
Thou stoodest in the sinner's stead,
Bear'st all my ill for me.
A victim led, Thy blood was shed;
Now there's no load for me.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Death and the curse were in our cup,
But Thou has drained the last dark drop,
That bitter cup, love drank it up;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: The tempest's awful voice was heard;
O Christ, it broke on Thee!
Thy open bosom was my ward;
It braved the storm for me.
Thy form was scarred, Thy visage marred;

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O Christ, it woke' gainst Thee!
Thy blood the flaming blade must slake,
Thy heart its sheath must be;
All for my sake my peace to make,
Now sleeps that sword for me.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: The Holy One did hide His face;
Dumb darkness wrapt Thy soul a space,
But now that face of radiant grace
Shines forth in light on me.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: For me, Lord Jesus, Thou hast died,
And I have died in Thee;
Thou'rt risen; my bands are all untied,
And now Thou liv'st in me.
When Thou dost come to take Thy Bride,

title: O Christian, awake! for the strife is at hand
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Christian, awake! for the strife is at hand,
With helmet and shield and a sword in thy hand,
To meet the bold tempter, go, fearlessly go!
And stand, like the brave, with thy face to the foe.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Whatever thy danger, take heed and beware,
But turn not thy back, for no armour is there;
The legions of darkness if thou wouldst o'erthrow,
Then stand, like the brave, with thy face to the foe.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: The cause of thy Master with vigour defend;
Be watchful, be zealous, and fight to the end;
Wherever He leads thee, go, valiantly go,
And stand, like the brave, with thy face to the foe.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Press on, never doubting, thy Captain is near,
With grace to supply, and with comfort to cheer;
His love like a stream in the desert will flow;
Then stand, like the brave, with thy face to the foe

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Stand like the brave, stand like the brave,
Stand like the brave, with thy face to the foe.

title: O Christ! in Thee my soul hath found
author: Unknown tr/ad by Emma Frances Bevan

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Christ! in Thee my soul hath found,
The peace, the joy I sought so long,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I sighed for rest and happiness,
I yearned for them, not Thee;
But while I passed my Saviour by
His love laid hold on me.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: I tried the broken cisterns, Lord,
E'en as I stooped to drink they fled,
And mocked me as I wailed.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: The pleasures lost I sadly mourned,
Till grace the sightless eyes received

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Now none but Christ can satisfy,
There's love, and life, and lasting joy,

title: O Christ, Thou heavenly Lamb!
author: Charles Russell Hurditch

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Now let Thy love my soul inflame,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Power to glory in the Cross

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: And all its depths to know;
Power to fix the heart above,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Power to lift the warning cry
To souls from wrath to flee.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Power to hail the happy day

stanzas.label: Verse 7
lines: To swell redemption's song to Thee,

title: O Come, Thou stricken Lamb of God!
author: Wolfgang Christopher Deszler tr/ad by John Wesley (note: some sources attribute authorship to Nikolaus Ludwig von Zinzendorf, another to Hursley)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Come, Thou stricken Lamb of God!
Who shed'st for us Thine own life-blood,
And teach us all Thy love: then pain
Were sweet, and life or death were gain.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Take Thou our hearts, and let them be
For ever closed to all but Thee;
Thy willing servants, let us wear
The seal of love for ever there.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: How blest are they who still abide
Close sheltered by Thy watchful side;
Who life and strength from Thee receive,
And with Thee move, and in Thee live.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Ah, Lord! enlarge our scanty thought
To know the wonders Thou hast wrought;
Unloose our stamm'ring tongues to tell

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: To whom both heaven and earth must bow!
Heirs of Thy shame and of Thy throne
We bear the cross, and seek the crown.

title: O blessed God! How kind
author: John Kent

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Are all Thy ways to me,
Yet now, subdued by sovereign grace,
My spirit longs for Thine embrace.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: How great their sum, how high they rise,
Can ne'er be known beneath the skies.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: My feet made haste to hell!
And there should I have gone,
But Thou dost all things well:
Thy love was great, Thy mercy free,
Which from the pit delivered me.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: The sun to rule the day,
What thoughts of peace and mercy flowed
In Thy great heart of love, O God.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: The streams of love I trace
And in His sovereign counsels see
Eternal thoughts of love to me.

title: O eyes that are weary, and hearts that are sore
author: John Nelson Darby & Anna Bartlett Warner

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O eyes that are weary, and hearts that are sore,
Look off unto Jesus and sorrow no more;
The light of His countenance shineth so bright,
That on earth, as in heaven, there need be no night.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Looking off unto Jesus, my eyes cannot see
The troubles and dangers that throng around me;
They cannot be blinded with sorrowful tears,
They cannot be shadowed with unbelief fears.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Looking off unto Jesus my spirit is blest;
In the world I have turmoil, in Him I have rest;
The sea of my life all about me may roar;
When I look unto Jesus I hear it no more.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Looking off unto Jesus I go not astray;
My eyes are on Him and He shows me the way;
The path may seem dark as He leads me along,
But following Jesus, I cannot go wrong.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Looking off unto Jesus my heart cannot fear,
Its trembling is still when I see Jesus near;
I know that His power my safeguard will be,
For, "Why are you troubled?" He saith unto me.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Soon, soon shall I know the full beauty and grace
Of Jesus, my Lord, when I stand face to face;
I shall know how His love went before me each day,
And wonder that ever my eyes turned away.

title: O Gracious Lord, be with us now
author: Sir Edward Denny

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Gracious Lord, be with us now,
On Christ, the Bread of Life, may we

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: With water from the smitten Rock
And make us all rejoice to feel

title: Of Thee, Lord, we would never tire;
author: Mary Bowly Peters

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Of Thee, Lord, we would never tire;
For life is in Thy blood.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: If through the night a happy song
What greater joys shall cause ere long

stanzas.label: Verse 3
