lines: To look within and see no stain,
To shed no tears, to feel no pain,
To see Thee face to face.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: To find each hope of glory gained,
And fully all to have attained

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: For this we're pressing onward still!
And in this hope would be
More subject to the Father's will,

title: O God of matchless grace
author: Hannah Kilham Burlingham

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: We stand accepted in the place
That none but Christ could claim.
Our willing hearts have heard Thy voice,
And in Thy mercy we rejoice.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: That Thou shouldst place us in Thy sight,
Thy perfect love has cast out fear;
Thy favour shines upon us here.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O Christ of God, in Thee!
Now of Thy peace, Thy joy possessed,
We wait Thy face to see.
Now to the Father's heart received,
We know in whom we have believed.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: In life or death are we;
Then keep us ever, blessed Lord,
Bought with a price, we're not our own;
We died, we live to God alone.

title: O joy of the justified, joy of the free!
author: Francis (Frank) Bottome

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O joy of the justified, joy of the free!
I'm washed in that crimson tide opened for me;
In Christ, my Redeemer, rejoicing I stand,
And point to the print of the nail in His hand.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Lord Jesus, the crucified, now Thou art mine;
Though once a lost sinner, yet now I am Thine;
In conscious salvation I sing of His grace
Who lifts now upon me the smile of His face.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Lord Jesus, my Saviour, I'll still sing of Thee,
Yes, sing of Thy precious blood poured out for me;
And when in the mansions of glory above,
I'll praise and adore Thine unchangeable love.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: O sing of His mighty love,

title: O head, once filled with bruises
author: Paul Gerhardt

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O head, once filled with bruises,
Mocked with a crown of thorn!
O Head, to death once wounded

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Which Thou didst pay in blood.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: When Thou for us didst bleed;
We see Thee face to face.

title: O happy day, that fixed my choice
author: Philip Doddridge (c. 1755)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O happy day, that fixed my choice
On Thee, my Saviour and my God!
Well may this glowing heart rejoice
And tell its raptures all abroad.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I am my Lord's and He is mine;
He drew me, and I followed on,
Charmed to confess the voice divine.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Fixed on this blissful centre, rest;
Nor ever from Thy Lord depart,
With Him of every good possessed.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: When Jesus washed my sins away.
He taught me how to watch and pray,

title: O happy day! when first we felt
author: James George Deck (1841)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O happy day! when first we felt
Our souls with deep contrition melt,
And saw our sins of crimson guilt
All cleansed by blood on Calvary spilt.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: O happy day! when first Thy love
Began our grateful hearts to move;
And gazing on Thy wondrous Cross,
We saw all else as worthless dross.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O happy day! when we no more
Shall grieve Thee whom our souls adore,
When sorrows, conflicts, fears shall cease,
And all our trials end in peace.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O happy day! when we shall see
And fix our longing eyes on Thee,
On Thee, our Light, our Life, our Love,
Our All below, our Heaven above.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: O happy day of cloudless light!
Lord, when shall we its dawning see,
And spend it all in praising Thee?

title: O Christ! He is the fountain
author: Anne Ross Cundell Cousin

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Christ! He is the fountain,
The deep, sweet well of love;
The streams on earth I've tasted,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: My web of time He wove,
And aye the dews of sorrow
I'll bless the hand that guided,
I'll bless the heart that planned,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: He brings a poor vile sinner

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: The Bride eyes not her garment,
I will not gaze at glory,
But on the King of grace.
Not at the crown He giveth,
The Lamb is all the glory

title: O for a thousand tongues to sing
author: Charles Wesley (1739)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O for a thousand tongues to sing
The glories of my God and King,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Jesus! the Name that charms our fears,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: He breaks the power of cancelled sin,
His blood can make the foulest clean,

title: O for the peace that floweth as a river!
author: Jane Fox Crewdson (1864)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O for the peace that floweth as a river!
Making life's desert places bloom and smile;
O for the faith to grasp heaven's bright "for ever"!
Amid the shadows of earth's "little while."

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: "A little while" for patient vigil keeping,
To face the storm and wrestle with the strong;
"A little while" to sow the seed with weeping,
Then bind the sheaves and sing the harvest song.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: "A little while" the earthen pitcher taking
To wayside brooks, from far-off fountains fed;
Then the parched lip its thirst for ever slaking
Beside the fullness of the Fountain-head.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: "A little while" to keep the oil from failing,
"A little while" faith's flick'ring lamp to trim;
And then the Bridegroom's coming footsteps hailing,
We'll haste to meet Him with the bridal hymn.

title: O for robes of whiteness
author: Charatie de Cheney Lees Smith Bancroft

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O for the no more weeping

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: O for the bliss of flying,
O for the rest of lying
O for the hour of seeing

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O Christ! Thou King of Glory,
I soon shall dwell with Thee!
I soon shall sing the story
Of Thy great love to me!
That all my love might centre

title: O Holy Saviour! Friend unseen!
author: Charlotte Elliott (1834)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Since on Thine arm Thou bidst us lean,
Help us throughout life's changing scene
By faith to cling to Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Far from our home, fatigued, opprest,
In Thee we've found our place of rest;
As strangers still, yet not unblest,
While we can cling to Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Our former dreams of earthly bliss,
Each hour to cling to Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Though faith and hope may oft be tried,
We ask not, need not aught beside;
So safe, so calm, so satisfied,
The souls that cling to Thee.

title: O teach us more of Thy blest ways
author: James Hutton

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O teach us more of Thy blest ways,
And fix and root us in Thy grace,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: O tell us often of Thy love,
Of all Thy grief and pain!
And let our hearts with joy confess
That thence comes all our gain.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: For this, O may we freely count
The dearest object of our love

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Engrave this deeply on our heart,
That so we may, in some degree,

title: O Lamb of God! 'tis joy to know
author: James George Deck (1841)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Lamb of God! 'tis joy to know
That path is o'er of shame and woe,
All finished is Thy work of toil;
Thou reapest now the fruit and spoil,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thy holy head, once bound with thorns,
The crown of glory now adorns;
Ten thousand thousands sing Thy praise,
Their harps the eternal anthem raise,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: And, Lord, for us Thou sittest there;
Thy members here Thy fullness share,
Thy boundless love has made all ours,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: We triumph in Thy triumphs, Lord;
Thy joys our deepest joys afford,
How does the thought our spirits cheer,

title: O Lamb of God! still keep me
author: James George Deck (1841)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Lamb of God! still keep me
What foes and snares surround me!
The grace that sought and found me

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: In all its cares and woe.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Soon shall my eyes behold Thee
The half hath not been told me
Of all Thy power and grace.

title: O Lord, who art Thy people's light
author: Sir Edward Denny

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Lord, who art Thy people's light,
When shall Thy face be seen?
When wilt Thou meet our longing sight,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: We know, Lord Jesus, that Thy heart
Still for Thy saints doth care;
But we would see Thee as Thou art,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thy love sustains us on our way
And grace to help us day by day

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: But O the more we learn of Thee,
The more we long Thyself to see,

title: O Lord! 'tis joy to look above
author: James George Deck (1841)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Lord! 'tis joy to look above
And see Thee on the throne;
To search the heights and depths of love
Which Thou to us hast shown

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: To look beyond the dark, long night
When Thou, to all the saints in light,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: And O 'tis joy the path to trace
Learning of Thee to walk in grace

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Joy to confess Thy blessed Name,
And to the wearied heart proclaim,

title: O Lord, I would delight in Thee
author: John Ryland (1777)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Lord, I would delight in Thee,
To Thee in every trouble flee,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: When all created streams are dried
May I with this be satisfied,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O that I had a stronger faith
To credit what my Saviour saith,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Thou who hast made my heaven secure
While Christ is rich, can I be poor,
Christ, who for me has died?

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: O Lord, I cast my care on Thee;
Henceforth my great concern shall be
To love and praise Thee more.

title: O Lord, how much Thy Name unfolds
author: Mary Bowly Peters

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Lord, how much Thy Name unfolds

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Jesus! It speaks a life of love,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: It tells us of Thy sinless walk
And to our ears no tale so sweet

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: That God, as man, could show;
There only can the Spirit trace

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: The mention of Thy Name shall bow
The chiefest of ten thousand Thou!

title: O Lord, when we the path retrace
author: James George Deck (1841)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Lord, when we the path retrace
Which Thou on earth hast trod,
To man Thy wondrous love and grace,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thy love to man, so sorely tried,
The very spear that pierced Thy side
Drew forth the blood to save.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thou didst Thy Father's Name confess,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Thy path, uncheered by earthly smiles,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: O Lord, with sorrow and with shame,
How little we, who bear Thy Name,

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Give us Thy meek, Thy lowly mind;
And all our rest and pleasure find

title: O love divine, how sweet Thou art!
author: Charles Wesley (1749)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O love divine, how sweet Thou art!
When shall I find my longing heart
O may I pant and thirst to prove
The love of Christ to me.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: God only knows the love of God:
O that it more were shed abroad
For love I sigh, for love I pine;
This only portion, Lord, be mine,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O that I may for ever sit,
Like Mary, at the Master's feet!
My only care, my only bliss,
My joy, my heaven on earth be this,To hear the Bridegroom's voice.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O that I may like favoured John
From care, and sin, and sorrow free,
Give me, O Lord, to find in Thee

title: O Lord, where'er Thy people meet
author: William Cowper

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Lord, where'er Thy people meet
Where'er they see Thee, Thou art found,
And every place is hallowed ground.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Great Shepherd of Thy chosen few
Here to our waiting hearts proclaim
The sweetness of Thy saving Name.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Now may we prove the power of prayer
To strengthen faith and banish care;
To teach our faint desires to rise,
And bring all heaven before our eyes.

title: O Lord, who now art seated
author: James George Deck (1841)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Lord, who now art seated
For which Thou cam'st to die.
To Thee our hearts are lifted

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: We know that Thou has bought us
And cleansed us by Thy blood;
We know Thy grace has brought us
As kings and priests to God.
We know that soon the morning,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: So full, so vast, so free!
For us Thou cam'st from heaven,
For us to bleed and die;

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O let this love constrain us
To give our hearts to Thee;

title: O Lord, Thy love's unbounded!
author: John Nelson Darby

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: So sweet, so full, so free!

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: To joy in all its brightness
Yet sure, if in Thy presence

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: If clouds have dimmed my sight,
Towards me, as e'er, Thou'rt bright.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O guard my soul, Lord Jesus,
And if I wander, teach me
Soon back to Thee to flee,
May to my soul be known;
And versed in this Thy goodness,

title: O God, our help in ages past
author: Isaac Watts (1719)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O God, our help in ages past,
Our hope for years to come,
Our shelter from the stormy blast,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Before the hills in order stood,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Under the shadow of Thy throne

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O God, our help in ages past,
Our hope for years to come,
Be Thou our guard while life shall last,

title: O what a lonely path were ours
author: Sir Edward Denny

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O what a lonely path were ours
No home or rest beyond it all,
No guide or help in Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: But Thou art near and with us still
To keep us on the way,
That leads along the vale of tears
To yon bright world of day.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: There shall Thy glory, O our God!
And we, Thy saints, rejoice to prove
That all Thy Word was true.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: There Jesus, on His heavenly throne,
While we the blest associates there
Of all His joy shall be.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Sweet hope! we leave without a sigh
To bear the cross, despise the shame,
For all that weight of bliss.

title: O what a Saviour that He died for me!
author: James McGranahan (1878)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O what a Saviour that He died for me!
From condemnation He hath made me free;
He that believeth on the Son saith He,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: All my iniquities on Him were laid,
All my indebtedness by Him was paid;
All who believe on Him, the Lord hath said,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Though poor and needy I can trust my Lord;
Though weak and sinful I believe His Word;
O glad message! every child of God

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Though all unworthy, yet I will not doubt;
For him that cometh He will not cast out;
He that believeth, O the good news shout!

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Verily, verily, I say unto you;
He that believeth on the Son, 'tis true.

title: O Our Saviour, crucified!
author: Robert Cleaver Chapman

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Near Thy Cross would we abide,
There to look with steadfast eye

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Jesus bruised and put to shame
God is love, we surely know
By the Saviour's depths of woe.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O how vile our low estate
Since our ransom was so great.

title: Once more before we part
author: Joseph Hart & Robert Stephen Hawker

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Lord, in Thy grace we came;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: We'd live, and feed, and grow;
Go on to know the Lord,

title: On Christ salvation rests secure;
author: Samuel Medley

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: The Rock of Ages must endure;
Nor can that faith be overthrown

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: To Him we look, on Him we lean;
And build on Christ, the "Living Stone."

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: In Him it is ordained to raise
Composed of all His saints, who own

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: View the vast building, see it rise;
The work, how great! the plan, how wise!
That rests it on the "Living Stone."

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: But most adore His precious Name;
His glory and His grace proclaim;
For us, the lost, condemned, undone,

title: One there is above all others;
author: Marianne Nunn

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: One there is above all others;
His is love beyond a brother's;
Earthly friends may fail or leave us,
One day soothe, the next day grieve us,
But this Friend will ne'er deceive us;

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Think, O think how much we owe Him;
With His precious blood He bought us,
In the wilderness He sought us,
To His fold He safely brought us;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: We have found a friend in Jesus;
'Tis His great delight to bless us;
How our hearts delight to hear Him
Bid us dwell in safety near Him!
Why should we distrust or fear Him?

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Through His Name we are forgiven;
Backward shall our foes be driven;
Best of blessings He'll provide us;
Nought but good shall e'er betide us;
Safe to glory He will guide us;

title: On Thy broken body feeding
author: Mary Carter

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lord, our hearts in one unite;
Here our souls behold Thee bleeding,
Put to grief in sinners' sight.
O that Jesus thus should love us,
Love us unto death and shame!
Let the dear remembrance move us
While we meet in His blest Name.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Here the pledge of Thy returning
Tells of all the joys of home,
And our hearts within us burning,
Soon, full soon, we thus together
In the Father's house shall meet;

title: O Patient, spotless One!
author: Christian Andreas Bernstein

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: To bear Thy yoke and learn of Thee,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The mind and heart to fill;
Thy life, to calm the anxious soul,

title: O precious blood, O glorious death
author: Augustus Montague Toplady

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O precious blood, O glorious death,
When stung by sin this blood we view,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The blood that purchased our release,
We challenge earth and hell to show

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Our scarlet crimes are made as wool,
And we brought nigh to God;

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: The blood that makes His glorious Church
And O the riches of His love!
He poured it out for me.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Shall be our endless themes of praise

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: In patience let us then possess
Our Head already is in heaven,
And we shall soon be there

title: O Spotless Lamb of God, in Thee
author: Mary Jane Deck Walker

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Spotless Lamb of God, in Thee
And with delight Thy children trace,
In Thee, His wondrous love and grace.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: For Thou didst leave Thy throne above
To teach us that our God is Love;
And now we see His glory shine
In every word and deed of Thine.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: When we behold Thee, Lamb of God,
How great our guilt with grief we see.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: There we with joy Thy grace behold;
Its height and depth can ne'er be told!
It bursts our chains and sets us free,
And sweetly draws our souls to Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: The cross reveals Thy love below;
But better soon our hearts shall know,
When we behold Thy face above,
The fullness of our Father's love.

title: O Thou spotless Lamb of God
author: James George Deck (1841)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Thou spotless Lamb of God
Thou hast bought us with Thy blood;

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: We are Thine, and Thine alone;
And in all our works and ways
Now would only seek Thy praise.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Help us to confess Thy Name,
Bear with joy the cross and shame;

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: When Thou shalt in glory come,
And we reach our heavenly home,
Louder still our lips shall own
We are Thine, and Thine alone!

title: Our Father! O what gracious ways
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Our Father! O what gracious ways
And thoughts of love that Name conveys!
It tells us of the tender care

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Our Father! by Thy mercies past,
We learn on Thee our cares to cast;
And while our wants are known to Thee,
We need not fear whate'er they be.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: How oft when wand'ring far away
Thy care has hedged up all our way;
So bidding us return and live,
And learn how much Thou canst forgive.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: How precious are Thy thoughts to us!
How dear Thy Name revealed thus!
O make us followers of Thee,
As Thy dear children ought to be.

title: Our Father! we would worship
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The fire Thy love hath kindled
Though dimmed by sin and doubt:
O make it burn more brightly
The grace that made Thee ours.

title: Our souls are in God's mighty hand
author: Charles Wesley

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Our souls are in God's mighty hand,
And you and I shall surely stand

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Him eye to eye we then shall see,
Our face like His shall shine;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O what a joyful meeting there!
We all shall join in praising Him

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: When we've been there ten thousand years,
We'll have no less to sing His praise

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: We'll stem the storm, it won't be long,
In the haven of eternal rest,

title: Our times are in Thy hand;
author: William Freeman Lloyd

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Our times are in Thy hand;
Our life, our souls, our all we leave

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Our times are in Thy hand,
Pleasing or painful, dark or bright,
As best may seem to Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Our times are in Thy hand;
Why should we doubt or fear?
Our Father's hand will never cause

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Our times are in Thy hand,
The hand our many sins have pierced
Is now our guard and guide.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Our times are in Thy hand,
Nor is that hand outstretched in vain

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Our times are in Thy hand;
Till we have left this weary land

title: Our Lord is now rejected
author: Daniel Webster Whittle (1881)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: But soon He'll come in glory!
For the crowning day is coming

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The heavens shall glow with splendour;
The saints shall shine in glory
In the crowning day that's coming

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Our pain shall then be over,
We'll sin and sigh no more;
As we to Him are nigh,
In the crowning day that's coming

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: By gathering in the lost ones
For whom our Lord did die,
For the crowning day that's coming

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: O the crowning day is coming!
When our Lord shall come in power
O the glorious sight will gladden
In the crowning day that's coming

title: Ours are peace and joy divine
author: William Watkins Reid

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Ours are peace and joy divine,
When, like branches in the vine,
We may bear all holy fruit
Love of Christ, love of Christ,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Other's woes pierce like a dart
Sinners warn to flee from hell,
Love of Christ, love of Christ,
Heaven's ranks we'll seek to swell

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: We will love with tender care,
And our love to all shall flow
Love of Christ, love of Christ,
We now love all Christ-like ones

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Now we live and walk by faith
Depths and heights of love explore,
Till we gain the heavenly shore
Love of Christ, love of Christ,
When He comes we then shall know

title: O what shall we feel in Thy presence when first
author: Emily Grimley

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O what shall we feel in Thy presence when first
The visions of glory upon us shall burst!
Since now our soul longeth and seeketh for Thee;
O when, blessed Saviour, Thy face shall we see?

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: That face, once so marred, we shall gaze on at length,
And fearless behold, as the sun in his strength;
Those eyes, flames of fire, that so searching we prove,
Shall beam on us then inexpressible love.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thy voice, like great waters, how calmly our soul
Shall hear in the glory its deep waters roll;
Though now it rebukes us and humbles our pride,
It shall speak only love to Thy glorified Bride.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O Thou who this world as a lone pilgrim trod,
Thy Father our Father, Thy God is our God;
To Thee we behold the bright seraphim bow;
Lord Jesus, what glory doth rest on Thee now!

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Thy Spirit has shown God's deep purpose to be
To empty, then fill us with glory like Thee;
And now Thou dost wait—Thy full joy to impart,
For that day of espousals—the joy of Thy heart.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Now moment by moment, to answer our needs,
Thy blood, holy Saviour, in righteousness pleads;
And sheltered by that, how serene and how calm
Our souls on Thy bosom are shielded from harm.

stanzas.label: Verse 7
lines: We see Thee, Lord Jesus, with glory now crowned,
And waiting Thy coming, in peace would be found;
The visions of glory have turned all to dross;
For Thee give us grace to count all things but loss.

title: Praise Him! praise Him! Jesus, our blessed Redeemer!
author: Frances (Fanny) Jane Crosby

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Praise Him! praise Him! Jesus, our blessed Redeemer!
Sing, ye saints! His wonderful love proclaim;
Hail Him! hail Him! mightiest angels in glory,
Strength and honour give to His holy Name.
Like a shepherd Jesus will feed His people,
In His arms He carries them all day long;
O ye saints that dwell in the light of His presence
Praise Him! praise Him! ever in joyful song.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Praise Him! praise Him! Jesus, our blessed Redeemer!
For our sins He suffered, and bled, and died;
He's our Rock, our hope of eternal salvation,
Hail Him! hail Him! Jesus, the crucified.
Crowned with thorns that cruelly pierced His brow;
Once for us rejected, despised, and forsaken,
Prince of Glory! He is triumphant now.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Praise Him! praise Him! Jesus, our blessed Redeemer!
Heavenly portals loud with hosannahs ring!
Jesus, Saviour, reigneth for ever and ever;
Crown Him! crown Him! prophet, and priest, and king.
Death is vanquished! tell it with joy, ye faithful,
Where is now thy victory, boasting grave?
Jesus lives! no longer thy portals are cheerless;
Jesus lives! the mighty and strong to save.

title: Peace! What a precious sound!
author: John F. Elwin

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Our souls are brought to God

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Love was the spring of all,
Yea, sound from shore to shore

title: Praise, praise ye the Name of Jehovah, our God;
author: Horatius Bonar (1845)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Praise, praise ye the Name of Jehovah, our God;
Declare, O declare ye His glories abroad;
Proclaim ye His mercy from nation to nation
Till the uttermost islands have heard His salvation.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Praise, praise ye the Lamb who for sinners was slain,
Who went down to the grave and ascended again;
And who soon shall return, when these dark days are o'er,
To set up His kingdom in glory and power.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Then the heavens, the earth, and the sea shall rejoice;
The fields and the forests shall lift the glad voice;
The sands of the desert shall flourish in green,
And Lebanon's glory be shed o'er the scene.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Her bridal attire and her festal array
All Nature shall wear on that glorious day;
For her King cometh down with His people to reign,
And His presence shall bless her with Eden again.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: For His love floweth on free and full as a river,
And His mercy endureth for ever and ever.

title: Praise the Lord, and leave to-morrow
author: William Sloan

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Praise the Lord, and leave to-morrow
Leave thy troubles in His hands.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Each day has enough of care;
God will give thee strength to bear.
Cast on Him thine every care.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Bring with it whate'er it may;
Trust Him, therefore, come what may.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: May appear to take thee home.
Look for Him, the coming One.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: All around there's sin and sorrow;
He shall bless thy work indeed.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Each day, as our time rolls on,
We shall find the promised blessing,
He will come to take us home.

title: Praise thy Saviour, O my soul!
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Praise thy Saviour, O my soul!
He has drunk the bitter gall,
Paid thy ransom, set thee free;

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: O the wonders of His love!
To atone and die for thee;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: See the waves and billows roll
O my soul, it was for thee!

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Yes, with joy we'll praise Him now
Till with saints above we bow,

title: Precious is the blood of Jesus
author: Gordon Furlong

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Precious is the blood of Jesus
From the wrath of God it frees us,
Sounds with joy through earth and heaven.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Jesus now in heaven is seated,
And by faith on Him we rest;
Soon the Church will be completed,
And the saints with Him be blest:

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Soon will pass the night of sorrow,
And the Lord in glory come;
We shall see Him on the morrow,
And the Bride be welcomed home: Hallelujah!

title: Praise the Lord, who died to save us
author: Thomas Kelly (1806)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Praise the Lord, who died to save us,
Praise Him that He lives to bless us,
We would all Thy love proclaim.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Grace it was, yea, grace abounding,
Brought Thee down to save the lost;
Praise Him, praise Him all His host:
Ye are they who owe Him most.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: We, of all His hand created,
Destined now to share His throne,
Sing of what our Lord hath done.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Praise His Name, who died to save us;
And in Him the Father gave us
All that boundless love could give:

title: Praise the Saviour, ye who know Him!
author: Thomas Kelly (1806)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Praise the Saviour, ye who know Him!
Who can tell how much we owe Him?
Gladly let us render to Him

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Jesus is the Name that charms us,
He for conflict fits and arms us;
Nothing moves, and nothing harms us

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Trust in Him, ye saints, for ever;
Neither force nor guile can sever

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Keep us, Lord, O keep us cleaving
Till the hour of our receiving

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Then we shall be where we would be,
Then we shall be what we should be,
That which is not now, nor could be,

title: Prayer is the soul's sincere desire
author: James Montgomery (1818)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Prayer is the soul's sincere desire,
The motion of a hidden fire

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Prayer is the burden of a sigh,
The upward glancing of an eye
When none but God is near.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Prayer is the simplest form of speech
Prayer, the sublimest strains that reach

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Prayer is the Christian's vital breath,
His watchword at the gates of death:

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: The saints, in prayer, appear as one
In word and deed and mind,
While with the Father and the Son

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: O Thou by whom we come to God,
The Life, the Truth, the Way!
The path of prayer Thyself hast trod:
Lord, teach us how to pray!

title: Press forward and fear not!
author: Edward Wakefield

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: In the power of His promise,
Through the sea and the desert
But He who hath saved us

title: "Praise ye the Lord!" again, again
author: Mary Bowly Peters

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Nor toucheth He our hearts in vain;
We praise, we praise the Lord.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: And faith takes up the happy strain
Our joy is in the Lord.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: "Stand fast in Christ!" ah! yet again
Our best endeavours are in vain,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: "Clean every whit!" Thou saidst it, Lord;
Thine, surely, is a faithful word,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: For ever be the glory given
To Thee, O Lamb of God!
No joy for us, in earth or heaven,
We owe not to Thy blood.

title: Rejoice! rejoice! ye saints, rejoice!
author: Charles Russell Hurditch

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Rejoice with all your heart and voice,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Rejoice! rejoice! lift up your head
That for your souls the Saviour shed

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Rejoice! rejoice! in His sweet Name
Our Jesus still abides the same,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: For dead ones raised, and lost ones found,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: For mercies countless as the sand
Have to your souls been given.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Rejoice! rejoice! the Lord shall come
And gather all His ransomed home,

title: Rise, my soul! behold 'tis Jesus
author: Joseph Denham Smith

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: See Him now in glory seated,
Where thy sins no more can rise.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Lo! He doth in heaven appear,
Shows the blood of His atonement
As thy title to be there.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: All thy sins were laid upon Him,
Jesus bore them on the tree;
God who knew them, laid them on Him,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: God now brings thee to His dwelling,
Spreads for thee His feast divine,
What a portion there is thine.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: In that circle of God's favour,
All is rest, and rest for ever,

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Nought divide them from the Lord.

title: Rise, my soul! thy God directs thee;
author: John Nelson Darby

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Rise, my soul! thy God directs thee;
Pass thou on; His hand protects thee,
Strength that has the captive freed.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Heavenly springs shall there restore thee

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: God Himself shall mark thy way;

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: In the desert God will teach thee
What the God that thou hast found;
All His grace shall there abound.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Though thy way be long and dreary,
Tell how God hath brought thee through.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: There no stranger God shall meet thee;
He who to His rest shall greet thee
Greets thee with a well-known love.

title: Rejoice, ye saints, the time draws near
author: Anonymous (c.19)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Rejoice, ye saints, the time draws near
When Christ will in the clouds appear

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The trumpet sounds! through earth and sky

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: The Lord will come to claim His own,
And on each faithful one a crown

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: We'll cast our crowns down at His feet,
And crown Him King of kings,

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Trim your lamps and be ready,
Trim you lamps and be ready,
Trim your lamps and be ready
Trim your lamps and be ready,

title: Rise up and hasten!
author: Joseph Denham Smith

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The morn of heaven is dawning;
We're near the break of day.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: And soon will be no more;
Now never more can charm us
With such a goal in view.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: By His blood He bought them,
With rapture now they praise Him,
The Lamb that once was slain.

title: "Revive Thy work, O Lord!"
author: Albert Midlane (1858)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Speak with the voice which wakes the dead,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: And hung'ring for the Bread of Life

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Grant that Thy blessed Gospel may

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: The glory shall be all Thine own,

title: Safe in the arms of Jesus
author: Frances (Fanny) Jane Crosby (1868)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Safe in the arms of Jesus,
Borne in a song to me,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Safe in the arms of Jesus,
Free from the blight of sorrow,
Free from my doubts and fears;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Firm on the Rock of Ages
Here let me wait with patience,
Wait till the night is o'er,
Wait till I see the morning

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Safe in the arms of Jesus,

title: Saviour, more than life to me
author: Frances (Fanny) Jane Crosby (1868)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Saviour, more than life to me
I am clinging, clinging close to Thee;
Keep me ever, ever near Thy side.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Lead me gently, gently as I go;
I can never, never lose my way.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Let me love Thee more and more,
Till this fleeting, fleeting life is o'er;
Till my soul is lost in love
In a brighter, brighter world above.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Let me feel Thy cleansing power;
May Thy tender love to me
Bind me closer, closer, Lord, to Thee.

title: Saviour, Thy Name I love!
author: James George Deck (1841)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Thou art all to me!

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Hast bought me with Thy blood,
O how great is Thy love,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: What need I now to fear?

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Then, Thine own face I'll see;
Then I shall like Thee be;

title: Salvation to our God!
author: Mary Bowly Peters

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: The shedding of His precious blood
And through the Lamb it flows;
Once slain for us—for us He lives,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The Lamb once slain is seen
And His redeemed are white and clean

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Our hearts are tuned for this,
The Lamb, the spring of all our bliss,
And to the Lamb who shed His blood.

title: Sound the high praises of Jesus, the King!
author: John Charles Ryle

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Sound the high praises of Jesus, the King!
He came and He conquered—His victory sing;
Sing, for the power of the tyrant is broken;
The triumph complete over death and the grave.
Vain is their boasting; Jehovah hath spoken,
And Jesus proclaimed Himself mighty to save.
Sound the high praises of Jesus, the King!
He came and He conquered—His victory sing.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Praise to the Conqueror! Praise to the Lord!
The enemy quailed at the might of His word;
To heaven He ascends and unfolds the glad story,
The host of the blessed exult in His fame.
In love He looks down from the throne of His glory,
And rescues the ruined who trust in His Name.
Sound the high praises of Jesus, the King!
He came and He conquered—His victory sing.

title: Simply trusting every day
author: Edgar Page Stites (1876)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Even when my faith is small,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Into this poor heart of mine;
While He leads I cannot fall,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Singing, if my way is clear,
Praying, if the path is drear;
If in danger, for Him call;

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Trusting as the days go by;

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Trusting Him while life shall last,
Trusting Him till earth is past,

title: Sovereign grace! o'er sin abounding
author: John Kent

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: 'Tis a deep that knows no sounding;
Who its breadth or length can tell?
Let my soul for ever dwell.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: What from Christ the soul can sever,
Once in Him, in Him for ever,
From the Strength of Israel's hands.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Heirs of God, joint-heirs with Jesus
Long ere time its race began;
O what wonders love hath done!

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: On such love, my soul, still ponder,
Love so great, so rich, so free!
Say, while lost in holy wonder,
Why, O Lord, such love to me?

title: Son of God, 'twas love that made Thee
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Son of God, 'twas love that made Thee
Die, our ruined souls to save;
'Twas our sins' vast load that laid Thee,
Lord of Life, within the grave;
Showed Thee conqueror o'er the tomb;
So the saints by Thy protection

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thou to heaven hast now ascended,
Ent'ring there by Thine own blood;
All Thy work of suff'ring ended,
Fully wrought the will of God.
For Thy Church Thou still art caring,
For us pleading in Thy love;
And our place of rest preparing

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Now the Holy Ghost doth gather
What a debt of love we owe Thee,
Love that we can ne'er express,
Since we, through the Spirit, know Thee,

title: Saviour, we remember Thee!
author: Samuel Trevor Francis

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: All Thy suffering on the tree:

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Love, eternal love to me: Saviour, we adore Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: When for sin Thy blood was shed,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Jesus, Lord, Thou now art risen!
Thou hast all our sins forgiven;
Haste we to our home in heaven:

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: We will praise Thee more and more;
Spread Thy Name from shore to shore

title: Sweet feast of love divine!
author: Edward Denny (1839)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: To feed upon this bread and wine,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Waits, Lord, from Thee to learn
The secrets of Thy Father's breast,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: The sweetness of the Bread of Life,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: That blood that flowed for sin
And feel the blessed pledge within
That we are loved of Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: O if this glimpse of love
What will it be, O Lord, above,

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: To see Thee face to face,
And all Thy ways of wondrous grace

title: Sweet are the seasons when we wait
author: Thomas Kelly

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Sweet are the seasons when we wait
To hear what God our Lord will say,
For they who watch at Wisdom's gate

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Behold us, Lord, a few of Thine
Who hither come to seek Thy face;
In mercy on Thy people shine
And let Thy presence fill the place.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: How sweet, how blessed is the thought
That Thou dost hear Thy people's cries!
And whether Thou dost give, or not,
'Tis love that grants, and love denies.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O teach us, Lord, to wait Thy will,
To be content with all Thou dost;
For us, Thy grace sufficient still,
With most supplied when needing most.

title: Saviour, through the desert lead us!
author: Thomas Kelly

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Saviour, through the desert lead us!
Thou from cruel chains hast freed us,
Thou hast laid the tyrant low;
Cheer us all our journey through.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: What a price Thy love has bought us;
Saviour, what a love is Thine!
Hitherto Thy power has brought us,
Power and love in Thee combine:

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Through a desert, waste and cheerless,
While we see Thee, Saviour, nigh.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: When we halt, no track discovering,
O'er our path Thy pillar hovering,
Fire by night, and cloud by day,
That we may not miss our way.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: When we hunger Thou wilt feed us;
Faint and thirsty, Thou wilt head us,
Streams shall from the rock abound:
What a Saviour we have found!

title: Sun and Shield, O Lord, art Thou
author: Horatius Bonar (1845)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Sun and Shield, O Lord, art Thou,
Never wilt Thou cease to shine,
Cheer our steps as on we go,
Come between us and the foe.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Bread and Wine, O Lord, art Thou,
Never wilt Thou cease to feed
Feed we still on bread divine,
Drink we still this heavenly wine.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Love and Life, O Lord, art Thou,
Ne'er to quicken shalt Thou cease,
All of life and love we need
Is in Thee, in Thee indeed.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Peace and Joy, O Lord, art Thou,
Joy that fades not, changes not,
Joy and peace we have in Thee,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Song and Strength, O Lord, art Thou,
Still to us this strength and song

title: Sweet is the savour of His Name
author: Thomas Kelly

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Sweet is the savour of His Name
Who suffered in His people's stead;
His portion here, reproach and shame:
He liveth now; He once was dead.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: He once was dead; the very same
Who sits on yonder throne above;
Who bears in heaven the greatest Name,
Whom angels serve, whom angels love.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: He once was dead; the very same
Who made the worlds—a work of power,
Who now upholds the mighty frame,
And keeps it till the final hour.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: He once was dead; but now He lives,
His glory fills all heaven above;
Its blessedness to heaven He gives.
The fountain He of joy and love.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: His people shall His triumph share,
With Him shall live, and with Him reign;
In heaven their joy is full, for there
They see the Lamb for sinners slain.

title: Sweeter sounds than music knows
author: John Newton (1779)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: All her hopes my spirit owes
To His birth, His Cross, His shame.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: When He came, the angels sang,
Who should louder sing than I?

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Did the Lord a man become
That He might the law fulfil,
Bleed and suffer in my room;
And canst thou, my tongue, be still?

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: No! I must my praises bring,
Though they worthless are and weak,
For should I refuse to sing
Sure the very stones would speak.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: O my Saviour, Shield, and Sun,
I will love Thee without end.

title: Sweet the moments, rich in blessing
author: James Allen tr/ad by William Walter Shirley (1761)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Sweet the moments, rich in blessing,
Which before the Cross we spend,
Life, and health, and peace possessing

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Here we rest, in wonder viewing
All our sins on Jesus laid,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Here we find the dawn of heaven,
While upon the Cross we gaze,
And our songs of triumph raise.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O that near the Cross abiding,
We may to the Saviour cleave!
Nought with Him our hearts dividing,
All for Him content to leave.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: May we still, the Cross discerning,
There for peace and comfort go;
All the depths of mercy know.

title: Take the world, but give me Jesus
author: Frances (Fanny) Jane Crosby (1879)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Take the world, but give me Jesus,
All its joys are but a name;

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Take the world, but give me Jesus,
With my Saviour watching o,er me
I can sing, though billows roll.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Take the world, but give me Jesus,
Let me see His constant smile;
Light will cheer me all the while.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Take the world, but give me Jesus,
In His Cross my trust shall be,
Face to face my Lord I see.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: O the height and depth of mercy!
O the length and breadth of love!

title: The atoning work is done
author: Thomas Kelly (1806)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: He stands in heaven, their great High Priest,
And bears their names upon His breast.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: But justice now withstands no more,
And mercy yields its boundless store.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: In Him the shadows of the law
Are all fulfilled, and now withdraw.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Hid from the eyes of men,
In brightest glory He will come
And take His waiting people home.

title: The Cross! the Cross! the blood-stained Cross!
author: John Hart Stockton

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: The Cross! the Cross! the blood-stained Cross!
The Cross of Christ I see,
It tells me of that precious blood
That once was shed for me.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The wrath! the wrath! the awful wrath
When bearing my sin's heavy load

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: But Jesus lives! the Saviour lives!
In heaven He pleads for me;
And boldly I approach to God,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: The crown! the crown! the glorious crown!
The crown of life! it shall be mine

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: He comes! He comes! the Saviour comes!
Who bled and died for me;
Then will I sing, with rapture sing,

title: The cloudless day is nearing
author: C. A. H.

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: When Thou, O Lord, wilt come,
Bright hosts on hosts around Thee
And all who once have found Thee
Breathe out new songs of praise.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: But how shall I then know Thee
What tokens true will show me

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thy wounds, Thy wounds, Lord Jesus,
Those deep, deep wounds will tell
From self, and death, and hell!
These link Thee once for ever
With all who own Thy grace;
No hand these bonds can sever,

title: The glory shines before me
author: Hannah Kilham Burlingham

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Though clouds may darken o'er me
I am not far from home.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I'm going to the better land.
For this is not my rest.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: The Lamb is there the glory!
The Lamb is there the light!
The voice of Jesus calls me,
My race will soon be run;
The prize will soon be won.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: I know that all is well;
My Father's care is o'er me,
The love of Christ constrains me,
His blood hath washed me white;

title: The Cross! the Cross!
author: E. M. Miln

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I see the standard rise: (2x for Yarmouth)
The Cross of Christ before thee;

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I see the banner wave: (2x for Yarmouth)

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Ah, who at last shall gain it?
That Cross a crown affords. (2x for Yarmouth)

title: The countless multitude on high
author: Archibald Rutherford & R. Sandeman (1775)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: That tune their songs to Jesus' Name,
All merit of their own deny,
Firm on the ground of sovereign grace,
The only song in that blest place

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: With spotless robes of purest white,
They shout, with transports of delight,
To Him who sits upon the throne,
And to the Lamb whose blood was shed;
Thou! Thou art worthy! Thou alone.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: "For Thou wast slain, and in Thy blood
These robes were washed so spotless pure;
Thou mad'st us kings and priests to God,
For ever let Thy praise endure.
Let us with joy adopt the strain
We soon shall sing for ever there:
Worthy alone the crown to wear!"

title: The day of glory bearing
author: James George Deck (1841)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: We hail, in hope to meet Thee,
When every heart shall greet Thee

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: And bruise Thee in our stead.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: For all who on Thee rest,
Till Thou shalt come in glory

title: The Gospel of Thy grace
author: James George Deck (1841)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: For God so loved the world

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Bids me to look and live.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: But that the world might have

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Give me the peace of faith

title: The happy morn is come;
author: Thomas Haweis (1792)

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: On Him our help is laid,

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Since Jesus liveth that was dead.

title: The Head that once was crowned with thorns
author: Thomas Kelly (1820)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: The Head that once was crowned with thorns

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Delight of all who dwell above,
To us still manifest Thy love
That we its depths may know.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: To us Thy Cross, with all its shame,
With all its grace be given!
Though earth disowns Thy lowly Name,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Who suffer with Thee, Lord, below,
Then let it be our joy to know
Thy way of peace and love.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: To us Thy Cross is life and health,
Though shame and death to Thee;
Our present glory, joy and wealth,

title: The holiest now we enter
author: Mary Bowly Peters

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Though great may be our dulness
In thought, and word, and deed,
Of Him who meets our need.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: To all our prayers and praises

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O God, we come with singing,
Our names to Thee is bringing,
For us He wears the mitre
For us His robes are whiter

title: The Lamb of God to slaughter led
author: Robert Cleaver Chapman

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: The Lamb of God to slaughter led,
The crown of thorns upon His head,
They nail Him to the tree!

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The Father gives His only Son;
For us, the guilty and undone,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thy Name is holy, O our God!
Thy bosom is Thy saints' abode,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Enthroned with Thee now sits the Lord,
Justice, that smote Him with the sword,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Eternal death was once our doom;
Now death has lost its sting;
We rose with Jesus from the tomb

title: The Lord Himself shall come
author: James Montgomery & John Russell Darbyshire

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Thousands shall answer from the tomb,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Shall be our shout of victory,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: How shall I meet those eyes?
And own myself the Saviour's prize;

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: How shall I love that word?
How oft repeat before the throne,

title: The God of Abraham praise
author: Daniel ben Judah tr/ad by Thomas Olivers (c.14)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I bow and bless the sacred Name,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: From earth I rise, and seek my joys
And Him my only portion make,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Shall guide me all my pilgrim days,
He calls a worm His friend,
And He shall save me to the end

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: And sing the wonders of His grace

title: There is a fountain filled with blood
author: William Cowper & Unknown (1771)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: There is a fountain filled with blood
And sinners plunged beneath that flood

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The dying thief rejoiced to see
And there have I, as vile as he,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Dear dying Lamb! Thy precious blood
Till all the ransomed Church of God
Be saved, to sin no more.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: E'er since, by faith, I saw the stream
Redeeming love has been my theme,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Soon, in a nobler, sweeter song,
I'll sing Thy power to save,
And with the heavenly, blood-bought throng

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Lord, I believe Thou hast prepared,
For me a blood-bought, free reward,

stanzas.label: Verse 7
lines: 'Tis strung and tuned for endless years,
To sound in God the Father's ears

title: The Lord is risen indeed!
author: Thomas Kelly (1802)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Mercy and truth are now agreed,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The captive Surety now is freed,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: He lives to die no more;
He lives, His people's cause to plead,
Whose curse and shame He bore.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: And hell has lost its prey;
And with Him all the ransomed seed

title: The Lord of Glory! Who is He?
author: Robert Cleaver Chapman

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: The Lord of Glory! Who is He?
Who is the King of Glory?
Only the Son of God can be
The Christ, the King of Glory:
Consider all His wounds, and see
How Jesus' death upon the tree

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Above all heavens, at God's right hand,
Now sits the King of Glory;
The angels, by His favour, stand
Swiftly they fly at His command
To guard His own of every land,
To keep the heirs of glory.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Death and the grave confess the Lamb
To be the King of Glory;
The powers of darkness dread His Name,
He said: "E'er Abram was, I am;"

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Thrice happy who in Him believe,
They soon will share His glory;
Born of His Spirit, they receive;
Taught by His Cross, for sin they grieve,
He calls them brethren, and they cleave
To Him, their hope of glory.

title: The Lord is risen: now death's dark judgment flood
author: William Paton MacKay

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: The Lord is risen: now death's dark judgment flood
Is passed in Him who bought us with His blood.
The Lord is risen: we stand beyond the doom
Of all our sin, through Jesus' empty tomb.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The Lord is risen: with Him we also rose,
And in His grave see all our vanquished foes.
The Lord is risen: beyond the judgment land
In Him, in resurrection-life, we stand.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: The Lord is risen: we're now redeemed to God
And tread the desert which His feet have trod.
The Lord is risen: the sanctuary's our place
Where now we dwell before the Father's face.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: The Lord is risen: the Lord is gone before;
We long to see Him and to sin no more!
The Lord is risen: our trumpet shout shall be,
"Thou hast prevailed! Thy people, Lord, are free!"

title: The night is wearing fast away
author: Mary Jane Hoare

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: The night is wearing fast away,
When Christ shall all His grace display
Gloomy and dark the night hath been,
And long the way, and dreary;
And sad the weeping saints are seen,
And faint, and worn, and weary.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Ye mourning pilgrims, dry your tears,
And hush each sigh of sorrow;
The light of that bright morn appears,
Lift up your heads! Behold from far
It is the bright and Morning Star

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: And see that star-like host around
Hark! hark! the trumpet's gladdening sound,
He comes! The Bridegroom promised long;
Go forth with joy to meet Him,
And raise the new and nuptial song,
In cheering strains to greet Him.

title: There is a fold whence none can stray
author: John East

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: There is a fold whence none can stray,
Where sultry sun, or stormy day,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: There is a Shepherd living there,
care The flock for which He bled.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: There congregate the sons of light,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Their joy bursts forth in strains of love
And through the heavenly courts above

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: O may our faith take up that sound

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Until we reach that happy shore
And join to swell their strain,
And from our God go out no more

title: The Saviour lives, no more to die;
author: Samuel Medley

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: The Saviour lives, no more to die;
He lives our Head, enthroned on high;
He lives triumphant o'er the grave;

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: He lives to still His people's fears;
He lives to wipe away their tears;
He lives their mansions to prepare;
He lives to bring them safely there.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: The chief of sinners He receives;
His saints He loves, and never leaves;
He'll guard us safe from every ill,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Then let our souls in Him rejoice
And sing His praise with cheerful voice;
Our doubts and fears for ever gone,
For Christ is on the Father's throne.

title: The sorrows of the daily life
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: The sorrows of the daily life,
The shadows o'er my path which fall,
Too oft obscure the glory's light
Until I rise above them all.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I stand, my God, with Thee alone,
Bathed in the fullest, clearest light,
The glory that surrounds the throne.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Calm in Thy secret presence, Lord,
I rest this weary soul of mine;
Feed on the fullness of Thy word,
And die to all the things of time.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Alone with Thee, O Master, where
The light of earthly glory dies,
To do what Thine own heart will prize.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Such be my path through life down here,
One long, close, lonely walk with Thee,
Until past every doubt and fear,
Thy face in light above I see.

title: The love that Jesus had for me
author: Jane (Jonathan? --hymntime.com) E. Hall

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: The love that Jesus had for me,
To suffer on the cruel tree
That I a ransomed soul might be,
Is more than tongue can tell!

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The many sorrows that He bore,
And O the crown of thorns He wore,
That I might live for evermore,
Is more than tongue can tell!

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: The peace I have in Him, my Lord,
Who pleads before the throne of God
The merit of His precious blood,
Is more than tongue can tell!

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: The joy that comes when He is near,
The rest He gives, so free from fear,
The Hope in Him, so bright and clear,
Is more than tongue can tell.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: His love is more than tongue can tell!
His love is more than tongue can tell!
The love that Jesus had for me
Is more than tongue can tell!

title: The veil is rent: Lo! Jesus stands
author: James George Deck (1841)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: The veil is rent: Lo! Jesus stands
And clouds of incense from His hands

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: His precious blood is sprinkled there,
And His own wounds in heaven declare
His work on earth is done.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: "'Tis finished!" on the Cross He said,
'Tis finished! Now He lives to plead

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: 'Tis finished! Here our souls can rest,
By Him, our Sacrifice and Priest,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Before Thy throne Thy children fall,

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Boldly our heart and voice we raise,
His Name, His blood, our plea;
Assured our prayers and songs of praise

title: The night is far spent, the day is at hand;
author: Thomas Kelly (1836)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: The night is far spent, the day is at hand;
Already the dawn may be seen in the sky;
Rejoice then, ye saints, 'tis your Lord's own command;
Rejoice, for the coming of Jesus draws nigh.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: What a day will that be when the Saviour appears!
How welcome to Those who have shared in His Cross!
A crown incorruptible then will be theirs,
A rich compensation for suff'ring and loss.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: What is loss in this world when compared to that day,
To the glory that then will from heaven be revealed;
"The Saviour is coming," His people may say,
"The Lord whom we look for, our Sun and our Shield."

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O pardon us, Lord! that our love to Thy Name
Is so faint, with so much our affections to move;
Our deadness should fill us with grief and with shame!
So much to be loved, and so little to love.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: O kindle within us a holy desire
Like that which was found in Thy people of old!
Who felt all Thy love, and whose hearts were on fire
While they waited impatient Thy face to behold.

title: There is a Name I love to hear
author: Frederick Whitfield (©1855)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: There is a Name I love to hear,
I love to speak its worth;
It sounds like music in mine ear,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: It tells me of a Saviour's love
Who died to set me free;
It tells me of His precious blood,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: It tells me of a Father's smile
It cheers me through this "little while,"

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: It bids my trembling soul rejoice,
It tells me, in a "still, small voice"

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Jesus! The Name I love so well,
The Name I love to hear;
No saint on earth its worth can tell,

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: This Name shall shed its fragrance still
Shall sweetly smooth the rugged hill
That leads me up to God.

stanzas.label: Verse 7
lines: And there, with all the blood-bought throng,
I'll sing the new, eternal song

title: The wanderer no more will roam
author: Mary Jane Deck Walker

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: The wanderer no more will roam,
The lost one to the fold hath come,
O Lamb of God, in Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Though clad in rags, by sin defiled,
The Father hath embraced His child;
O Lamb of God, in Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: It is the Father's joy to bless,
His love provides for me a dress,
O Lamb of God in Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Now shall my famished soul be fed,
A feast of love for me is spread,
I feed upon the children's bread,
O Lamb of God, in Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Yea, in the fullness of His grace
He puts me in the children's place,
Where I may gaze upon His face,
O Lamb of God, in Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: I cannot half His love express,
Yet, Lord, with joy my lips confess,
O Lamb of God, in Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 7
lines: And when I in Thy likeness shine,
The glory and the praise be Thine,
O Lamb of God, in Thee.

title: Thy Name we bless, Lord Jesus!
author: Samuel Prideaux Tregelles

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Thy Name we bless, Lord Jesus!
How great Thy love, all praise above,
In giving Thee was shown us;
Now by Thy blood-redeemed to God,
As children He doth own us.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thou hadst with God the Father,
He gave His Son, that He in one
Our sins were all laid on Thee,
It was for us Thou suffer'dst thus,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thou from the dead wast raised,
The Church is free, as risen in Thee,
To God's right hand in heaven;
The Lamb once slain, alive again,
To Thee all power is given.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Till Thou shalt come to take us home
We're sealed by God the Spirit.
When we shall know more fully
The grace divine that made us Thine,
Thou Lamb of God most holy.

title: Thou art coming, O our Saviour!
author: Frances Ridley Havergal

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Thou art coming, O our Saviour!
Well may we rejoice and sing.
Thou art coming! Rays of glory,
Through the veil Thy death has rent,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thou art coming! Not a shadow,
Not a mist, and not a tear,
Not a sin, and not a sorrow
On that sunrise grand and clear:
Nothing else seems worth a thought;
And the bliss Thy pain hath bought.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thou art coming! We are waiting
Asking not the day or hour,
Thou are coming! At Thy table
As we meet Thee in communion,

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Thou art coming! Thou art coming!
We shall meet Thee on Thy way;
Thou art coming! We shall see Thee,
And be like Thee on that day:
Thou art coming! Thou art coming!
O the joy to see Thee reigning,

title: Through Thy precious body broken
author: Elizabeth Dark

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O what words to sinners spoken
Precious as the blood that bought us,
Perfect as the love that sought us,
Holy as the Lamb that brought us

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: When we see Thy love unshaken
Scorned by man, by God forsaken
Thy loved Cross alone can charm us,
Shame need now no more alarm us,
Glad we follow, nought can harm us

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Lamb of God, through Thee we enter
Cleansed by Thee, we boldly venture
Not a stain; a new creation;
Ours is such a full salvation;

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Forth we hasten, fear no danger
Drawn by love that knows no measure,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Soon Thy saints shall all be gathered
All at home, no more be scattered,
Nought from Thee our hearts shall sever;
We shall see Thee, grieve Thee never;
Praise the Lamb! shall sound for ever

title: Thou hidden love of God, Whose height
author: Gerhard Tersteegen tr/ad by John Wesley (1729)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Thou hidden love of God, Whose height,
Whose depth unfathomed no man knows,
I see from far Thy beauteous light,
And inly sigh for Thy repose:
My heart is pained, nor can it be
At rest till it finds rest in Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Is there a thing beneath the sun
That strives with Thee my heart to share?
O tear it thence, and reign alone
The Lord of every motion there!
Then shall my heart from earth be free,
When it has found repose in Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O hide this self from me that I
No more, but Christ in me may live!
Nor let one darling sin survive:
In all things nothing may I see,
Nothing desire, or seek, but Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Each moment calls from earth away
My heart which lowly waits Thy call;
Speak to my inmost soul and say,
"I am thy Life, thy God, thy All!"
To know Thy power, to hear Thy voice,
To feel Thy love, be all my choice.

title: Thy broken body, gracious Lord
author: Samuel Prideaux Tregelles

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Is shadowed by this broken bread:
The wine, which in this cup is poured,
Points to the blood which Thou hast shed.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: And while we meet together thus
We show that we are one in Thee;
Thy precious blood was shed for us,
Thy death, O Lord, has set us free.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Brethren! In Thee, in union sweet,
For ever be Thy grace adored!
'Tis in Thy Name that now we meet,
And know Thou'rt with us, gracious Lord.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: We have one hope that Thou wilt come;
Thee in the air we wait to see,
When Thou wilt take Thy people home,
And we shall ever reign with Thee.

title: Though often here we're weary
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Where all is peace and love:
O then let us press forward
We'll soon be free from sorrow,
From toil, and care, and pain.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Our Saviour will be with us
He'll give us grace to conquer,
And take us home to rest.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Who bought us with His blood;
Who keeps us to the end:
To the Triune God be glory,

title: Through the dark path of sorrow
author: Mary Carter

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Through the dark path of sorrow
And the thick clouds that gather

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: From the cold world that knoweth

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: In the fierce hour that trieth
Let the weak and the feeble
In the blast of the terrible,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: When the hearts of all others
Then we lift up our heads,

title: Thou, my everlasting portion!
author: Frances (Fanny) Jane Crosby (1874)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: More than friend or life to me,
Saviour, let me walk with Thee.
Close to Thee, close to Thee,
Close to Thee, close to Thee,
Saviour, let me walk with Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Not for ease or worldly pleasure,
Nor for fame my prayer shall be,
Gladly will I toil and suffer,
Only let me walk with Thee.
Close to Thee, close to Thee,
Close to Thee, close to Thee,
Gladly will I toil and suffer,
Only let me walk with Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Lead me through the vale of shadows,
Bear me o'er life's fitful sea;
Then the gate of life eternal
I shall enter, Lord, with Thee,
Close to Thee, close to Thee,
Close to Thee, close to Thee,
Then the gate of life eternal
I shall enter, Lord, with Thee.

title: Thy love we own, Lord Jesus;
author: W. Yerbury

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Thy love we own, Lord Jesus;
Within the veil Thou dost prevail,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thy love we own, Lord Jesus!
For though Thy toils are ended,
Thy tender heart doth take its part
And bidst us cheer while pilgrims here,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thy love we own, Lord Jesus!
Thy way is traced before Thee;
Thou wilt descend, and we ascend,
Call forth Thy saints to meet Thee,
With gladness then we'll greet Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Thy love we own, Lord Jesus!
And wait to see Thy glory,
To know as known, and fully own
Then endless praise our lips shall raise
For love like Thine, Lord Jesus.

title: Through the love of God our Saviour
author: Mary Bowly Peters (1847)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Through the love of God our Saviour
Free and changeless is His favour;
Precious is the blood that healed us,
Perfect is the grace that sealed us,
Strong the hand stretched forth to shield us,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Ours is such a full salvation;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Faith can sing through days of sorrow,

title: Twas love that sought Gethsemane
author: William Dickinson

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Or Judas ne'er had found Thee;
'Twas love that nailed Thee to the tree
Or iron ne'er had bound Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: 'Twas love that lived, 'twas love that died,
With endless life to bless us;
Well hast Thou won Thy blood-bought Bride,

title: This world is a wilderness wide
author: John Nelson Darby

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: This world is a wilderness wide,
I have nothing to seek or to choose;
I've no thought in the waste to abide;
I have nought to regret nor to lose.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The path where my Saviour is gone
Has led up to His Father and God,
To the place where He's now on the throne;
And His strength shall be mine on the road.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: With Him shall my rest be on high,
When in holiness bright I sit down,
In the joy of His love ever nigh,
In the peace that His presence shall crown.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: 'Tis the treasure I've found in His love
That has made me a pilgrim below;
And 'tis there, when I reach Him above
As I'm known, all His fullness I'll know.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: And Saviour, 'tis Thou from on high
I await till the time Thou shalt come,
To take him Thou hast led by Thine eye
To Thyself in Thy heavenly home.

title: "Till He come!" O let the words
author: Edward Henry Bickersteth (1861)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: "Till He come!" O let the words
In their golden light be seen;
Let us think how heaven and home

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: When the weary ones we love
When their words of love and cheer
Fall no longer on our ear,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Clouds and darkness round us press;
Would we have one sorrow less?
All the sharpness of the cross,
All that tells the world is loss,
Death, and darkness, and the tomb,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Sweet the feast of love divine,
Call us round His heavenly board,
Some from earth, from glory some,

title: Tis we, O Lord, whom Thou hast shown
author: Mary Bowly Peters

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Tis we, O Lord, whom Thou hast shown
We, who forgiving love have known,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thy presence called for Israel's praise,
And when in death they met their gaze,
What songs of glorious triumph rose.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: And we have known redemption, Lord,
From bondage worse than theirs by far;
Sin held us by a stronger cord,
Yet by Thy mercy free we are.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O blessed Lord! Thy groans and tears,
Thy death the power of darkness broke;
Bursting the chains we wore for years
It freed us from the iron yoke.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Thy people from the deep couldst bring;
The glorious triumph all Thine own:
Thy Name, Thy might, Thy grace, we sing.

title: To Thee, O gracious Saviour!
author: John Samuel Bewley Monsell

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: My peace is in Thy favour,
Though all the world deceive me
I know that I am Thine,
And Thou wilt never leave me,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: O Thou whose mercy found me,
And then for ever bound me

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: My grief is in the dullness
My joy is in Thy merit,
That binds my life to Thine.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Have failed in love to Thee,
O for a heart to love Thee
In deed, or word, or thought.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: O for the bliss that by it

title: 'Tis the blessed hour of prayer when our hearts lowly bend
author: Frances (Fanny) Jane Crosby (1880)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: 'Tis the blessed hour of prayer when our hearts lowly bend,
And we gather to Jesus, our Saviour and Friend;
If we come to Him in faith, His protection to share,
What a balm for the weary! O how sweet to be there.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: "'Tis the blessed hour of prayer when the Saviour-draws near
With tender compassion His people to hear;
When He tells us we may cast at His feet every care:
What a balm for the weary! O how sweet to be there.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: "'Tis the blessed hour of prayer when the tempted and tried,
To the Saviour who loves them, their sorrows confide;
With a sympathising heart He removes every care:
What a balm for the weary! O how sweet to be there.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: At the blessed hour of prayer, if we firmly believe
That the blessing we ask for we'll surely receive,
In the fullness of delight we shall lose every care:
What a balm for the weary! O how sweet to be there.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: What a balm for the weary!
O how sweet to be there.

title: Tis finished all: our souls to win
author: Sir Edward Denny

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Tis finished all: our souls to win
His life the blessed Saviour gave;
Then rising, left His people's sin
Behind Him in His open grave.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Past suff'ring now, the tender heart,
Of Jesus, on His Father's throne,
Still in our sorrow bears a part,
And feels it as He felt His own.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Sweet thought! We have a Friend above,
Our weary, faltering steps to guide,
Who follows with the eye of love
The little flock for which He died.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: and more On Thee alone to cast our care;
And gazing on Thy Cross, adore
The wondrous grace that brought Thee there.

title: Tis past, the dark and dreary night.
author: Sir Edward Denny

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Tis past, the dark and dreary night.
And, Lord, we hail Thee now,
Our Morning Star, without a cloud

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thy path on earth. the Cross, the grave,
And O sweet thought! Thine eye shall weep.
Thy heart shall break no more.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Deep were those sorrows, deeper still
The love that brought Thee low,
That bade the streams of life from Thee,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Drawn from Thy pierced and bleeding side,
Speaks peace to every heart that knows

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Yet 'tis not that we know the joy
But, happier far, Thy saints are called

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: So closely are we linked in love,
That all Thy bliss and glory then

title: To Calvary, Lord, in spirit now
author: Sir Edward Denny

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: To Calvary, Lord, in spirit now
To dwell upon Thy dying love,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: That feels the plague of sin,
Yet knows the deep, mysterious joy

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: There, through Thine hour of deepest woe,
Grace there its wondrous victory gained,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O Lamb of God! Thy bleeding wounds,
Have drawn our willing hearts to Thee,
And linked our life with Thine.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Our longing eyes would fain behold
Once wrung with bitterest anguish, wear

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Thy sympathies and hopes are ours:
We long, O Lord, to see

title: Unworthy our thanksgiving
author: Mary Bowly Peters

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Our Priest, to bear it in;

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: A bond that nought can sever
Has fixed us to the Rock;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: As dews that fall on Hermon
Through Thee to us doth flow.
Ah, then, how good and pleasant,
As one, to live in love,

title: Unto Him who loved us, gave us
author: Samuel Miller Waring

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Unto Him who loved us, gave us
Every pledge that love could give;
Freely shed His blood to save us;
Gave His life that we might live;

title: Unto the Lamb that was slain
author: Isaac Watts

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Unto the Lamb that was slain,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thou has redeemed us with Thy blood,
Hast made us kings and priests to God,
And we shall reign with Thee.

title: Walk in the light, so shalt thou know
author: Bernard Barton (1826)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Walk in the light, so shalt thou know

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Walk in the light, o'er sin abhorred
The blood of Jesus Christ Thy Lord

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Walk in the light, and thou shalt find
Who dwells in cloudless light enshrined,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Walk in the light, and e'en the tomb
Glory shall chase away the gloom,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Walk in the light, and thine shall be.
For God, by grace, shall dwell in thee,

title: We bless our Saviour's Name
