author: James George Deck (1841)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: To suffer, once to earth He came,
And now He's crowned in heaven.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Rememb'ring this we break the bread,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Let each by faith Thy body see

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Our theme of joy and wonder here,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Our souls to cleave to Thee!
And ever in our hearts remain

title: We come, our gracious Father
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Of peace with Thee, our God;

title: We love to sing with one accord
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: We love to sing with one accord
We love to come before Thee, Lord,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: We love to lean upon Thy breast
And find our soul's enduring rest

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: He witnessed to the constant guilt
That marked the path we trod;
He witnessed that Thy blood was spilt
To bring us nigh to God.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: He made us look to Thee alone,
He brings the message from the throne,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: In songs of praise we would record
And standing in Thy presence, Lord,

title: We praise Thy great love
author: William Paton MacKay

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: For the joy Thou hast given

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: For the Word of Thy love,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Who has stood in our place,
We shall show in the glory

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: For the day Thou shalt come;

title: We're a pilgrim band in a stranger land
author: A. B. MacKay

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: We're a pilgrim band in a stranger land
Where the wondrous Cross, with its gain and loss,
Is the sum of our history:
There we lost our stand in a death-doomed land,
As children of wrath by the fall;
There we gained a place as heirs of grace
At the feast in the heavenly hall.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: We read our guilt in the blood that was spilt,
And we weep o'er the crimson flow;
But we joy in the grace of the unveiled face
And as sons of God, redeemed by blood,
We cross the sand to the pleasant land
And the joys of an endless day.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: We were children of night, kept far from the light,
But Jesus' pains broke the iron chains,
And redeemed our souls from woe:
Now as children of light we walk and we fight
In a path of triumphant joy;
For our strength is the Lord, whose Word is our sword,
While faith is the shield we employ.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Our home is with God, and our path has been trod
By the faithful of ages all,
And us He will bring, as on eagles' wing,
To our place in the marriage hall:
Then, then shall we sing, as the Bride of the King,
Of the blood that has brought us so nigh,
To bask in the blaze of the Ancient of Days,

title: We sing the praise of Him who died
author: Thomas Kelly (1815)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: We sing the praise of Him who died,
Of Him who died upon the Cross,
For Him we count the world but loss.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Inscribed upon the Cross we see,
The Lamb who died upon the tree
Has brought us mercy from above.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: The Cross! It takes our guilt away;
It holds the fainting spirit up;
It cheers with hope the gloomy day

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: It makes the coward spirit brave,
And nerves the feeble arm to fight;
It takes its terror from the grave,
And gilds the bed of death with light.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: The balm of life, the cure of woe,
The measure and the pledge of love,
The theme of praise in heaven above.

title: What grace, O Lord, and beauty shone
author: Edward Denny (1839)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: What grace, O Lord, and beauty shone
What patient love was seen in all
Thy life and death of woe!

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: For ever on Thy burdened heart

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thy foes might hate, despise, revile,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O give us hearts to love like Thee!
Like Thee, O Lord, to grieve
Far more for others' sins, than all

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: One with Thyself, may every eye,
That gentleness and grace that spring

title: What a Friend we have in Jesus
author: Joseph Medicott Scriven & Charles Crozat Converse (1857)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: What a Friend we have in Jesus,
All our sins and grief's to bear!
O what peace we often forfeit,
O what needless pain we bear!
All because we do not carry

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Take it to the Lord in prayer!
Can we find a friend so faithful,
Who will all our sorrows share?
Take it to the Lord in prayer.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Cumbered with a load of care?
Take it to the Lord in prayer!
Do thy friends despise, forsake thee?
Take it to the Lord in prayer!
In His arms He'll take and shield thee,
Thou shalt find a solace there.

title: We'll sing of the Shepherd that died
author: Thomas Kelly

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: We'll sing of the Shepherd that died,
That died for the sake of the flock;
His love to the utmost was tried,
But firmly endured as a rock.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: When blood from a victim must flow,
This Shepherd, by pity, was led
To stand between us and the foe,
And willingly die in our stead.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Our song then for ever should be
Of the Shepherd who gave Himself thus;
No subject's so glorious as He,
No theme's so affecting to us.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: We'll sing of such subjects alone
None other our tongues shall employ,
Till fully His love becomes known
In yonder bright regions of joy.

title: When first, o'erwhelmed with sin and shame
author: James George Deck (1841)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: When first, o'erwhelmed with sin and shame,
To Jesus' Cross I trembling came,
Burdened with guilt, and full of fear,
Yet drawn by love to venture near,
Pardon I found, and peace with God,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: My sin is gone, my fear is o'er,
I shun God's presence now no more;
He sits upon the throne of grace,
He bids me boldly seek His face:
Sprinkled upon the throne of God
I see that rich, atoning blood.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Here I can rest without a fear;
By this, to God I now draw near;
By this, I triumph over sin,
For this has made and keeps me clean;
And when I reach the throne of God
I'll praise that rich, atoning blood.

title: When languor and disease invade
author: Augustus Montague Toplady (1780)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: 'Tis sweet to look beyond our cage

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Sweet to look inward, and attend
Sweet to look upward to the place

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Sweet to look back, and see my name
In life's fair book set down;
Sweet to look forward, and behold

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Sweet to reflect how grace divine
Sweet to remember that His blood

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Sweet in God's righteousness to stand,
Sweet to experience, day by day,

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Sweet on His faithfullness to rest,
Sweet on His covenant of grace

stanzas.label: Verse 7
lines: Sweet, in the confidence of faith,
Sweet to lie passive in His hands,
And know no will but His.

title: Come, ye saints, rejoice with Jesus
author: Richard Chenevix Trench (George Frederick Trench?)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Come, ye saints, rejoice with Jesus,
Called with Him His joy to share;
We His friends and followers are:
Now the heart of Jesus cheer.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Praise His Name for these great mercies,
Turn we now His praise to sing:
Make the court of heaven ring.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Praise Him! Praise Him! Never ceasing,
Ye who prove God's boundless grace;
Have we asked, and has He answered?

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Heartfelt praise to God we give;
They should loudest sing His praises
Let us render while we live.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Shout, ye ransomed heirs of heaven!
Saved to show God's praises forth;
While ye shout, let joys unspoken
Fill your hearts with heavenly mirth:
Put to shame the joys of earth

title: When I survey the wondrous Cross
author: Isaac Watts & Hymns Ancient and Modern (1707)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: When I survey the wondrous Cross
On which the Prince of Glory died,
My richest gain I count but loss,
And pour contempt on all my pride.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Forbid it, Lord, that I should boast,
Save in the Cross of Christ, my God;
All the vain things that charm me most
I sacrifice them to His blood.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: See from His head, His hands, His feet,
Sorrow and love flow mingled down;
Did e'er such love and sorrow meet,
Or thorns compose so rich a crown?

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Were the whole realm of nature mine
That were an offering far too small;
Demands my heart, my life, my all!

title: While in sweet communion feeding
author: Sir Edward Denny

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: On this earthly bread and wine,
Saviour, may we see Thee bleeding
On the Cross to make us Thine!
Now our eyes we would be closing
More of grace and mercy know.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Though unseen, be ever near us
With the still small voice of love,
Whispering words of peace to cheer us,
Bring before us all the story
Of Thy life and death of woe,
And, with hopes of endless glory,
Wean our hearts from all below.

title: When peace, like a river, attendeth my way
author: Horatio Gates Spafford (1873)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: When peace, like a river, attendeth my way,
Whatever my lot, Thou hast taught me to say,
It is well, it is well with my soul.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Though Satan should buffet, though trials should come,
That Christ hath regarded my helpless estate,
And hath shed His own blood for my soul.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: My sin, O the bliss of this glorious thought!
My sin, not in part but the whole,
Is nailed to His Cross, and I bear it no more;
Praise the Lord, praise the Lord, O my soul!

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: For me be it Christ, be it Christ hence to live!
If death's waters o'er me shall roll
No pang shall be mine, for in death as in life,
Thou wilt whisper Thy peace to my soul.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: But, Lord, 'tis for Thee, for Thy coming we wait;
The sky, not the grave is our goal:
O trump of the angel! O voice of the Lord!
Blessed hope! Blessed rest of my soul!

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: It is well with my soul,
It is well, it is well with my soul.

title: With Jesus in our midst
author: Robert Cleaver Chapman

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Though many, we are one in Christ,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Our sins were laid on Him
With Christ we died and rose again,
And sit with Him on high.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Faith eats the bread of life,
Thus we, in love together knit,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Soon shall the night be gone,
The marriage supper of the Lamb

title: With joy we meditate the grace
author: Isaac Watts (1707)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: With joy we meditate the grace

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: He knows what sore temptations are

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: No stain of sin did e'er defile

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: He, when He sojourned here below,
Poured forth His cries and tears;

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Then boldly let our faith address

title: Hark! hark! hear the glad tidings
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Hark! hark! hear the glad tidings,
Robed, robed, in honour and glory,
To gather His ransomed ones home:
To gather His ransomed ones home.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Joy, joy, sound it more loudly;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Now, now, through a glass darkly,
Soon, soon, we shall behold Him,
Cloudless and bright in our home:
Cloudless and bright in our home.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Long, long, have we been waiting,
Who, who love His blest Name;

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Still, still, rest on the promise;
Cling, cling, fast to His Word;
Wait, wait, He will not tarry,
We'll patiently wait for the Lord:
We'll patiently wait for the Lord.

title: Worthy, worthy is the Lamb!
author: William Paton MacKay

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thou redeem'st our souls to God

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thou has made us kings and priests

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: We shall ever reign with Thee,

title: I am Thine, O Lord! I have heard Thy voice
author: Frances (Fanny) Jane Crosby (1875)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I am Thine, O Lord! I have heard Thy voice,
And it told Thy love to me;
But I long to rise in the arms of faith,
And be closer drawn to Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Consecrate me now to Thy service, Lord,
By the power of grace divine;
Let my soul look up with a steadfast hope,
And my will be lost in Thine.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O the pure delight of a single hour,
That before Thy throne I spend!
When I kneel in prayer, and with Thee, my God,
I commune as friend with friend.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: There are depths of love that I cannot know
Till I cross the narrow sea;
There are heights of joy that I may not reach
Till I rest in peace with Thee.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Draw me nearer, nearer blessed Lord,
To the Cross where Thou hast died;
Draw me nearer, nearer, nearer blessed Lord,

title: I will never, never leave thee
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I will never, never leave thee,
I will guard, and save, and keep thee,
For My Name and mercy's sake!
Fear no evil, fear no evil,
For I'll never, never leave thee,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: When the storm is raging round thee,
Call on Me in humble prayer,
I will fold My arms about thee,
Guard thee with the tend'rest care;
In the trial, in the trial
I will make thy pathway clear.
For I'll never, never leave thee,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: When the sky above is glowing,
And around thee all is bright,
I'll be with thee, I'll be with thee,
I will guide thy steps aright.
For I'll never, never leave thee,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: When thy soul is dark and clouded,
Filled with doubt, and grief, and care,
Through the mist by which 'tis shrouded.
I will make a light appear.
And the banner, and the banner
Of My love I will uprear.
For I'll never, never leave thee,

title: With steady pace the pilgrim moves
author: Richard Jukes (no B.H.B.C. entry available)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: With steady pace the pilgrim moves
And sings with cheerful heart and voice,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: His passage through a desert lies
He takes his staff, and, smiling, says,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: When tempted to forsake his God
He hears a voice which says, "Look up!

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: When stern affliction clouds his cheek,
And want stands at the door,
Hope cheers him with her sunniest note,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: And if on Jordan's bank he stands,

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: And so it is, for high in heaven

title: O thou whose bounty fills our cup
author: Jane Fox Crewdson (1860)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O thou whose bounty fills our cup
We give Thee thanks for every drop,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: We thank Thee for the desert road,
For all Thy goodness has bestowed,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: We thank Thee for the smile and frown,
And for the gain and loss;
We bless Thee for the future crown,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: We bless Thee for the glad increase,
And for the calm and settled peace

title: Just as I am, without one plea
author: Charlotte Elliott & William Batchelder Bradbury (1835)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Just as I am, without one plea
But that Thy blood was shed for me,
And that Thou bidst me come to Thee,
O Lamb of God, I come!

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Just as I am, and waiting not
To rid my soul of one dark blot,
To Thee, whose blood can cleanse each spot,
O Lamb of God, I come!

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Just as I am, though tossed about
With many a conflict, many a doubt,
O Lamb of God, I come!

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Just as I am, poor, wretched, blind,
Sight, riches, healing of the mind,
Yea, all I need in Thee to find,
O Lamb of God, I come!

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Just as I am, Thou wilt receive,
O Lamb of God, I come!

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Just as I am, Thy love unknown
Now to be Thine, yea, Thine alone,
O Lamb of God, I come!

title: Come ye, who bow to sovereign grace
author: Charles Haddon Spurgeon & Maria de Fleury

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Come ye, who bow to sovereign grace,
Join in a song of grateful praise

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Once in the gloomy grave He lay,
He bore the gates of death away:

title: Come sing, my soul, and praise the Lord
author: Daniel Webster Whittle

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Come sing, my soul, and praise the Lord,
Who hath redeemed thee by His blood;
Delivered thee from chains that bound,
And brought thee to redemption ground.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Once from my God I wandered far,
And with His holy will made war;
But now my songs to God abound:

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O joyous hour when God to me
My bonds were loosed, my soul unbound:

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: No works of merit now I plead,
But Jesus take for all my need;
No righteousness in me is found,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Come, weary soul, and here find rest;
The Christ who died, by God is crowned

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Redemption ground, the ground of peace!
Here let our praise to God abound,
Who saves us on redemption ground!

title: Endless praises to our Lord
author: Thomas Kelly

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: He is worthy, praise His Name!

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Saints, adore Him, sound His fame,
You He saved from endless shame;
He is worthy, praise His Name!

title: Father of mercies! In Thy Word
author: Anne Steele (1760)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Father of mercies! In Thy Word
For ever be Thy Name adored

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O may these holy pages be
And still new beauties may we see,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Teach us to love Thy sacred Word

title: Hark! How the blood-bought hosts above
author: John Kent

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Hark! How the blood-bought hosts above
Conspire to chant the Saviour's love,
And while they strike their golden lyres
This glorious theme each bosom fires,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: We'll join the song, for we can tell
How sovereign grace dissolved the spell
That kept us bound in chains;
And from that dear and happy day
How oft we've been constrained to say

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Yes! Though we've strayed, like saints of old,
Grace has restored us to the fold,
Thus saved by grace, we'd gladly sing,
Till all the earth and heavens ring

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: When called to meet our glorious Head,
That perfect love shall banish dread,
And when we rise to endless day,
We'll raise our voice and boldly say,

title: Here, O our Lord, we see Thee face to face;
author: Horatius Bonar (1855)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Here, O our Lord, we see Thee face to face;
Here would we touch and handle things unseen;
Here grasp with firmer hand th' eternal grace,
And all our weariness upon Thee lean.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Here would we feed upon the bread of God;
Here drink with Thee the royal wine of heaven;
Here would we lay aside each earthly load;
Here taste afresh the calm of sin forgiven.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Ours is the sin, but Thine the righteousness;
Ours is the guilt, but Thine the cleansing blood;
Here is our robe, our refuge and our peace,
Thy blood, Thy righteousness, O Lord, our God.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Too soon we rise; the symbols disappear;
The feast, though not the love, is past and gone;
The bread and wine remove, but Thou art here,
Nearer than ever, still our shield and sun.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: But see, the pillar-cloud is rising now,
And moving onward through the desert night;
It beckons, and we follow, for we know
It leads us to the heritage of light.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Feast after feast thus comes and passes by;
Yet passing, points to the glad feast above;
Giving sweet foretaste of the festal joy,
The Lamb's great bridal feast of bliss and love.

title: Is it Thy will that I should be
author: Anonymous (1888)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Is it Thy will that I should be
Buried, in symbol, Lord, with Thee?
Owning Thee by this solemn sign,
Telling the world that I am Thine.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: In all things to Thy will I'd bow;
I'll follow where my Saviour led,
And humbly in His footsteps tread.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Shows forth His love, who came to save;
And as I enter it, I see
The price my Saviour paid for me.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Forth from Thy burial, Lord, I come,
For Thou hast triumphed o'er the tomb;
My portion is no longer here.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: O may I count myself to be
Dead to the sins that wounded Thee,
Dead to the pleasures of this earth

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Lord Jesus, when I gaze on Thee
And all Thy radiant glory see,
That joy will far exceed the shame
I bear on earth for Thy loved name.

title: Jesus, the Christ! Eternal Word!
author: William Morshead (R. Morshead?)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: On Thee alone by faith we rest,
And lean our weakness on Thy breast.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thy blood hath washed us from our sin;
And Thou for us in all our need
At God's right hand dost ever plead.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O Keep us in the narrow way
That ne'er from Thee our footsteps stray;
Sustain our weakness, calm our fear,
And to Thy presence keep us near.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: And be it thus till that blest day
When God shall wipe all tears away:
Quickly! The promise of Thy word;
E'en so; Amen. Come, Jesus, Lord!

title: Join all the glorious names
author: Isaac Watts (1709)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: All are too mean to speak His worth,
Too mean to set our Saviour forth.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Our tongues would bless Thy name;
The joyful news of sins forgiven,
Of hell subdued, of peace with heaven.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Still keep us near Thy side;
O let our feet ne'er run astray,
Nor rove, nor seek the crooked way.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: He feeds His flock, He calls their names,
His bosom bears the tender lambs.

title: Light of the world, shine on our souls;
author: Edward Henry Bickersteth

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Light of the world, shine on our souls;
And while we meet to learn Thy truth

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: May we its riches, power, and depth,
Its joyful news of saving grace

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thus may Thy word be dearer still,
And as it richly dwells within,

title: Low in the grave He lay
author: Robert Lowry (1874)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Low in the grave He lay,

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Up from the grave He arose
With a mighty triumph o'er His foes;
He arose a victor from the dark domain,
And He lives for ever with His saints to reign;

title: O safe to the rock that is higher than I
author: William Orcutt Cushing (1876)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O safe to the rock that is higher than I
My soul in its conflicts and sorrows would fly;
So sinful, so weary, Thine, Thine would I be;
Thou blest Rock of Ages I'm hiding in Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: In the calm of the noontide, in sorrow's lone hour,
In times when temptation casts o'er me its power;
In the tempest of life, on its wide, heaving sea,
Thou blest Rock of Ages I'm hiding in Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: How oft in the conflict, when pressed by the foe,
I have fled to my refuge, and breathed out my woe;
How often, when trials like sea-billows roll,
Have I hidden in Thee O Thou rock of my soul.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Hiding in Thee, hiding in Thee,
Thou blest Rock of Ages I'm hiding in Thee.

title: O Lamb of God, we lift our eyes
author: Alexander Stewart

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Lamb of God, we lift our eyes
Shine on us, bid Thy light arise,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: We know Thy work for ever done,
Graced with the Spirit of the Son,
Made nigh to God in Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Yet would we prove Thine instant grace,
Lift on us now Thy glorious face,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: From Thy high place of purest light,
Shine forth upon our waiting sight

title: O how the thought that I shall know
author: Joseph Swain

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O how the thought that I shall know
For me and all the saints I love,
Both here and with Himself above,
At that sweet word, for ever.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: For ever to behold Him shine,
For evermore to call Him mine,
And see Him still before me;
For ever on His face to gaze,
And meet His full assembled rays,
While all His beauty He displays
To all His saints in glory.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Not all things else are half so dear
As is His blissful presence here;
What must it be in heaven?
'Tis heaven on earth we hear Him say,
As now we journey day by day,
Poor sinner, cast thy fears away,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: But how will His celestial voice
When we shall stand before Him;
When we for Him no longer wait,
But, opened wide the heavenly gate,
We rise our glorious Lord to meet,
And all His saints adore Him.

title: O They've reached the sunny shore
author: Mary Whateley

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O They've reached the sunny shore,
All their pain and grief are o'er,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: O the street is shining gold,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O they've done the weary fight,
Jesus saved them by His might,
And they walk with Him in white

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O they never shed a tear
For the Lord Himself is near,
And to Him they're ever dear

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: O they feel no chilling blast
For their winter time is past,

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: O they need no lamp at night
For the day is always bright,
And the Saviour is their light

stanzas.label: Verse 7
lines: O we'll form a happy band
When we hear our Lord's command,
And in glory round Him stand

title: Poor, weak, and worthless though I am
author: John Newton (1779)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Poor, weak, and worthless though I am,
I have a rich, almighty friend;
Jesus, the Saviour, is His name;
He freely loves, and without end.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: He ransomed me from hell with blood,
And by His power my foes controlled;
He found me wand'ring far from God,
And brought me to His chosen fold,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: He cheers my heart, my want supplies,
And says that I shall shortly be
Enthroned with Him above the skies;
O what a friend is Christ to me!

title: Rock of Ages! Cleft for me
author: Augustus Montague Toplady (1776)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Rock of Ages! Cleft for me,
Lo, I hide myself in Thee,
Where the water and the blood
From Thy wounded side which flowed
Are of sin the double cure,
Cleansing from its guilt and power.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Not the labour of my hands
Could my zeal no respite know,
Could my tears for ever flow,
All for sin could not atone:
Thou must save, and Thou alone.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Nothing in my hand I bring,
Simply to Thy cross I cling;
Naked, come to Thee for dress;
Helpless, look to Thee for grace;

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: While I draw this fleeting breath,
Should mine eyelids close in death,
When I soar to heights unknown,
And behold Thee on Thy throne,
Rock of Ages, cleft for me,
Still I'll hide myself in Thee.

title: Without a cloud between;
author: Albert Midlane

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: To see Him face to face;
Not struck with dire amazement dumb,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: To see Him as He is;
O who can tell the height of joy,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: For that sweet hour, from which my soul

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: The morning bright without a cloud,

title: Thou art the Everlasting Word
author: Josiah Condor (1836)

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: But the high myst'ries of His name

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Yet loving Thee, on whom His love
Thy members all, in Thee, above,
As one with Thee are blest.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Th' eternal theme of praise is this,

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Worthy, O Lamb of God, art Thou,
That every knee to Thee should bow.

title: When we reach our peaceful dwelling
author: William Paton MacKay & Anne Ross Cundell Cousin 1878

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: When we reach our peaceful dwelling
And our praise to Him is swelling,
When the path of prayer, and duty,
And we wake and see the beauty
Of our Saviour and our God:

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: And we gain the full perfection
When the life the flesh obscureth
In each radiant form shall shine,
And the joy that aye endureth

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Of His kindness and His care,
When the wants and woes are vanished,
Which He loved to soothe and share?
All the way by which He led us,
All the grievings which He bore,
All the patient love He taught us,
Shall we think of them no more?

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: We shall read the tender meaning
As we trod the desert, leaning
And His rest will be the dearer
When we think of weary ways,
And His light will shine the clearer
As we muse on cloudy days.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: To a dark and stormy day
When we smile upon our sorrow,
And the storms have passed away.

title: What was it, O our God
author: Anne Taylor Gilbert

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: What was it, O our God,
Led Thee to give Thy Son,
To give Thy well-beloved for us.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: What led the Son of God
To leave His throne on high,
Led Him to die and suffer thus.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Moved Thee to give Thy Spirit thus.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: What love to Thee we owe,
Our God, for all Thy grace,
Help us, O Lord, to praise Thee thus
For all Thy boundless love to us.

title: What will it be to dwell above
author: Joseph Swain

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: What will it be to dwell above,
And with the Lord of glory reign?
Since the blest knowledge of His love
So brightens all this dreary plain;
No heart can think, no tongue can tell
What joy 'twill be with Christ to dwell.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: When sin no more obstructs the sight,
And flesh and sense deceive no more,
When we shall see the prince of light,
And all His works of grace explore;
What heights and depths of love divine
Will there through endless ages shine!

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: And God has fixed the happy day
When the last tear shall dim our eyes,
When He will wipe these tears away
And fill our hearts with glad surprise
To hear His voice, and see His face,
And know the fullness of His grace.

title: When this passing world is done;
author: Robert Murray McCheyne (1837)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: When this passing world is done;
When has sunk yon glaring sun;
When I stand with Christ on high
Then, Lord, shall I fully know,
Not till then, how much I owe.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: When I stand before the throne
Dressed in beauty not my own;
When I see Thee as Thou art,
Then, Lord, shall I fully know,
Not till then, how much I owe.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: When the praise of heaven I hear
Loud as thunders to the ear,
Then, Lord, shall I fully know,
Not till then, how much I owe.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Chosen, not for good in me;
Wakened up from wrath to flee;
Teach me, Lord, on earth to show
By my love, how much I owe.

title: God is love! His word has said it;
author: Thomas Kelly

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: God is love! His word has said it;
This is news of heavenly birth:
Speed abroad and widely spread it,
Make it known through all the earth

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Where the Lord, with glory crowned,
Will the brightest proof be found

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: All His love, how vast it is;
Earth's the favoured spot He chooses
To display the truth of this,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: But, in heaven, of highest wonder,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: His a throne, the throne of heaven,
Yet He comes on earth to bleed,
And for man His life is given;

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Not for those who ever loved Him
Did the Lord of glory die;
Pity to the wretched moved Him:
Who that hears it will deny

stanzas.label: Verse 7
lines: 'Tis a truth: away and spread it;
Spread the tidings far and near;
O may sinners give it credit,
And be joyful when they hear

title: Farewell, for the present, farewell
author: Charles Russell Hurditch

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: At most for a few fleeting years;
For soon with our God we shall dwell.
And know neither sorrow nor tears.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: May you run in the heavenly race
Till we meet in the glory above.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: No parting shall ever be known
On that happy and heavenly shore;
Those seated with Christ on His throne
Go out from His presence no more.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: The joys of that morn, who can tell?
When Jesus our Lord will appear.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Soon Jesus our Lord will appear.

title: Praise God, from whom all blessings flow;
author: Thomas (Bishop) Ken

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Praise God, from whom all blessings flow;
Praise Him, all creatures here below;
Praise Him above, ye heavenly host:
Praise Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,

title: Glory, honour, praise, and power
author: Theodulph of Orleans? or Isaac Watts?

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Be unto the Lamb for ever;

title: All hail the power of Jesus' name!
author: Edward Perronet & John Rippon (1779)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: All hail the power of Jesus' name!
And crown Him Lord of all!

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Crown Him ye martyrs of your God
Extol the stem of Jesse's rod
And crown Him Lord of all!

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Ye seed of Israel's chosen race,
Hail Him who saves you by His grace,
And crown Him Lord of all!

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Sinners, whose love can ne'er forget
Go, spread your trophies at His feet,
And crown Him Lord of all!

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: And crown Him Lord of all!

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: O that, with yonder sacred throng,
We at His feet may fall;
And crown Him Lord of all!

title: Abide in me, my Saviour
author: E. Costello

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: And let me in Thee live;
My soul, my life I give:
Without Thy grace to keep me
I know my steps will slide,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I long, my Lord and Master,
To love and serve Thee more,
To live more near to Thee, Lord.
To keep more sure and steadfast

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Then let my life and labours
And seeking that in all things

title: Amidst us our Beloved stands
author: Charles Haddon Spurgeon (1866)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: And bids us view His pierced hands,
Points to His wounded feet and side,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: What food luxurious loads the board
When at His table sits the Lord!
The wine how rich, the bread how sweet,
When Jesus deigns the guests to meet.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: If now, with eyes defiled and dim,
We see the signs, but see not Him,
O may His love the scales displace
And bid us see Him face to face.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Thou glorious Bridegroom of our hearts,
Thy present smile a heaven imparts;
O lift the veil, if veil there be,
Let every saint Thy beauties see.

title: All the way my Saviour leads me;
author: Frances (Fanny) Jane Crosby (1875)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: All the way my Saviour leads me;
What have I to ask beside?
Can I doubt His tender mercy
Who through life has been my guide?
Here by faith in Him to dwell;
For I know, whate'er befall me,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: All the way my Saviour leads me;
Cheers each winding path I tread;
Gives me grace for every trial,
Feeds me with the living bread:
Though my weary steps may falter,
And my soul athirst may be,
Gushing from the rock before me,
Lo! a spring of joy I see.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: All the way my Saviour, leads me;
O the fullness of His love!
Perfect rest to me is promised
Wings its flight to realms of day,
This my song through endless ages,
Jesus led me all the way.

title: And can it be that I should gain
author: Charles Wesley (1738)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: And can it be that I should gain
An interest in the Saviour's blood?
Died He for me who caused His pain?
For me who Him to death pursued?
Amazing love! How can it be
That Thou, my God, shouldst die for me?

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Who can explore His strange design?
In vain the first-born seraph tries
To sound the depths of love divine;
Let angel minds inquire no more.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: He left His Father's throne above,
So free, so infinite His grace;
Emptied Himself of all but love,
And bled for Adam's helpless race;
For, O my God, it found out me.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Fast bound in sin and nature's night;
Thine eye diffused a quickening ray—
I woke, the dungeon flamed with light;
My chains fell off, my heart was free,
I rose, went forth, and followed Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Jesus, and all in Him, is mine,
Alive in Him, my living Head,
Bold I approach the eternal throne,
And claim the crown, through Christ, my own.

title: And is it so! we shall be like Thy Son
author: John Nelson Darby (1872)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: And is it so! we shall be like Thy Son,
Is this the grace which He for us has won?
Father of glory! thought beyond all thought
In glory to His own blest likeness brought.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: O Jesus, Lord, who loved us like to Thee?
Fruit of Thy work, with Thee, too, there to see
Thy glory, Lord, while endless ages roll;
Thy saints the prize and travail of Thy soul.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Yet it must be, Thy love had not its rest
Were Thy redeemed not with Thee fully blest;
That love that gives not as the world, but shares
All it possesses with its loved co-heirs.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Not we alone, Thy loved ones all, complete,
In glory round Thee there with joy shall meet,
All like Thee, for Thy glory like Thee, Lord,
Object supreme of all, by all adored.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: The heart is satisfied, can ask no more;
All thought of self is now for ever o'er;
Christ, its unmingled object, fills the heart
In blest adoring love—its endless part.

title: Assembled, Lord, at Thy behest
author: David J. Beattie

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: We wait Thy voice to hear;
O come and bless this hallowed feast—

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Draw near, yea, linger in our midst;
With thoughts of Thine unfailing love;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: That Thou, blest Lamb of God,
Should'st bear sin's curse, and interpose

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: With hearts adoring thus we view
Love's sweet memorial feast to Thee,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: O help us, Lord, while gathered here,
That we none else may see;
Keep Thou our thoughts graced with Thy love,

title: Awake, and sing the song
author: William Hammond (1745)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Wake every heart and every tongue

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: For those whose sins He bore.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Soon shall we hear Him say,
Soon will He call us hence away,
And take us to His home.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: And sweeter voices tune the song

title: Blest be the everlasting God
author: Isaac Watts & William Cameron

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: When from the dead He raised His Son,
And called Him to the sky,
He gave our souls a lively hope

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: He taught our hearts to rise;

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Saints by the power of God are kept
We walk by faith as strangers here,
But Christ shall call us home.

title: Blest morning, whose first dawning rays
author: Isaac Watts 1709

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Blest morning, whose first dawning rays

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Wrapt in the silence of the tomb
Till the revolving skies had brought

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Hell and the grave combined their force
To hold our Lord, in vain;

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: To Thy great name, almighty Lord,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Let heaven and earth, and rocks and seas,

title: Break every barrier down
author: Bertha Mullen

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Show me the awfullness of sin,
Purge Thou my soul from dross,
Wash me in Thine atoning blood,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Till Christ be formed in me;
Till of the travail of Thy soul
May self be lost to sight,
Reproach for Thee be counted joy

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Take Thou possession of my heart,
I crown Thee now as Lord!

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: May every breathing of my heart
To walk with Thee, as Enoch walked,

title: By Christ redeemed, in Christ restored
author: George Rawson (1857)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: By Christ redeemed, in Christ restored,
And show the death of our dear Lord

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: His body, broken in our stead,
Is seen in this memorial bread,
And so our feeble love is fed

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: The drops of His dread agony,
His life-blood shed for us, we see;
The wine shall tell the mystery

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Until the trump of God be heard,
Until the ancient graves be stirred,
And with the great commanding word

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: O blessed hope! With this elate,
Let not our hearts be desolate,
But, strong in faith, in patience wait

title: Break Thou the bread of life
author: Mary Artemisia Lathbury & Alexander Groves (1877)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Break Thou the bread of life,
As Thou didst break the loaves

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Break Thou the bread of life,
And let my steps be all

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Bless Thou the truth, dear Lord,
As Thou didst bless the bread
And I shall find my peace,

title: Come, my soul, thy suit prepare;
author: John Newton (1779)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Come, my soul, thy suit prepare;
He Himself has bid thee pray,
Therefore will not say thee nay.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thou art coming to a King;
For His grace and power are such,
None can ever ask too much.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Lord, I come to Thee for rest;

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: As the image in the glass

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: While I am a pilgrim here
Let Thy love my spirit cheer;
As my guide, my guard, my friend,
Lead me to my journey's end.

title: Come, every joyful heart
author: Samuel Stennett

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Tell all above and all below
The debt of love to Him you owe.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: On wings of love came down,
And wept, and bled, and died:
What He endured no tongue can tell,
To save our souls from death and hell.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: From the dark grave He rose—
Up through the sky the Conqueror rode,
And reigns on high, the Saviour God.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: There shall we see His lovely face,
And ever be in His embrace.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: The debt of love we owe;
Yet grant us day by day
Our life, our all, to Thee we give,
To Thee, by whom alone we live.

title: Crown Him with many crowns
author: Matthew Bridges & Godfrey Thring (1852)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Hark! How the heavenly anthem drowns
Of Him who died for thee,
And hail Him as thy matchless King

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Crown Him the Lord of love;
For Thou hast died for me:
Thy praise shall never, never fail

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Crown Him the Lord of life
And rose victorious in the strife
For those He came to save:
Who died and rose on high,
Who died eternal life to bring,
And lives that death may die.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Crown Him the Lord of heaven,
The King of kings to whom is given
His reign shall know no end,

title: Dear Lord and Father of mankind
author: John Greenleaf Whittier (1872)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Dear Lord and Father of mankind,
Reclothe us in our rightful mind;
In purer lives Thy service find,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: In simple trust like theirs who heard,
The gracious calling of the Lord,
Let us, like them, without a word

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Where Jesus knelt to share with Thee

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: With that deep hush subduing all
Our words and works that drown
The tender whisper of Thy call,
As noiseless let Thy blessing fall

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Drop Thy still dews of quietness
Take from our souls the strain and stress,
And let our ordered lives confess

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Breathe through the heats of our desire
Let sense be dumb, let flesh retire;
Speak through the earthquake, wind and fire,
O still small voice of calm!

title: Eternal Light! eternal Light!
author: Thomas Binney (c.18)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: How pure the soul must be
When, placed within Thy searching sight,
It shrinks not, but with calm delight
Can live, and look on Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The spirits that surround Thy throne
But that is surely theirs alone,
Since they have never, never known

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O how shall I, whose native sphere
Is dark, whose mind is dim,
And on my naked spirit bear

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: There is a way for man to rise

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: These, these prepare us for the sight
The sons of ignorance and night
May dwell in the eternal Light,

title: Far, far away, in heathen darkness dwelling
author: James McGranahan (1886)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Far, far away, in heathen darkness dwelling,
Millions of souls for ever may be lost;
Who, who will go? salvation's story telling,
Looking to Jesus, counting not the cost.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: See o'er the world wide open doors inviting:
Soldiers of Christ, arise and enter in;
Christians, awake! your forces all uniting,
Send forth the gospel, break the chains of sin.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Why will ye die? the voice of God is calling,
Why will ye die? re-echo in His name;
Jesus hath died to save from death appalling;
Life and salvation therefore go, proclaim.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: God speed the day when those of every nation
Glory to God triumphantly shall sing;
Shout Hallelujah, for the Lord is King!

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: All power is given unto Me;
All power is given unto Me;
Go ye into all the world and preach the gospel;
And lo, I am with you alway.

title: Father of peace, and God of love
author: Philip Doddridge & William Cameron(?) (1751)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Father of peace, and God of love,
We own Thy power to save,
That power by which our Shepherd rose

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Him from the dead Thou brought'st again,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O may Thy Spirit fill our souls,
And mould them to Thy will,
That our weak hearts no more may stray,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: And all we think, and all we do,

title: Fight the good fight with all thy might;
author: John Samuel Bewley Monsell (1863)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Fight the good fight with all thy might;
Christ is thy strength, and Christ thy right;
Lay hold on life, and it shall be

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Run the straight race through God's good grace,
Lift up thine eyes, and seek His face;
Life with its way before thee lies;
Christ is the path, and Christ the prize.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Cast care aside; lean on thy Guide,
Lean, and the trusting soul shall prove
Christ is its life, and Christ its love.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Faint not, nor fear; His arm is near;
He changeth not, and thou art dear;
Only believe, and thou shalt see
That Christ is all in all to thee.

title: From Greenland's icy mountains
author: Reginald Heber (1819)

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The gifts of God are strewn;
Bows down to wood and stone.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Can we, whose souls are lighted

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Waft, waft, ye winds, His story,
Till, like a sea of glory,
It spreads from pole to pole;

title: Gathered, Lord, around Thy table
author: Douglas Russell

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Let us know Thy presence with us,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Love divine first drew us to Thee
For our sin, in deep compassion,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thou hast snapt the chains that bound us:

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Drink we too the cup of blessing
Through Thy blood we have redemption:

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Backward look we, drawn to Calvary,
Forward haste we to Thy coming,

title: Gathered to Thy name, Lord Jesus
author: C. A. Wellesley

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Gathered to Thy name, Lord Jesus,
Losing sight of all but Thee,
O what joy Thy presence gives us,
Calling up our hearts to Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Loved with love which knows no measure
Save the Father's love to Thee,
Blessed Lord, our hearts would treasure
All the Father's thoughts of Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: All His joy, His rest, His pleasure,
All His deep delight in Thee;
Lord, Thy heart alone can measure
What Thy Father found in Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: How He set His love upon Thee,
Yet for us He did not spare Thee,
By Thy death our life was won.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: O the joy, the wondrous singing
When we see Thee as Thou art;
Thy blest name, Lord Jesus, bringing

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Through God's endless day of days.

title: Gazing on Thee, Lord, in glory
author: Centra Thompson

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Gazing on Thee, Lord, in glory,
While our hearts in worship bow,
There we read the wondrous story
Of the cross, its shame and woe.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: All the depths of Thy heart's sorrow

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Where no pitying eye was found;
Now to God's right hand exalted,
With Thy praise the heavens resound.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Did Thy God e'en then forsake Thee,
Hide His face from Thy deep need?
In Thy face, once marred and smitten,
All His glory now we read.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Gazing on it we adore Thee,
Thou, the Lamb, art ever worthy;
This be earth's and heaven's accord.

title: Glory to Thee; Thou Son of God most High
author: Edward C. Quine

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Glory to Thee; Thou Son of God most High,
Glory to Thee, enthroned above the sky,
High on Thy throne, Thine ear, Lord Jesus, bend
As grateful hearts now to Thyself ascend.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Deep were Thy sorrows, Lord, when heaven frowned—
Bloodlike Thy sweat, Lord falling to the ground
Dark was the night, but heaven was darker still,
O Christ my God!—is this the Father's will?

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thorns wreathed Thy brow when hanging on the tree,
Why lavish love like this, O Lord, on me!
Would that my soul could understand its length,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Thy precious blood was freely shed for me
To save me from a lost eternity;
Nor death, nor hell, nor things below—above
Can sever me from Thy eternal love.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Like shoreless seas, Thy love can know no bound;
And when above, my crown is at Thy feet,
I'll praise Thee still for Calvary's

title: Go, labour on; spend, and be spent;
author: Horatius Bonar (1843)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Go, labour on; spend, and be spent;
Thy joy to do the Father's will;
It is the way the Master went,
Should not the servant tread it still?

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Go, labour on, 'tis not for naught;
Thy earthly loss is heavenly gain;
Men heed thee, love thee, praise thee, not;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Go, labour on while it is day,
The world's dark night is hastening on;
Speed, speed thy work, cast sloth away,
It is not thus that souls are won.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Toil on, faint not, keep watch and pray;
Be wise the erring soul to win;
Go forth into the world's highway,
Compel the wanderer to come in.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Toil on, and in thy toil rejoice;
For toil comes rest, for exile, home;
Soon shalt thou hear the Bridegroom's voice,
The midnight cry, Behold, I come!

title: Gracious God, we worship Thee
author: Samuel Trevor Francis

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Vast Thy love, how deep, how wide,
In the gift of Him who died;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Low we bow before Thy face,
Sons of God, O wondrous place!
Great the riches of Thy grace;

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: By Thy Spirit grant that we
Praise, as incense sweet to Thee;

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Yet again our song we raise,
Now, and soon through endless days;

title: Hail to the Lord's Anointed
author: James Montgomery (1821)

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: He shall come down like showers
And love, joy, hope, like flowers,
Spring in His path to birth;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Kings shall fall down before Him,
Or dove's light wing can soar,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: He on His throne shall rest;
From age to age more glorious,
The tide of time shall never
His name shall stand for ever;

title: He dies! He dies! The lowly Man of sorrows
author: Charles Russell Hurditch

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: He dies! He dies! The lowly Man of sorrows,
On whom were laid our many griefs and woes;
Our sins He bore beneath God's awful billows,
And He hath triumphed over all our foes.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: He lives! He lives! What glorious consolation!
Exalted at His Father's own right hand;
He pleads for us, and, by His intercession,
Enables all His saints by grace to stand.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: He comes! He comes! O blest anticipation!
In keeping with His true and faithful word;
To call us to our heavenly consummation—
Caught up, to be for ever with the Lord.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: I am He that liveth, that liveth, and was dead;
And behold, . . I am alive . . for evermore, . .
Behold, . . I am alive . . for evermore . . .
I am He that liveth, that liveth. And was dead;
And behold, . . I am alive . . for evermore.

title: He giveth more grace when the burdens grow greater
author: Annie Johnson Flint

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: He giveth more grace when the burdens grow greater,
He sendeth more strength when the labours increase,
To added affliction He addeth His mercy,
To multiplied trials His multiplied peace.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: When we have exhausted our store of endurance,
When strength has declined ere the day is half-done,
When we reach the end of our hoarded resources,
Our Father's full giving is only begun.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: (or chorus) His love has no limit, His grace has no measure,
His power no boundary known unto men,
For out of His infinite riches in Jesus
He giveth and giveth and giveth again.

title: Holy, holy, holy! Lord God Almighty!
author: Reginald Heber (1826)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Holy, holy, holy! Lord God Almighty!
Early in the morning our song shall rise to Thee;
Holy, holy, holy! Merciful and mighty,
God in Three Persons, blessed Trinity!

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Holy, holy, holy! Though the darkness hide Thee,
Though the eye of sinful man Thy glory may not see;
Only Thou art holy, there is none beside Thee,
Perfect in power, in love, and purity.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Holy, holy, holy! Lord God Almighty!
All Thy works shall praise Thy name in earth, and sky and sea;
Holy, holy, holy! Merciful and mighty,
God in Three Persons, blessed Trinity!

title: How I praise Thee, precious Saviour!
author: Mary E. Maxwell

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: How I praise Thee, precious Saviour!
That Thy love laid hold of me;
Thou has saved and cleansed and filled me,
That I might Thy channel be.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Just a channel, full of blessing,
To tell out Thy full salvation,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Emptied that Thou shouldest fill me,
A clean vessel in Thine hand;
With no power but as Thou givest

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Witnessing Thy power to save me,
Setting free from self and sin;
Thou hast bought me to possess me,
In Thy fullness, Lord, come in.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: But with all Thy wondrous power
Flowing through us, Thou canst use us

title: I am the Lord's! O joy beyond expression
author: Lucy Ann Bennett

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I am the Lord's! O joy beyond expression,
O sweet response to voice of love divine;
Faith's joyous Yes to the assuring Whisper,
Fear not, I have redeemed thee. thou art Mine.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I am the Lord's! it hushes every murmur,
It soothes the fevered spirit to its rest;
I am the Lord's! it is the child's rejoinder,
Who knows and feels the Father's will is best.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: I am the Lord's! O eagerly and gladly,
I am the Lord's it is the rock unfailing
To which our storm-tossed souls in danger cling.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: I am the Lord's! yet teach me all it meaneth,
All it involves of love and loyalty,
Of holy service, full and glad surrender,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: I am the Lord's! yes; body, soul and spirit;
As Thou, Beloved, in Thy grace and fullness
For ever and for evermore art mine.

title: In heavenly love abiding
author: Anna Laetitia Waring & E. Cronin(?) (1850)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: No change my heart shall fear;
The storm may roar without me,
My heart may low be laid,
But God is round about me,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: No want shall turn me back;
He knows the way He taketh,
And I will walk with Him.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Which yet I have not seen;
Bright skies will soon be o'er me
Where dark the clouds have been:
My path to life is free;
And He will walk with me.

title: Immortal, invisible, God only wise
author: Walter Chalmers Smith (1876)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: In light inaccessible hid from our eyes,
Most blessed, most glorious, the Ancient of Days,
Almighty, victorious, Thy great name we praise.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Unresting, unhasting, and silent as light,
Nor wanting, nor wasting, Thou rulest in might;
Thy justice like mountains high soaring above
Thy clouds which are fountains of goodness and love.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: To all, life Thou givest—to both great and small;
In all life Thou livest, the true life of all;
We blossom and flourish as leaves on the tree,
And wither and perish—but nought changeth Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Great Father of glory, pure Father of light,
Thine angels adore Thee, all veiling their sight;
All laud we would render: O help us to see
'Tis only the splendour of light hideth Thee.

title: In the name of Jesus every knee shall bow
author: Caroline Maria Noel (1870)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: In the name of Jesus every knee shall bow
Every tongue confess Him King of glory now;
'Tis the Father's pleasure we should call Him Lord,
Who from the beginning was the mighty Word.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Humbled for a season to receive a name
From the lips of sinners unto whom He came;
Faithfully He bore it spotless to the last,
Brought it back victorious when from death He passed:

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Bore it up triumphant with its human light,
Through all ranks of creatures to the central height;
To the throne of Godhead, to the Father's breast,
Filled it with the glory of that perfect rest.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: In your hearts enthrone Him; there let Him subdue
All that is not holy, all that is not true;
Crown Him as your Captain in temptation's hour;
Let His will enfold you in its light and power.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Brethren, this Lord Jesus shall return again,
With His Father's glory, with His angel train;
For all wreaths of empire meet upon His brow,
And our hearts confess Him King of glory now.

title: Jesus calls us! o'er the tumult
author: Cecil Frances (Humphreys) Alexander (1852)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus calls us! o'er the tumult
Of our life's wild restless sea
Day by day His sweet voice soundeth,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: As, of old, apostles heard it
Turned from home and toil and kindred,
Leaving all for His dear sake.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Jesus calls us from the worship
Of the vain world's golden store,
From each idol that would keep us;

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: In our joys and in our sorrows,
Days of toil and hours of ease,
Still He calls, in cares and pleasures,
Christian, love Me more than these.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Jesus calls us! By Thy mercies,
Saviour, may we hear Thy call,
Give our hearts to Thy obedience,
Serve and love Thee best of all.

title: Jesus, Lord, I need Thy presence
author: George Goodman

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus, Lord, I need Thy presence
As I journey on my way,
For without Thee I am lonely,
And my feet are apt to stray;
But if Thou wilt walk with me
Life will calm and holy be.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Jesus, Lord, I need Thy wisdom,
And without Thee I am foolish,
Nor can bear the strain and stress;
But if Thou wilt counsel me
I shall true and upright be.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Jesus, Lord, I need Thy power,
And without Thee I am helpless,
With no strength to meet the foe;
But if Thou wilt strengthen me

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Jesus, Lord, I need Thy guidance,
Fire by night, and cloud by day,
For without Them I am sightless,
But if Thou dost lead me on

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Jesus, Lord, Thy love so tender
Is my greatest need of all,
For without Thee pride and anger
But if Thou Thy love impart
I shall have a gracious heart.

title: Jesus, I am resting, resting
author: Jean Sophia Pigott (1876)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: In the joy of what Thou art;
I am finding out the greatness
Thou hast bid me gaze upon Thee,
And Thy beauty fills my soul,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Yes, I rest in Thee, Beloved,
Know what wealth of grace is Thine,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: I behold Thee as Thou art,
And Thy love, so pure, so changeless,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Ever lift Thy face upon me
As I work and wait for Thee,

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: In the joy of what Thou art;
I am finding out the greatness

title: Jesus, Lord, we come together
author: Thomas Henry Reynolds

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: In the bonds of Thine own love;
Thou hast drawn our footsteps hither
Its deep meaning now to prove.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: In Thy presence break the bread;
Never more can grief befall Thee,
Thou art risen from the dead.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: But Thy love remains, that entered
Into death to make us Thine;
In that death all love was centred;
Thankful now we drink the wine.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Here by grace we taste the blessing,
Soon to fill a world of bliss;
And we bless Thy name confessing
Thine own love our portion is.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Sweet it is to sit before Thee,
Sweet to hear Thy blessed voice,
Sweet to worship and adore Thee,
For our hearts in Thee rejoice.

title: Jesus, our Lord, with what joy we adore Thee
author: Henry d'Arcy Champney

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus, our Lord, with what joy we adore Thee,
Chanting our praise to Thyself on the throne,
Blest in Thy presence, we worship before Thee,
Own Thou art worthy, and worthy alone.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Verily God, yet become truly human—
Lower than angels—to die in our stead;
How hast Thou, long promised Seed of the woman,
Trod on the serpent and bruised his head!

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: How didst Thou humble Thyself to be taken,
Led by Thy creatures, and nailed to the cross?
Hated of men, and of God, too, forsaken,
Shunning not darkness, the curse, and the loss.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: How hast Thou triumphed, and triumphed with glory,
Battled death's forces, rolled back every wave!
Can we refrain, then, from telling the story,
How Thou art victor o'er death and the grave?

title: Jesus shall reign where'er the sun
author: Isaac Watts (1719)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus shall reign where'er the sun
His kingdom stretch from shore to shore
Till moons shall wax and wane no more.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: For Him shall endless prayer be made,
And praises throng to crown His head;
His name like sweet perfume shall rise

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: People and realms of every tongue
Dwell on His love with sweetest song;
Their early blessings on His name.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: The prisoner leaps to lose his chains,
And all the sons of want are blest.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Let every creature rise and bring
And earth repeat the loud Amen.

title: Jesus, Thou joy of loving hearts
author: Bernard of Clairvaux tr/ad by Ray Palmer (12 c)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus, Thou joy of loving hearts,
Thou fount of life, Thou light of men,
From the best bliss that earth imparts
We turn unfilled to Thee again.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thy truth unchanged hath ever stood;
Thou savest those that on Thee call;
To them that seek Thee Thou art good;
To them that find Thee, all in all.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: We taste Thee, O Thou living bread!
And long to feast upon Thee still;
We drink of Thee, the fountain-head,
And thirst our souls from Thee to fill.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Our restless spirits yearn for Thee,
Where'er our changeful lot is cast:
Glad, when Thy gracious smile we see;
Blest, when our faith can hold Thee fast.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: O Jesus ever with us stay,
Make all our moments calm and bright;
Chase the dark night of sin away;
Shed o'er the world Thy holy light.

title: Just as I am, Thine own to be
author: Marianne "Farningham" Hearn (1887)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Just as I am, Thine own to be,
Friend of the young, who lovest me,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: In the glad morning of my day,
My life to give, my vows to pay,
With no reserve and no delay,
With all my heart, I come.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Just as I am, young, strong and free,
To be the best that I can be
For truth, and righteousness, and Thee,
Lord of my life, I come.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: And for Thy sake to win renown,
And then to take the victor's crown
And at Thy feet to lay it down,

title: Let the song go round the earth
author: Sarah Geraldina Stock (1898)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Let the song go round the earth,
Sound His praises, tell His worth,
Join the grand, the glorious song.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Let the song go round the earth
Where the daylight has its birth,
Waft them on to India's plains.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Let the song go round the earth;
Darkly broods o'er home and hearth,
Let His praise from Afric's shore
Rise and swell her wide lands o'er.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Let the song go round the earth
Let the notes of holy mirth
Snowbound coasts give back the hymn.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Let the song go round the earth,
With the story of His worth

title: Like a river, glorious
author: Frances Ridley Havergal (©1876)

title: Lo, He comes! With clouds descending
author: John Cennick tr/ad by Charles Wesley & Martin Madan (1752)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lo, He comes! With clouds descending,
Swell the triumph of His train;
Jesus comes, and comes to reign!

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Every eye shall now behold Him
Those who set at naught and sold Him,
Pierced and nailed Him to the tree,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Lo, the tokens of His passion
Now the day of Christ appears.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Yea, Amen! Let all adore Thee,
Saviour, take the power and glory,
Share the kingdom with Thine own;

title: Lord, e'en to death Thy love could go
author: H. L. Rossier tr/ad by C. A. Wellesley

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lord, e'en to death Thy love could go,
A death of shame and loss,
To vanquish for us every foe,
And break the strong man's force.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: O what a load was Thine to bear,
Our sins in all their terror there,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: The storm that bowed Thy blessed head
And rest divine is ours instead,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Within the Father's house on high
We soon shall sing Thy praise;
But here, where Thou didst bleed and die,
We learn that song to raise.

title: Lord, speak to me, that I may speak
author: Frances Ridley Havergal (1872)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lord, speak to me, that I may speak
In living echoes of Thy tone;
As Thou hast sought, so let me seek
Thy erring children lost and lone.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: O lead me, Lord, that I may lead
The wand'ring and the wav'ring feet;
O feed me, Lord, that I may feed
Thy hung'ring ones with manna sweet.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O teach me, Lord, that I may teach
The precious things Thou dost impart;
And wing my words, that they may reach
The hidden depths of many a heart.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O fill me with Thy fullness, Lord,
In kindling thought and glowing word,
Thy love to tell, Thy praise to show.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: O use me, Lord, use even me,
Just as Thou wilt, and when, and where,
Until Thy blessed face I see;
Thy rest, Thy joy, Thy glory share.

title: Look upon us, blessed Lord
author: >Tobias Clausnitzer tr/ad by Robert Alexander Stewart MacAlister (1663)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Take our wandering thoughts and guide us;
We have come to hear Thy word,
With Thy teaching now provide us,
We Thy message may be learning.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: If Thou shouldst withhold the light,
In the dark our souls were groping;
In word, deed, and thought direct us;
Thou, none other, canst correct us.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Light of light, from God proceeding,
Make us ready in this place;
Ear and heart await Thy leading:
In our study, prayers and praising,
May our souls find their upraising.

title: Lord, Thy word abideth
author: Henry Williams Baker (1861)

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: When our foes are near us,
Then Thy word doth cheer us,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: When the storms are o'er us,

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Lord, may love and fear Thee,

title: Love divine, all loves excelling
author: Charles Wesley (1747)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Joy of heaven, to earth come down;

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Let us all Thy grace receive,
Follow in Thy steps, and never,
Then our hearts will yield their blessing,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Till in heaven we take our place,
Then to worship and adore Thee,
Lost in wonder, love and praise.

title: Majestic sweetness sits enthroned.
author: Samuel Stennett (1787)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: His head with radiant glories crowned,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: No mortal can with Him compare
Fairer is He than all the fair

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: He saw me plunged in deep distress,
For me He bore the shameful cross,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: To Him I owe my life and breath,
And all the joys I have;
He makes me triumph over death,
He saves me from the grave.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Since from His bounty I receive
Had I a thousand hearts to give,
Lord, they should all be Thine!

title: Master, speak! Thy servant heareth
author: Frances Ridley Havergal (1869)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Longing for Thy voice that cheereth,
Master, let it now be heard:
I am listening, Lord, for Thee;
What hast Thou to say to me?

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Master, speak! though least and lowest,
Master, speak! for O Thou knowest
All the yearning of my heart:
Speak! And make me blest indeed.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Master, speak! and make me ready
When Thy voice is truly heard,
I am listening, Lord, for Thee:
Master, speak, O speak to me!

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Speak to me by name, O Master!
Let me know it is to me;
Speak! That I may follow faster
With a step more firm and free,
Where the Shepherd leads the flock
In the shadow of the rock.

title: May the mind of Christ my Saviour
author: Kate Barclay Wilkinson

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: May the mind of Christ my Saviour
Live in me from day to day,
By His love and power controlling

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: May the word of God dwell richly
In my heart from hour to hour
So that all may see I triumph

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: May the peace of God my Father
That I may be calm to comfort

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: May the love of Jesus fill me
As the waters fill the sea;

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: May I run the race before me,
Strong and brave to face the foe,

title: Mine eyes are unto Thee, my God
author: Frances (Fanny) Jane Crosby

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Mine eyes are unto Thee, my God
My soul on Thee doth wait,
My hope is in Thy faithful word,
And in Thy love so great.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thy promise true my faith receives
And claims it for its own;
My trusting heart with joy believes

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: What if Thy love impose a task
Too hard for me to scan?
I will not question it, nor ask

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O Lord, I only ask for grace
To work it out with Thee;
And as in faith each step I take

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Its rich unfoldings on my soul
Till glory, bright and endless, dawns

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Till then. O keep me safely, Lord,
Till that blest, happy moment come,
When, Lord, Thy face I'll see.

title: More about Jesus would I know
author: Eliza Edmunds Hewitt (1887)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: More about Jesus would I know,
More of His grace to others show;
More of His saving fullness see,
More of His love who died for me.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: More about Jesus let me learn,
More of His holy will discern:
Spirit of God, my teacher be,
Showing the things of Christ to me.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: More about Jesus; in His word
Hearing His voice in every line,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: More about Jesus; on His throne,
Riches in glory all His own;
More of His kingdom's sure increase;
More of His coming—Prince of Peace.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: More of His saving fullness see,
More of His love who died for me.

title: My glorious Victor, Prince divine
author: Handley Carr Glyn Moule

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Clasp these surrendered hands in Thine;
At length my will is all Thine own,
Glad vassal of a Saviour's throne.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: My Master, lead me to Thy door;
Pierce this now willing ear once more:
Thy bonds are freedom; let me stay
With Thee to toil, endure, obey.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Yes, ear and hand, and thought and will,
Use all in Thy dear slavery still;
Beneath Thy feet; there keep them fast.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Tread them still down; and then I know
These hands shall with Thy gifts o'erflow;
And pierced ears shall hear the tone
Which tells me Thou and I are one.

title: My heart is full of Christ, and longs
author: Charles Wesley (1743)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: My heart is full of Christ, and longs
Of Him I make my loftier songs,
And cannot from His praise forbear;
My ready tongue makes haste to sing
The glories of my heavenly King.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Fairer than all the earth-born race,
Replenished are Thy lips with grace,
And full of love Thy tender heart;
God ever blest! We bow the knee,
And own all fullness dwells in Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Gird on Thy thigh the Spirit's sword,
And take to Thee Thy power divine;
Stir up Thy strength, almighty Lord,
All power and majesty are Thine:

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Come, and maintain Thy righteous cause
And let Thy glorious toil succeed;
Extend the victory of Thy cross,
Ride on, and prosper in Thy deed;
And reign in every heart alone.

title: No gospel like this feast
author: Elizabeth Rundle Charles

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Spread for us, Lord, by Thee;
Preach the glad news more free.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: All it has won for us, the lost,
All it cost Thee, the Son.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Ours is the free gift given;
Thine was the blood of sacrifice,
Ours is the wine of heaven.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: That darkest and that brightest day

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: From that dark depth of woes
Thy love for us has trod,
We soar to heights of blest repose

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Still at the cross, while at this feast,

title: O God of Bethel! By whose hand
author: Philip Doddridge & John Logan & others (1737)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O God of Bethel! By whose hand

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Our vows, our prayers, we now present
God of our fathers! Be the God

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Through each perplexing path of life
Give us each day our daily bread.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O spread Thy covering wings around
And at our Father's loved abode

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Such blessings from Thy gracious hand
And Thou shalt be our chosen God,

title: O Christ, Thou Son of God!
author: William Bennett

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Christ, Thou Son of God!
Thou living One who once wast slain
To Thee, O Lord, we look,
Be Thou throughout our earthly course

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: No change Thou e'er shalt know;
The same art Thou upon the throne
The same e'en to eternal days

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Help us, however dark our path,
To stay our souls on Thee:
Help us to cleave unto Thy name,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: To wait for that blest hour when Thou
When we Thy voice shall hear,
And, like Thee, in Thy presence stand,

title: O Jesus Christ, grow Thou in me
author: Johann Caspar Lavater tr/ad by Elizabeth Lee Allen Smith (1780)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Jesus Christ, grow Thou in me,
My heart be daily nearer Thee,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Each day let Thy supporting might
My darkness vanish in Thy light,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: In Thy bright beams which on me fall,
That I am nothing, Thou art all,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: More of Thy glory let me see,
I would Thy living image be,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Fill me with gladness from above,
Lord, let the glow of Thy great love

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Make this poor self grow less and less,
Be Thou my life and aim;
O make me daily, through Thy grace,
More meet to bear Thy name.

title: O Jesus, I have promised
author: John Ernest Bode (1868)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: To serve Thee to the end,
I shall not fear the battle
If Thou art by my side,
If Thou wilt be my guide.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: O let me feel Thee near me;
I see the sights that dazzle,
My foes are ever near me,
And shield my soul from sin

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O let me hear Thee speaking,
O speak, and make me listen,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O let me see Thy footmarks,
And in them plant mine own;
O guide me, call me, draw me,
And then in heaven receive me,

title: O Lord of heaven and earth and sea
author: Christopher Wordsworth (1863)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Lord of heaven and earth and sea,
To Thee all praise and glory be:
How shall we show our love to Thee

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: For health and home and lengthened days,
For all the blessings earth displays,
Our God, we owe Thee thanks and praise,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thou didst not spare Thine only Son,
But gav'st Him for a world undone,
And freely with that blessed One

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: For souls redeemed, for sins forgiven,
For present grace and hopes of heaven,
Father, what can to Thee be given,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: We lose what on ourselves we spend;
We have as treasure without end
Whatever, Lord, to Thee we lend,

title: O Lord, it is Thyself to meet
author: Boethia Thompson

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Lord, it is Thyself to meet
To this sweet feast we come;
Like Mary, resting at Thy feet
We well remember Thou hast said,
So thus we take the wine, the bread,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: O Lord, we come, not for our need,
Nor with our grief to Thee;
But on the bread and wine to feed,
Yes, to remember all Thy love,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O Lord, from Thee the bread we take,
From Thy pierced hand the wine;
We praise Thee for this quiet hour
In which we feel the Spirit's power,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
