lines: O Lord, we come, for Thou art here;
Thy faithful promise brings Thee near
O body broken! poured out blood!
Thou Son of man! Thou Lamb of God!
How good to meet Thee here!

title: O love that wilt not let me go
author: George Matheson (1882)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O love that wilt not let me go,
I rest my weary soul in Thee;
I give Thee back the life I owe,
That in Thine ocean depths its flow

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: O light that followest all my way,
I yield my flickering torch to Thee;
My heart restores its borrowed ray,
That in Thy sunshine's blaze its day

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O joy that seekest me through pain,
I cannot close my heart to Thee;
I trace the rainbow through the rain,
And feel the promise is not vain

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O cross that liftest up my head,
I dare not ask to fly from thee,
I lay in dust life's glory dead,
And from the ground there blossoms red

title: O Master! when Thou callest
author: Sarah Geraldina Stock (1888)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: No voice may say Thee nay,
For blest are they that follow
Where Thou dost lead the way:

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: No foot may shrink in fear,
For they who trust Thee wholly

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: When Thou dost deign to use
Thou who for each one carest,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: They who go forth to serve Thee,
We, too, who serve at home,
Our song of hope we raise,
Till that blest shore is sighted
Where all shall turn to praise.

title: O the bitter shame and sorrow!
author: Theodore Monod (1874)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O the bitter shame and sorrow!
That a time could ever be
When I let the Saviour's pity
Plead in vain; and proudly answered,
All of self, and none of Thee!

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Yet He found me: I beheld Him
Heard Him pray: Forgive them, Father!
And my wistful heart said faintly,
Some of self, and some of Thee!

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Day by day His tender mercy,
Sweet and strong, and ah! So patient,
Brought me lower, while I whispered,
Less of self, and more of Thee!

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Lord, Thy love at last hath conquered;
None of self, and all of Thee!

title: O The deep, deep love of Jesus!
author: Samuel Trevor Francis (1875)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O The deep, deep love of Jesus!
Is the current of Thy love,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: O the deep, deep love of Jesus!
Spread His praise from shore to shore;
How He watches o'er His loved ones,
Died to call them all His own;
Watcheth o'er them from the throne.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O the deep, deep love of Jesus!
Love of every love the best:
O such love! the love of Jesus;
'Tis a heaven of heavens to me;
And it lifts me up to glory,
For it lifts me up to Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: O the deep, deep love of Jesus!
But a drop of all this ocean
Or a grain from off its shore:
Yet our hearts are beating highly,
If our faith is sometimes dim,
For the glory and the rapture
We shall have when we have Him.

title: O Thou, my soul, bless God the Lord;
author: Author Uncertain: Thomas Sternhold or Francis Rous (Rowe) & William Barton (1650)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O Thou, my soul, bless God the Lord;
And all that in me is
Be stirrèd up His holy name

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Bless, O my soul, the Lord thy God,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Who thy diseases all and pains

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Who doth redeem thy life, that thou
To death may'st not go down;
Who thee with loving kindness doth

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: O bless the Lord, all ye His works,
My soul, bless thou the Lord!

title: O wondrous hour, when Jesus, Thou
author: Edward Denny (1839)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O wondrous hour, when Jesus, Thou,
Beneath our sin didst deign to bow,
And in our stead didst bear the rod.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: When most in Satan's awful power,
O Lord, Thy suffering spirit seemed,
Then, in that dark and fearful hour,
Our souls were by Thy blood redeemed.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: 'Tis in Thy cross, Lord, that we learn
What Thou in all Thy fullness art;
There, through the darkening cloud, discern
The love of Thy devoted heart.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: That made Thee, blessed Saviour, die;
That triumphed in Thy mighty cry.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: 'Twas all for us—our life we owe,
Our hope, our crown of joy, to Thee;
Thy sufferings in that hour of woe,
Thy victory, Lord, have made us free.

title: O worship the King all-glorious above
author: William Kethe & Robert Grant (1561)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O worship the King all-glorious above,
O gratefully sing His power and His love;
Our shield and defender, the Ancient of Days,
Pavilioned in splendour and girded with praise.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: O tell of His might, O sing of His grace,
Whose robe is the light, whose canopy space;
His chariots of wrath the deep thunderclouds form,
And dark is His path on the wings of the storm.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: The earth, with its store of wonders untold,
Almighty, Thy power hath founded of old;
Hath stablished it fast by a changeless decree,
And round it hath cast, like a mantle, the sea.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Thy bountiful care what tongue can recite?
It breathes in the air, it shines in the light;
It streams from the hills, it descends to the plain,
And sweetly distils in the dew and the rain.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Frail children of dust, and feeble as frail,
In Thee do we trust, nor find Thee to fail;
Thy mercies how tender, how firm to the end,
Our maker, defender, redeemer, and friend.

title: On that same night, Lord Jesus
author: George West Frazer

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: On that same night, Lord Jesus,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: We think of all the darkness
Of all those waves and billows
With joy and yet with sorrow

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: We know Thee now as risen,
With heart and mind set free,
We think of all Thy sorrow,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Till Thou shalt come in glory
To share with Thee the brightness
We show Thy death, Lord Jesus,
And here would seek to be

title: Our blest Redeemer, ere He breathed
author: Harriet Auber (1829)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Our blest Redeemer, ere He breathed

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: He came sweet influence to impart,
While He can find one humble heart

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: And His that gentle voice we hear,
Soft as the breath of even,
That checks each fault, that calms each fear,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: O make our hearts, Thy dwelling-place,

title: Our great Redeemer liveth! This assurance
author: Frances (Fanny) Jane Crosby

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Our great Redeemer liveth! This assurance
Calms anxious fears and satisfies the heart;
Yes, Jesus lives! at God's right hand He reigneth,
And in His great salvation we have part.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: A living Christ, so strong, so pure, so tender,
Bears every ransomed soul before the throne;
Complete in Him we stand, saved by His merit—
It was His blood which did for sin atone.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: And now we live in Him, our great Redeemer,
Who, living, intercedes for us above,
Yet by His Spirit dwells with us, and keeps us
Enfolded in His mighty arms of love.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: We bless Thy holy name that Thou has taught
Our hearts to know Thee, loving, caring, pleading:
Now grant us grace to love Thee as we ought.

title: Praise, my soul, the King of heaven;
author: Henry Francis Lyte (1834)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Praise, my soul, the King of heaven;
To His feet thy tribute bring;
Who like thee His praise shall sing?

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Praise Him for His grace and favour
Praise Him, still the same as ever,
Slow to chide and swift to bless:

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Father-like He tends and spares us,
Well our feeble frame He knows;
In His hands He gently bears us,
Rescues us from all our foes:

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Frail as summer flower we flourish;
Blows the wind and it is gone;
But, while mortals rise and perish,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Angels, help us to adore Him,
Ye behold Him face to face;
Sun and moon, bow down before Him,
Dwellers all in time and space:
Praise with us the God of grace.

title: Praise to the Lord, the Almighty, the King of creation;
author: Joachim Neander & Rupert E. Davies tr/ad by Katherine Winkworth & others (1679)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Praise to the Lord, the Almighty, the King of creation;
O my soul, praise Him, for He is thy health and salvation;

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Praise to the Lord, who doth prosper thy work and defend thee;
Surely His goodness and mercy here daily attend thee;
If with His love He befriend thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Praise to the Lord, who, when darkness and sin is abounding,
Who, when the godless do triumph, all virtue confounding,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Praise to the Lord, O let all that is in me adore Him;
All that hath life and breath come now with praises before Him;
Gladly for aye we adore Him.

title: Put thou thy trust in God
author: Paul Gerhardt tr/ad by John Wesley [Paisley: Charles Wesley] (1656)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Put thou thy trust in God,
Walk in His strength with faith and hope,
So shall thy work be done.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Give to the winds thy fears;
God hears thy sighs and counts thy tears,
God shall lift up thy head.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: To His sure truth and tender care

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Though years on years roll on,
Though clouds and darkness hide His path,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Through waves, and clouds, and storms
Wait thou His time; so shall this night

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: So shalt thou, wondering, own His way
How wise, how strong His hand.

title: Rejoice! The Lord is King;
author: Charles Wesley (1744)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Lift up your heart, lift up your voice;

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The God of truth and love;
When He had purged our stains
Lift up your heart, lift up your voice;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: He rules o'er earth and heaven;
The keys of death and hell
Lift up your heart, lift up your voice;

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: He sits at God's right hand
Lift up your heart, lift up your voice,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: We soon shall hear th' archangel's voice;
The trump of God shall sound, rejoice!

title: Saviour, again to Thy dear name we raise
author: John Ellerton (1866)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Saviour, again to Thy dear name we raise
With one accord our parting hymn of praise:
We rise to bless Thee ere our worship cease;
Then, quietly waiting, hear Thy word of peace.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Grant us Thy peace upon our homeward way;
With Thee began, with Thee shall end the day;
Guard Thou the lips from sin, the hearts from shame,
That in this place have called upon Thy name.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Grant us Thy peace, Lord, through the coming night;
Turn Thou for us its darkness into light;
From harm and danger keep Thy children free,
For dark and light are both alike to Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Grant us Thy peace throughout our earthly life,
Our balm in sorrow and our stay in strife;
Then, when Thy voice shall bid our conflict cease,
Call us, O Lord, to Thine eternal peace.

title: Saviour, Thy dying love
author: Sylvanus Dryden Phelps (1862)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: In love my soul would bow,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Help me the cross to bear,
Some song to raise, or prayer,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: All that I am and have,
In joy, in grief, through life,
And when Thy face I see

title: Saviour, lead us by Thy power
author: William Williams of Pantycelyn

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Saviour, lead us by Thy power
Choose the path, the way whatever
Seems to Thee, O Lord, the best:
Be our guide in every peril,
Watch and keep us night and day,
Else our foolish hearts will wander
From the straight and narrow way.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Since in Thee is our redemption,
Naught can stay our steady progress,
If our eyes, whate'er the danger,
Look to Thee, and none but Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: In Thy presence we are happy;
In Thy presence we can conquer,
We can suffer, we can die;
Wandering from Thee we are feeble;
Let Thy love then keep us nigh.

title: Speak, Lord, in the stillness
author: Emily May Grimes Crawford (1920)

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Let me see Thy face, Lord,

title: Take my life, and let it be
author: Frances Ridley Havergal (1874)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Take my life, and let it be
Take my moments and my days,
Let them flow with ceaseless praise.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Take my hands, and let them move
At the impulse of Thy love;
Take my feet, and let them be

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Take my voice, and let me sing
Take my lips, and let them be

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Take my silver and my gold,
Not a mite would I withhold;
Every power as Thou shalt choose.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Take my will, and make it Thine,
It shall be no longer mine;
Take my heart—it is Thine own,
It shall be Thy royal throne.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Take my love; my Lord, I pour
Take myself, and I will be

title: Teach me Thy way, O Lord
author: Benjamin Mansell Ramsey (1919)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Teach me Thy way, O Lord,
More by faith, less by sight;

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Shine through the cloud and rain,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Long as my life shall last,

title: The bread and wine are spread upon the board
author: George Goodman

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: The bread and wine are spread upon the board,
The guests are here, invited by the Lord;
Why come they thus, why tarry for a space?
But for Thy presence, O Thou King of grace

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Hush, O our hearts, as in the sacred name
We bow in worship and the promise claim—
Where two or three are gathered there am I,
Unseen, yet present to faith's opened eye.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Here in our midst art Thou, O risen Lord;
Worthy, O Lamb once slain, to be adored;
Here in our midst to lead Thy people's praise,
And incense sweet unto the Father raise.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: We do remember Thee, as Thou hast said,
And think upon Thee as we break the bread,
Recall Thy dying love, Thy cross and shame,
Drinking the cup of blessing in Thy name.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Thus do we show the death of our dear Lord,
While in our hearts His love is shed abroad;
So is faith quickened for the conflict here,
Till in a little while He shall appear.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Only a little while we pilgrims stay
To spread the table on our desert way;
Soon will He come, and coming take us home,
Amen, e'en so, Lord Jesus quickly come!

title: The Church's one foundation
author: Samuel John Stone (1866)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: From heaven He came and sought her
With His own blood He bought her,
And for her life He died.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Yet one o'er all the earth,
One Lord, one faith, one birth:
And to one hope she presses,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Yet saints their watch are keeping,
Their cry goes up, How long?
And soon the night of weeping
Shall be the morn of song.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Shall be the Church at rest.

title: The day Thou gavest, Lord, is ended;
author: John Ellerton (1870)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: The day Thou gavest, Lord, is ended;
The darkness falls at Thy behest;
To Thee our morning hymns ascended,
Thy praise shall sanctify our rest.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: We thank Thee that Thy Church unsleeping,
While earth rolls onward into light,
Through all the world her watch is keeping,
And rests not now by day or night.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: As o'er each continent and island
The dawn leads on another day,
The voice of prayer is never silent,
Nor dies the stain of praise away.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: The sun that bids us rest is waking
And hour by hour fresh lips are making
Thy wondrous doings heard on high.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: So be it, Lord! Thy throne shall never,
Like earth's proud empires, pass away;
Thy kingdom stands, and grows for ever,
Till all Thy creatures own Thy sway.

title: The King of love my Shepherd is
author: Henry Williams Baker (1868)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: The King of love my Shepherd is,
I nothing lack if I am His
And He is mine for ever.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Where streams of living water flow
And where the verdant pastures grow

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Perverse and foolish oft I strayed,
But yet in love He sought me,
And on His shoulder gently laid,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: In death's dark vale I fear no ill
With Thee, dear Lord, beside me;
Thy rod and staff my comfort still,
Thy cross before to guide me.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Thou spread'st a table in my sight
And O what transport of delight

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: And so through all the length of days
Good Shepherd, may I sing Thy praise

title: The gloomy night will soon be past
author: Samuel Prideaux Tregelles (1855)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: The gloomy night will soon be past,
The day of glorious light at last

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Ah, yes, Lord Jesus, Thou whose heart
Still for Thy saints doth care,
We shall behold Thee as Thou art,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thy love sustains us on our way
Thou dost, O Saviour, day by day

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: But, oh, the more we learn of Thee,
The more we long Thy face to see,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Then Shine, Thou bright and morning star,
O take from sin and grief afar

title: The Lord will perfect that which doth concern me
author: Winifred A. Iverson

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: The Lord will perfect that which doth concern me,
His way is perfect, so His goal must be;
All life's events in harmony are working
For those clear issues which I yet shall see.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The Lord will perfect that which doth concern me,
And will complete each half-formed thing He sends:
His rich designs most carefully are woven,
There are with Him no loose or broken ends.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: The Lord will perfect that which doth concern me,
And finish what His grace has here begun;
He gathers up life's fragments, losing nothing,
And turns to good account each single one.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: The Lord will perfect that which doth concern me,
Will do it in so many different ways;
By loss or gain, by high success or failure,
By steady course or unexpected phase.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: The Lord will perfect that which doth concern me,
Expecting me to show Him on my part
A trust intelligent and full of interest
In all these purposes of His great heart.

title: The Lord's my Shepherd, I'll not want:
author: Francis Rous (Rowe) & (1650) Scottish Psalter (1650)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: The Lord's my Shepherd, I'll not want:
He makes me down to lie
In pastures green; He leadeth me

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: My soul He doth restore again;
And me to walk doth make
E'en for His own name's sake.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Yea, though I walk in death's dark vale,
Yet will I fear none ill;
For Thou art with me; and Thy rod

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: My head Thou dost with oil anoint,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Goodness and mercy all my life
And in God's house for evermore

title: There is a green hill far away
author: Cecil Frances (Humphreys) Alexander (1852)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: There is a green hill far away,
Where the dear Lord was crucified,
Who died to save us all.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: We may not know, we cannot tell
What pains He had to bear;
But we believe it was for us

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: He died that we might be forgiven,
He died to make us good,
That we might go at last to heaven,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: There was no other good enough
To pay the price of sin;
He only could unlock the gate
Of heaven, and let us in.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: O dearly, dearly has He loved,
And we must love Him too,
And trust in His redeeming blood,
And try His works to do.

title: Thou who did'st come to die
author: K. H. Elders

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Thou who did'st come to die
From the bright realms on high,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thy tomb was sealed in vain,
All power to Thee is given,
And we with Thee are risen,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: To take Thy loved ones home,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Peace, life and hope, O Lord,
Thou giv'st us in Thy word,

title: Thou whose almighty word
author: John Marriott (1813)

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Thou who didst come to bring,
Health to the sick in mind,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Through the world, far and wide,

title: Thy life was given for me
author: Frances Ridley Havergal tr/ad by Church Hymns (1858)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Thy life was given for me,
Thy blood, O Lord, was shed
Thy life was given for me;
What have I given for Thee?

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Long years were spent for me
Long years were spent for me:
Have I spent one for Thee?

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thou, Lord, hast borne for me
More than my tongue can tell
What have I borne for Thee?

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: And Thou hast brought to me,
What have I brought to Thee?

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: O let my life be given,
My years for Thee be spent;

title: 'Twas on that night, when doomed to know
author: John Morrison (1781)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: 'Twas on that night, when doomed to know
The eager rage of every foe,
That night in which He was betrayed,
The Saviour of the world took bread.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: And after thanks and glory given
To Him that rules in earth and heaven,
That symbol of His flesh He broke,
And thus to all His followers spoke.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: My broken body thus I give
For you, for all; take, eat, and live:
And oft the sacred rite renew
That brings My wondrous love to view.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Then in His hands the cup He raised,
And God anew He thanked and praised,
While kindness in His bosom glowed,
And from His lips salvation flowed.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: My blood I thus pour forth, He cries,
To cleanse the soul in sin that lies;
In this the covenant is sealed,

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: With love to man this cup is fraught,
Let all partake the sacred draught;
Through latest ages let it pour
In memory of My dying hour.

title: We bless Thee, God and Father
author: Alexander Carruthers

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: We bless Thee, God and Father,
We share Thy Son's blest place:
He lives a Man before Thee

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: His God and ours Thou art;
We're His, in joy He brings us
To share His part and place,
To know Thy love and favour,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Thy love that now enfolds us
Can ne'er wax cold or dim;
In Him that love doth centre,
And we are loved in Him:
In Him Thy love and glory
In Him how near, how blest!

title: We saw Thee not when Thou didst come
author: Anne Rigby Richter & John Hampden Gurney (1834)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: We saw Thee not when Thou didst come
To this poor world of sin and death,
Nor e'er beheld Thy cottage home
But we believe Thy footsteps trod
Its streets and plains, Thou Son of God.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: We did not see Thee lifted high
Amid that wild and savage crew,
Nor heard Thy meek, imploring cry,
Forgive, they know not what they do;
Yet we believe the deed was done
Which shook the earth, and veiled the sun.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: We stood not by the empty tomb
Where late Thy sacred body lay,
Nor sat within that upper room,
Nor met Thee in the open way;
But we believe the angel said,
Why seek the living with the dead?

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: We did not mark the chosen few
When Thou didst through the clouds ascend,
First lift to heaven their wondering view,
Then to the earth all prostrate bend;
Yet we believe that mortal eyes
Beheld that journey to the skies.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: And now that Thou dost reign on high,
And thence Thy waiting people bless,
No ray of glory from the sky
But we believe Thy faithful word,
And trust in our redeeming Lord.

title: Worthy of homage and of praise;
author: F. Theodora Wigram

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Worthy of homage and of praise;
Worthy by all to be adored;
Thou, Thou art worthy, Jesus, Lord.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: The Lamb once slain, in glory bright;
'Tis thence Thou watchest o'er Thine own,
Guarding us through the deadly fight.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: To Thee, e'en now, our song we raise,
Though sure the tribute mean must prove,
No mortal tongue can tell Thy ways,
So full of light and life and love.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Yet, Saviour, Thou shalt have full praise;
We soon shall meet Thee on the cloud,
We soon shall see Thee face to face,
In glory praising as we would.

title: Ye gates, lift up your heads on high;
author: Francis Rous (Rowe) & William Barton & (1650) Scottish Psalter

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Ye gates, lift up your heads on high;
Ye doors that last for aye
Be lifted up, that so the King
But who of glory is the King?
Ev'n that same Lord that great in might

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Ye gates, lift up your heads; ye doors,
Doors that do last for aye,
Be lifted up, that so the King
But who is He that is the King
The Lord of hosts, and none but He,

title: Ye servants of God, your Master proclaim
author: Charles Wesley (1744)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Ye servants of God, your Master proclaim,
And publish abroad His wonderful name;
The name all-victorious of Jesus extol;
His kingdom is glorious, and rules over all.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: God ruleth on high, almighty to save;
And still He is nigh, His presence we have;
The great congregation His triumph shall sing,
Ascribing salvation to Jesus our King.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Salvation to God who sits on the throne;
Let all cry aloud, and honour the Son;
The praises of Jesus the angels proclaim,
Fall down on their faces and worship the Lamb.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Then let us adore and give Him His right;
All glory and power, all wisdom and might;
All honour and blessing with angels above,
And thanks never-ceasing, and infinite love.

title: Now to Him who loved us, gave us
author: Samuel Miller Waring

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Now to Him who loved us, gave us
Every pledge that love could give,
Freely shed His blood to save us,
Gave His life that we may live,

title: A pilgrim was I and awand'ring
author: John W. Peterson (1921-2006)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: A pilgrim was I and a-wand'ring
In the cold night of sin I did roam
When Jesus the kind Shepherd found me
And now I am on my way home

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: He restoreth my soul when I'm weary,
He giveth me strength day by day;
He leads me beside the still waters,
He guards me each step of the way.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: When I walk through the dark lonesome valley,
My savior will walk with me there;
And safely His great hand will lead me
To the mansions He's gone to prepare.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me
All the days, all the days of my life;
Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me
All the days, all the days of my life.
And I shall dwell in the house of the Lord forever,
And I shall feast at the table spread for me;
Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me
All the days, all the days of my life.

title: A robe of white, a crown of gold
author: Robert Johnson

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: A robe of white, a crown of gold,
A harp, a home, a mansion fair,
A victor's wand of joys untold
Are mine when I get there.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: He paid my debt on Calvary's mountain,
I'm happy in His wondrous love,
I'm drinking, yes I'm drinking at the fountain.

title: He hideth my soul
author: Fanny J. Crosby (1820-1915)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: A wonderful Savior is Jesus my Lord,
He hideth my soul in the cleft of the rock,
Where rivers of pleasure I see.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: A wonderful Savior is Jesus my Lord,
He holdeth me up and I shall not be moved,
He giveth me strength as my day.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: With numberless blessings each moment He crowns,
And, filled with His fulness divine,
I sing in my rapture, oh, glory to God,
For such a Redeemer as mine!

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: When clothed in His brightness, transported I rise
To meet Him in clouds of the sky,
His perfect salvation, His wonderful love,
I'll shout with the millions on high.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: He hideth my soul in the cleft of the rock
That shadows a dry, thirsty land;
He hideth my life in the depths of His love,
And covers me there with His hand,
And covers me there with His hand.

title: All the way my Saviour leads me
author: Fanny J. Crosby (1820-1915)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: All the way my Savior leads me;
What have I to ask beside?
Can I doubt His tender mercy,
Who through life has been my Guide?
Here by faith in Him to dwell!
For I know, whate'er befall me,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: All the way my Savior leads me,
Cheers each winding path I tread,
Gives me grace for every trial,
Feeds me with the living bread.
Though my weary steps may falter,
And my soul athirst may be,
Gushing from the Rock before me,
Lo! a spring of joy I see.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: All the way my Savior leads me;
Oh, the fullness of His grace!
Perfect rest to me is promised
Wings its flight to realms of day,
This my song through endless ages:
Jesus led me all the way.

title: Amazing grace
author: John Newton (1725-1807)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Amazing grace! how sweet the sound,
That saved a wretch; like me!
I once was lost, but now am found,
Was blind, but now I see.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Twas grace that taught my heart to fear,
How precious did that grace appear

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Through many dangers, toils and snares
T'was grace that brought us safe thus far
And grace will lead us home.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: When we've been there ten thousand years,
We've no less days to sing God's praise

title: Altogether lovely
author: Wendell P. Loveless

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: And the fairest of ten thousand,
He gave Himself to save me,
Now He lives in heav'n to keep me,
Is this wonderful Savior of mine.

title: And can it be
author: Charles Wesley (1707-1788)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: And can it be that I should gain
An int'rest in the Savior's blood?
Died He for me, who caused His pain—
For me, who Him to death pursued?
Amazing love! How can it be,
That Thou, my God, shouldst die for me?

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: He left His Father's throne above—
So free, so infinite His grace—
Emptied Himself of all but love,
And bled for Adam's helpless race:
For, O my God, it found out me!

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Jesus, and all in Him, is mine;
Alive in Him, my living Head,
Bold I approach th' eternal throne,
And claim the crown, through Christ my own.

title: Anywhere with Jesus
author: Jessie B. Pounds (1861-1921)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Anywhere with Jesus I can safely go
Anywhere He leads me in this world below
Anywhere without Him dearest joy would fade
Anywhere with Jesus I am not afraid

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Anywhere with Jesus, I am not alone
Other friends may fail me, He is still my own
Tho' His hand may lead me over dearest ways
Anywhere with Jesus is a house of praise

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Anywhere with Jesus I can go to sleep
When the darkening shadows round about me creep
Knowing I shall waken nevermore to roam
Anywhere with Jesus will be home, sweet home

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Anywhere! Anywhere! Fear I cannot know
Anywhere with Jesus I can safely go

title: Awake my soul, in joyful lays
author: Samuel Medley (1738-1799)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Awake, my soul, in joyful lays
And sing thy great Redeemer's praise;
He justly claims a song from me;

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: He saw me ruined in the fall,
He saved me from my lost estate;

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: When trouble, like a gloomy cloud,
Has gathered thick and thundered loud,
He near my soul has always stood;

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Soon shall we mount and soar away
To the bright realms of endless day;
And sing, with rapture and surprise,

title: Beside the still waters
author: Ted Silva

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Beside the still waters in pastures of green,
The Shepherd is leading where all is serene;
By day and by night He will always be seen
Beside the still waters of peace.
For He's the Good Shepherd who died for the sheep;
His own He has promised to keep.
He lovingly watches and guards while they sleep
Beside the still waters of peace.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Beside the still waters the sheep find their rest;
The Shepherd stands by so that none can molest;
The flock, by His presence, is happy and blest
Beside the still waters of peace
The sheep know His voice and they go not astray,
For Jesus will guide all the way.
In paths that are righteous He leads day by day
Beside the still waters of peace.

title: Beyond the Sunset
author: Virgil P. Brock (1887-1978)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Beyond the sunset, O blissful morning,
When with our Saviour Heav'n is begun.
Earth's toiling ended, O glorious dawning;
Beyond the sunset, when day is done.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Beyond the sunset, no clouds will gather,
No storms will threaten, no fears annoy;
O day of gladness, O day unending,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Beyond the sunset, a hand will guide me
To God, the Father, whom I adore;
His glorious presence, his words of welcome,
Will be my portion on that fair shore.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Beyond the sunset, O glad reunion,
With our dear loved ones who've gone before;
In that fair homeland we'll know no parting,

title: Blessed Assurance
author: Fanny J. Crosby (1820-1915)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: O what a foretaste of glory divine
Heir of salvation, purchase of God
Born of His Spirit, washed in His blood

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Visions of rapture now burst on my sight;
Echoes of mercy, whispers of love.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Perfect submission, all is at rest
I in my Savior am happy and blessed
Filled with His goodness, lost in His love

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: This is my story, this is my song
Praising my Savior all the day long
This is my story, this is my song
Praising my Savior all the day long

title: He that winneth souls is wise
author: N. H. Lines

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Blessed is the service of our Lord and King,
Precious are the jewels we may help to bring;
Down the passing ages words of counsel ring:
He that winneth souls is wise.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: In the quiet homelife, showing love's bright ray,
More and more like Jesus living ev'ry day,
We may guide a dear one to the heav'nward way:
He that winneth souls is wise.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Sow beside all waters, sow the gospel seed,
Here a word in season, there a loving deed;
Sinners to the Saviour be it ours to lead:
He that winneth souls is wise.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: He that winneth souls is wise;
In that home beyond the skies,
There's a crown of glory, O the wondrous prize!
He that winneth souls is wise.

title: Let the Lower Lights Be Burning
author: Philip P. Bliss (1838-1876)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: But to us He gives the keeping
Of the lights along the shore.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Dark the night of sin has settled,
For the lights along the shore.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Let the lower lights be burning!
Send a gleam across the wave!
You may rescue, you may save.

title: By the Crowd of Worshippers
author: Carol & Jimmy Snow

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: By the crowd of worshippers, sorry for their sins,
Was a poor wanderer, rudely brought in.
Scribes came and Pharisees, anxious to see.
What the meek Nazarenes' verdict would be.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: They told of her wanderings, making each flaw
Spoke of her punishment, quoting the Law
Writing upon the ground, sadly and slow
But said he unheedingly, head bending low

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Still cried the Pharisees, "Pray, Master, pray
What shall we do with her, what doth thou say?"
Then said he rebukingly, "Let the first stone
Come from the sinless hands, hence and alone."

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Cheeks flushing with the shame, turning about
And from his presence walking slowly out
Then saw him standing there, head bending low
He who the world despised, bade her sin no more.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Spoke he most tenderly, 'pray woman, pray
Hast thou no accusers?" "Nay, Master, nay"
"Neither do I condemn thee, soul sick and sore
Go forth, I pardon thee, go and sin no more.'

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Neither do I condemn thee, precious words divine
From the lips of mercy, like sweetest chimes
Wonderful words of Jesus, sing them o'er and o'er
Neither do I condemn thee, go and sin no more.

title: Christ Has For Sin Atonement Made
author: Elisha A. Hoffman (1839-1929)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Christ has for sin atonement made -
We are redeemed, the price is paid -

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I praise Him for the cleansing blood -
That reconciled my soul to God -

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: He walks beside me in the way,
And keeps me faithful day by day;

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: What a wonderful Savior is Jesus, my Jesus!
What a wonderful Savior is Jesus, my Lord!

title: Crown Him With Many Crowns
author: Matthew Bridges (1800-1894)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Hark! How the heavenly anthem drowns
Of Him who died for thee.
And hail Him as thy matchless king

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Crown Him the Lord of love;
For thou hast died for me;
Thy praise shall never, never fail

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Crown him the Lord of life,
And rose victorious in the strife
For those He came to save.
Who died, and rose on high,
Who died, eternal life to bring,
And lives that death may die.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Crown him the Lord of Heaven,
The King of kings to whom is given
His reign shall know no end,

title: Burdens Are Lifted At Calvary
author: John M. Moore

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Days are filled with sorrow and care,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Cast your care on Jesus today,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Troubled soul, the Saviour can see

title: Brighten the Corner Where You Are
author: Ina D. Ogdon (1872-1964)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Do not wait until some deed of greatness you may do,
Do not wait to shed your light afar,
To the many duties ever near you now be true,
Brighten the corner where you are.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Brighten the corner where you are!
Brighten the corner where you are!
Someone far from harbour you may guide across the bar;
Brighten the corner where you are!

title: Does Jesus Care
author: Frank E. Graeff (1860-1919)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Does Jesus care when my heart is pained
Too deeply for mirth or song,
As the burdens press, and the cares distress,
And the way grows weary and long?

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Does Jesus care when my way is dark
With a nameless dread and fear?
As the daylight fades into deep night shades,
Does He care enough to be near?

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Does Jesus care when I've tried and failed
When for my deep grief there is no relief,
Though my tears flow all the night long?

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Does Jesus care when I've said "goodbye"
To the dearest on earth to me,
And my sad heart aches till it nearly breaks—
Is it aught to Him? Does He see?

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Oh, yes, He cares, I know He cares,
His heart is touched with my grief;
When the days are weary, the long nights dreary,

title: Down From His Glory
author: William E. Booth-Clibborn (1863-1969)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: A man of sorrows, tears and agony.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: That in the dead of night,
Not one faint hope in sight,
Stooping to woo, to win, to save my soul.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: He took the form of man,
And now I know Thou art the great I AM.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: O how I love Him! How I adore Him!
My breath, my sunshine, my All in All.
The great Creator became my Saviour,
And all God's fullness dwelleth in Him.

title: Everybody Ought to Know
author: Harry D. Loes (1892-1965)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Everybody ought to know who Jesus is.
He's the lily of the valley.
He's the fairest of ten thousand.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Jesus died upon the tree to set me free.
He has borne the wrath and judgment,
He has paid the debt for me;
He has wrought a full salvation,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Jesus soon will come again to take me home.
He has gone back home to Heaven,
To prepare a place for me,
Soon He'll come to call His loved ones,

title: Face to Face With Christ My Saviour
author: Carrie E. Breck (1855-1934)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Face to face with Christ my Savior,
Face to face, what will it be,
When with rapture I behold Him,
Jesus Christ, Who died for me

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Only faintly now I see Him,
But a blessed day is coming,
When His glory shall be seen.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Face to face! O blissful moment!
Face to face—to see and know;
Face to face with my Redeemer,
Jesus Christ who loves me so.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Face to face I shall behold Him,
Face to face in all His glory,
I shall see Him by and by.

title: That Man of Calvary
author: Manie P. Ferguson (1850-1932)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Fairest of all the earth beside,
Chiefest of all unto Thy bride,
Fullness divine in Thee I see,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Granting the sinner life and peace,
Shedding His blood to make us free,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Comfort of all my earthly way,
Jesus, I'll meet Thee some sweet day;
Center of glory, Thee I'll see,

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Has won my heart from me;
And died to set me free,

title: Give me a Sight, O Saviour
author: Katherine A. M. Kelly

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Give me a sight, O Savior
Of Thy wondrous love to me,
Of the love that brought Thee down to earth

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Was it the nails, O Savior,
That bound Thee to the tree?
Thy love for me, for me.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: That through Thy death for me
My open sins, my secret sins

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Then melt my heart, O Savior;
Bend me, yea, break me down

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Help me to take it in,
What it meant to Thee, the Holy One,

title: Grace! 'tis a Charming Sound
author: Philip Doddridge (1702-1751)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Heaven with the echo shall resound,
And all the earth shall hear.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: And new supplies each hour I meet,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Twas grace that wrote my name
'Twas grace that gave me to the Lamb

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Grace taught my soul to pray,
'Tis grace has kept me to this day
And will not let me go.

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: May all my powers to Thee aspire,
And all my days be Thine.

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Grace all the work shall crown
It lays in Heaven the topmost stone,

title: Do You Know My Jesus?
author: Rev. Vep B. Ellis (1917-1988)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Have you a heart that's weary
Are you a soul that's seeking
Rest from the burden you bear?

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Where is your heart, O pilgrim?
Who hears your call for comfort
When naught but sorrows you feel?

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Who hears each time you cry?
Who dries the tears from your eyes?

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Have you heard He loves you?
And that He will abide 'till the end?

title: God Is Still on the Throne
author: Kittie L. Suffield (1884-1972)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Have you started for glory and Heaven?
Have you left this old world far behind?
In your heart is the Comforter dwelling?
Can you say, "Praise the Lord, He is mine"?
Have the ones that once walked on highway
Gone back, and you seem all alone?
Keep your eyes on the prize, for the home in the skies;
God is still on the throne.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Burdened soul, is your heart growing weary
With the toil and the heat of the day?
Does it seem that your path is more thorny
As you journey along on life's way?
Go away and in secret before Him
Tell your grief to the Savior alone;
He will lighten your care, for He still answers prayer;
God is still on the throne.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: You may live in a tent or a cottage,
Unnoticed by those who pass by;
But a mansion for you He is building
In that beautiful city on high;
It will outshine the wealth and the splendor
Of the richest on earth we have known;
He's the Architect true, and He's building for you;
God is still on the throne.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: He is coming again, is the promise
To disciples when He went away;
In like manner as He has gone from you,
You will see Him returning some day;
Does His tarrying cause you to wonder,
Does it seem He's forgotten His own?
His promise is true, He is coming for you;
God is still on the throne.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: God is still on the throne, and He will remember His own;
Though trials may press us and burdens distress us,
He never will leave us alone;
God is still on the throne, He never forsaketh His own;
His promise is true, He will not forget you;
God is still on the throne.

title: Hast Thou Heard Him, Seen Him, Known Him
author: Ora Rowan (1834-1879)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Hast thou heard Him, seen Him, known Him?
Is not thine a captured heart?

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Idols once they won thee, charmed thee,
Lovely things of time and sense;
Gilded, thus does sin disarm thee,
Honeyed, lest thou turn thee thence.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: What has stripped the seeming beauty
From the idols of the earth?
Not a sense of right or duty,
But the sight of peerless worth.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Not the crushing of those idols,
With its bitter void and smart,
But the beaming of His beauty,

stanzas.label: Verse 5
lines: Tis that look that melted Peter,
'Tis that heart that wept with Mary,

stanzas.label: Verse 6
lines: Draw, and win, and fill completely,
What have we to do with idols,

title: He Leadeth Me
author: Joseph H. Gilmore (1834-1918)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: He leadeth me! O blessed thought!
O words with heavenly comfort fraught!
Whate'er I do, where'er I be,
Still 'tis God's hand that leadeth me.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: By waters still, o'er troubled sea,
Still 'tis God's hand that leadeth me.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Lord, I would clasp Thy hand in mine,
Since 'tis God's hand that leadeth me.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: He leadeth me, He leadeth me,
By His own hand He leadeth me;
His faithful foll'wer I would be,
For by His hand He leadeth me.

title: He giveth more grace
author: Annie J. Flint (1866-1932)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: He giveth more grace when the burdens grow greater,
He sendeth more strength when the labors increase;
To added afflictions He addeth His mercy,
To multiplied trials, His multiplied peace.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: When we have exhausted our store of endurance,
When our strength has failed ere the day is half done,
When we reach the end of our hoarded resources
Our Father's full giving is only begun.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: His love has no limits, His grace has no measure,
His power no boundary known unto men;
For out of His infinite riches in Jesus
He giveth, and giveth, and giveth again.

title: He washed my eyes with tears
author: Ira F. Stanphill (1920-1993)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: He washed my eyes with tears that I might see,
The broken heart I had was good for me;
He tore it all apart and looked inside,
He found it full of fear and foolish pride.
He swept away the things that made me blind
And then I saw the clouds were silver lined;
And now I understand 'twas best for me
He washed my eyes with tears that I might see.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: He washed my eyes with tears that I might see
The glory of Himself revealed to me;
I did not know that He had wounded hands
I saw the blood He spilt upon the sands.
I saw the marks of shame and wept and cried;
He was my substitute for me He died;
And now I'm glad He came so tenderly;
And washed my eyes with tears that I might see.

title: How I praise thee precious Savior
author: Mary E. Maxwell

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: How I praise Thee, precious Savior,
That Thy love laid hold of me;
Thou hast saved and cleansed and filled me,
That I might Thy channel be.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Just a channel, full of blessing,
To tell out Thy full salvation,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Witnessing Thy grace to save me,
Setting free from self and sin;
Thou hast bought me to possess me,
In Thy fulness, Lord, come in.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: But with all Thy wondrous grace,
Flowing through us, Thou canst use us

title: His name is Wonderful
author: Audrey Mier (1916-1996)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: His name is wonderful, His name is wonderful,
His name is wonderful, Jesus my Lord;
He is the mighty King, Master of everything,
His name is wonderful, Jesus my Lord.
He's the great Shepherd, the Rock of all ages,
Bow down before Him, love and adore Him,
His name is wonderful, Jesus my Lord.

title: How good is the God we adore
author: Joseph Hart (1712-1768)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: How good is the God we adore,
Whose love is as great as his power,
And knows neither measure nor end.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Tis Jesus, the First and the Last,
Whose Spirit shall guide us safe home;
We'll praise Him for all that is past,
And trust Him for all that's to come.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: In the sweet by and by,
We shall meet on that beautiful shore;
In the sweet by and by,
We shall meet on that beautiful shore.

title: I am not skilled to understand
author: Dorothy Greenwell (1821-1882)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I am not skilled to understand
What God has willed, what God has planned.
I only know at His right hand
Stands One who is my Savior.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I take Him at His word indeed;
"Christ died for sinners," this I read;
For in my heart I find a need
Of Him to be my Savior!

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: That He should leave His place on high
And come for sinful man to die,
You count it strange?—So once did I,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Yea, living, dying, let me bring
My strength, my solace from this spring,
That He who lives to be my King
Once died to be my Savior!

title: I am so glad that our Father in heaven
author: Emily S. Oakey (1829-1883)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I am so glad that our Father in heaven
Tells of His love in the Book He has given;
Wonderful things in the Bible I see:
This is the dearest, that Jesus loves me.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Though I forget Him and wander away,
Still He doth love me wherever I stray;
Back to His dear loving arms would I flee,
When I remember that Jesus loves me.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Oh, if there's only one song I can sing,
When in His beauty I see the great King,
This shall my song in eternity be:
"Oh, what a wonder that Jesus loves me."

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: I am so glad that Jesus loves me,
Jesus loves me, Jesus loves me.
I am so glad that Jesus loves me,

title: I am thine O Lord
author: Fanny J. Crosby (1820-1915)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I am Thine, O Lord, I have heard Thy voice,
And it told Thy love to me;
But I long to rise in the arms of faith,
And be closer drawn to Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Consecrate me now to Thy service, Lord
By the pow'r of grace divine.
Let my soul look up with a steadfast hope,
And my will be lost in Thine.

title: I am weak but Thou art strong
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I am weak, but Thou art strong;
Jesus, keep me from all wrong;
As I walk, let me walk close to Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Through this world of toil and snares,
If I falter, Lord, who cares?
Who with me my burden shares?
None but Thee, dear Lord, none but Thee.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: When my feeble life is o'er,
Time for me will be no more;
To Thy kingdom shore, to Thy shore.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Just a closer walk with Thee—
Grant it, Jesus, is my plea;
Let it be, dear Lord, let it be.

title: I come to the garden alone
author: Charles A. Miles (1868-1946)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I come to the garden alone,
While the dew is still on the roses,
And the voice I hear falling on my ear

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: He speaks, and the sound of His voice
Is so sweet the birds hush their singing,
And the melody that He gave to me,

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: And He walks with me, and He talks with me,
And He tells me I am His own;
And the joy we share as we tarry there,

title: I don't know about tomorrow
author: Ira F. Stanphill (1920-1993)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I just live from day to day;
I don't borrow from it's sunshine,
For its skies may turn to gray;
I don't worry o'er the future,
For I know what Jesus said,
And today I'll walk beside Him,
For He knows what is ahead.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: As the golden stairs I climb;
There the sun is always shining,
There no tear will dim the eye;
At the ending of the rainbow,
Where the mountains touch the sky.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: But the One who feeds the sparrow
Is the One who stands by me;
And the path that be my portion
May be through the flame or flood,
But His presence goes before me,
And I'm covered with His blood.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: But I know Who holds tomorrow,
And I know Who holds my hand.

title: I have a Friend so precious
author: L. Shorey (1851-1951)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I have a Friend so precious,
I could not live apart from Him,
I love to feel Him nigh,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: He knows how much I love Him,
He knows I love Him well;
But with what love he loveth me
And so we love each other,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: He knows how I am longing
And so he bids me go and speak
He bids me tell his wondrous love,
And why he came to die,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: In rest and peace at last
In the kingdom of the future
In the glory bye and bye,

title: I have a Shepherd
author: Leonard W. Weaver

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I have a Shepherd, One I love so well;
How he has blessed me tongue can never tell;
On the Cross He suffered, shed his blood and died
That I might ever in His love confide.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Pastures abundant doth His hand provide,
Still waters flowing ever at my side;
Goodness and mercy follow on my track,
With such a Shepherd, nothing can I lack.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: When labour's ended and the journey done,
Then He will lead me safely to my home;
There I shall dwell in rapture pure and sweet,
With all the loved ones gathered round His feet.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Following Jesus, ever day by day,
Nothing can harm me when he leads the way;
Jesus, the Shepherd, is my All in all.

title: I heard the voice of Jesus say
author: Horatius Bonar (1808-1889)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I heard the voice of Jesus say,
Lay down, thou weary one, lay down

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I heard the voice of Jesus say,
Stoop down, and drink and live."

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: I came to Jesus as I was,
I found in Him a resting place,
And He has made me glad.

title: In my heart there rings a melody
author: Elton M. Roth (1891-1951)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I have a song that Jesus gave me,
It was sent from Heaven, above.
There never was a sweeter melody,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I love the Christ who died on Calvary,
For He washed my sins away;
He put within my heart a melody,
And I know it's there to stay.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Twill be my endless theme in glory,
With the angels I will sing;
'Twill be a song of glorious harmony,
When the courts of Heaven ring.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: In my heart there rings a melody,
There rings a melody with heaven's harmony.
In my heart there rings a melody,
There rings a melody of love.

title: I know not the hour
author: Fanny J. Crosby (1820-1915)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I know not the hour of His coming
Nor how He will speak to my heart;
Nor whether at morning or midday
My spirit to Him will depart.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I know not the bliss that awaits me,
At rest with my Saviour above;
I know not how soon I shall enter,
And bathe in the ocean of love.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: I know not, but O, I am watching,
My lamp ever burning and bright,
I know not if Jesus will call me
At morning, at noon or at night.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: But I know...I shall wake in the likeness
Of Him I am longing to see;
I know...that mine eyes shall behold Him
Who died...for a sinner like me.

title: But I know Whom I have believed
author: D. W. Whittle (1840-1901)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I know not why God's wondrous grace
To me He hath made me known,
Nor why, unworthy of such love,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I know not what of good or ill
Of weary ways or golden days,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: I know not when my Lord may come,
Nor if I'll walk the vale with Him,
Or meet Him in the air.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: But I know Whom I have believed,
And am persuaded that He is able
To keep that which I've committed

title: I know that my Redeemer liveth
author: Jessie B. Pounds (1861-1921)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I know that my Redeemer liveth,
And on the earth again shall stand.
I know eternal life He giveth,
That grace and power are in His hand.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I know His promise never faileth,
The word He speaks, it cannot die;
Though cruel death my flesh assaileth,
Yet I shall see Him bye and bye.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: I know my mansion He prepareth,
That where He is, there I may be;
O wondrous thought, for me He careth,
And He at last will come for me.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: I know, I know, that Jesus liveth,
And on the earth again shall stand;
I know, I know, that life He giveth,
That grace and power are in His hand.

title: I must have the Saviour with me
author: Fanny J. Crosby (1820-1915)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I must have the Saviour with me,
For I dare not walk alone;
I must feel His presence near me,
And His arm around me thrown.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I must have the Saviour with me,
For my faith, at best, is weak;
He can whisper words of comfort
That no other voice can speak.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: I must have the Saviour with me,
And His eye the way must guide,
Till I reach the vale of Jordan,
Till I cross the rolling tide.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Then my soul shall fear no ill,
Let Him lead me where He will;
I will go without a murmur,

title: I need Thee every hour
author: Annie S. Hawks (1835-1918)

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: I need Thee, O I need Thee,
O bless me now, my Saviour,

title: I serve a risen Saviour
author: A. H. Ackley (1887-1960)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I know that He is living,
I see His hand of mercy,
I hear His voice of cheer,
And just the time I need Him,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Lift up your voice and sing
The hope of all who seek Him,
The help of all who find,

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: He walks with me and talks with me
You ask me how I know He lives-

title: I stand amazed in the presence
author: Charles H. Gabriel (1856-1932)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I stand amazed in the presence
And wonder how He could love me,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: For me it was in the garden
He prayed, Not My will, but Thine;
He had no tears for His own griefs,
But sweat drops of blood for mine.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: He took my sins and my sorrows,
He made them His very own;
He bore the burden to Calvary,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: When with the ransomed in glory
His face I at last shall see,
'Twill be my joy through the ages
To sing of His love for me.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: And my song shall ever be,
Is my Saviour's love for me.

title: I thirsted in the barren land
author: John W. Peterson (1921-2006)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I thirsted in the barren land of sin and shame,
And nothing satisfying there I found;
But to the blessed cross of Christ one day I came
Where springs of living water did abound.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: How sweet the living water from the hills of God,
It makes me glad and happy all the way;
Now glory, grace and blessing mark the path I've trod,

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Drinking at the springs of living water,
Drinking at the springs of living water,

title: I once was a sinner
author: Charles A. Miles (1868-1946)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I once was a sinner, but I came,
Pardon to receive from my Lord;
This was freely given and I found
That he always kept His word.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: In the book is written, 'Saved by grace,"
O the joy that came to my soul;
Now I am forgiven and I know
By the blood I am made whole.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: There's a new name written down in glory,
And it's mine, O yes it's mine;
And the white-robed angels sing the story,
For there's a new name written down in glory,
And it's mine, O yes it's mine,
With my sins forgiven, I am bound for heaven,

title: Love lifted me
author: James Rowe (1865-1933)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I was sinking deep in sin,
But the Master of the sea

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: All my heart to Him I give,
Love so mighty and so true,

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Love lifted me, love lifted me,
Love lifted me, love lifted me,

title: I was straying when Christ found me
author: Avis B. Christiansen (1895-1985)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I was straying when Christ found me
In the night so dark and cold;
Tenderly His arm went round me
And he bore me to His fold.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: To the shelter of His love;
Of His grace and will He taught me,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Through the night be dark around me,
I am safe, for He is near;
Never shall my foes confound me,
While the Saviour's voice I hear.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: In the shelter of His love;
And I'm sheltered in His love.

title: I will make you fishers of men
author: Harry D. Clarke

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I will make you fishers of men,
Fishers of men, fishers of men,
I will make you fishers of men
If you follow Me, if you follow Me.
I will make you fishers of men

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: "I will give you rest, I will give you rest."

title: I will meet you in the morning
author: Albert E. Brumley (1905-1977)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I will meet you in the morning, by the bright river side,
When all sorrow has drifted away;
I'll be standing at the portals, when the gates open wide,
At the close of life's long, dreary day.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I will meet you in the morning, at the end of the way,
On the streets of that City of gold;
Where we all can be together and be happy for aye,
While the years and the ages shall roll.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: I will meet you in the morning,
And we'll sit down by the river,
You'll know me in the morning
By the smiles that I'll wear
When I meet you in the morning
In the City that is built foursquare.

title: I will sing of my Redeemer
author: Philip P. Bliss (1838-1876)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I will sing of my Redeemer,
And His wondrous love to me.
On the cruel cross he suffered,
From the curse to set me free.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I will sing of my Redeemer,
And His heavenly love to me.
He from death to life hath brought me,
Son of God, with Him to be.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Sing, O sing of my Redeemer.
With His blood He purchased me.
On the cross He sealed my pardon,
Paid the debt and made me free.

title: I will work for Jesus
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I will work for Jesus, trust Him and obey,
Carry out His orders, serve Him day by day
In the ripened harvest, over hill and plain,
Gleaning for the Master sheaves of golden grain.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Gleaning some with gladness, gleaning some with tears,
On account of thistles with the golden ears,
Trusting in the Saviour, ever on I go,
Up and down the hillside, gleaning to and fro.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: I shall never weary of the work I do,
For the Lord will strengthen all the harvest through.
Laying down the sickle, when the end has come,
I shall be admitted to the harvest home.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: I will work for Jesus till the shadows fall,
Labour for the Master till I hear His call.
In the dewy evening when the gleaners leave
I will come rejoicing, bringing in the sheaves.

title: I'd Rather Have Jesus
author: Rhea F. Miller

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I'd rather have Jesus than silver or gold;
I'd rather be His than have riches untold;
I'd rather have Jesus than houses or lands.
I'd rather be led by His nail pierced hands

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I'd rather have Jesus than men's applause;
I'd rather be faithful to His dear cause;
I'd rather have Jesus than worldwide fame.
I'd rather be true to His holy name.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: He's fairer than lilies of rarest bloom;
He's sweeter than honey from out the comb;
He's all that my hungering spirit needs.
I'd rather have Jesus and let Him lead.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Than to be the king of a vast domain
And be held in sin's dread sway.
I'd rather have Jesus than anything

title: I'm Pressing On the Upward Way
author: Johnson Oatman, Jr

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I'm pressing on the upward way,
New heights I'm gaining every day;
Still praying as I'm onward bound,
"Lord, plant my feet on higher ground."

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: My heart has no desire to stay
Where doubts arise and fears dismay;
Though some may dwell where these abound,
My prayer, my aim, is higher ground.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: I want to scale the utmost height
And catch a gleam of glory bright;
But still I'll pray till heaven I've found,
"Lord, lead me on to higher ground."

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Lord, lift me up and let me stand,
A higher plane than I have found;
Lord, plant my feet on higher ground.

title: Mansions Over the Hilltop
author: Ira F. Stanphill (1920-1993)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I'm satisfied with just a cottage below
A little silver and a little gold
But in that city where the ransomed shall shine
I've got a gold one that's silver lined

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Don't think me poor or deserted or lonely
I'm not discouraged I'm heaven bound
I'm just a pilgrim in search of a city
I want a mansion, a harp and a crown

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: I've got a mansion just over the hilltop
In that bright land where we'll never grow old
And some day yonder we'll never more wander
But walk on streets that are purest gold

title: The Lily of the Valley
author: Charles W. Fry

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I've found a friend in Jesus, He's everything to me,
He's the fairest of ten thousand to my soul;
The Lily of the Valley, in Him alone I see
All I need to cleanse and make me fully whole.
In sorrow He's my comfort, in trouble He's my stay;
He tells me every care on Him to roll.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: He'll never, never leave me, nor yet forsake me here,
While I live by faith and do His blessed will;
A wall of fire about me, I've nothing now to fear,
With His manna He my hungry soul shall fill.
Then sweeping on to glory I'll see His blessed face,
Where rivers of delight shall ever flow.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: He's the Lily of the Valley, the Bright and Morning Star,
He's the Fairest of ten thousand to my soul.
In sorrow He's my Comfort, in trouble He's my Stay,
He tells me every care on Him to roll;
He's the Lily of the Valley, the Bright and Morning Star,
He's the Fairest of ten thousand to my soul.

title: I've Found a Friend
author: James G. Small

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: I've found a friend, O such a friend!
He loved me ere I knew Him
He drew me with the cords of love,
And thus he bound me to Him;
And round my heart still closely twine
Those ties which naught can sever,
For I am His, and He is mine,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I've found a friend, O such a friend!
He bled, he died to save me;
And not alone the gift of life,
But His own self He gave me;
Nought that I have my own I'll call,
I'll hold it for the Giver;
My heart, my strength, my life, my all

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: I've found a friend, O such a friend!
So kind and true and tender,
So wise a counselor and guide,
From Him who loves me now so well
What power my soul can sever?
Shall life or death shall earth or hell?

title: In My Father's House
author: The Blackwood Brothers

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: In my Father's house are many mansions;
If it were not true He would have told me so.
He has gone away to live in that bright city,
He's preparing me a mansion there I know.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Jesus died upon the cross to bear my sorrow,
Freely died that souls like you might have new life;
But I know there soon will come a bright tomorrow,
When the world will all be free from sin and strife.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Do not shun the Saviour's love, from up in glory,
Or you won't be there to sing the gospel story;
In my Father's house are many mansions;
If you're His, then to this land you'll surely go.

title: If I Gained the World
author: Anna Olander

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: If I gained the world, but lost the Saviour,
Were my life worth living for a day?
Could my yearning heart find rest and comfort
In the things that soon must pass away?
If I gained the world, but lost the Saviour,
Would my gain be worth the lifelong strife?
Are all earthly pleasures worth comparing
For a moment with a Christ-filled life?

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Had I wealth and love in fullest measure,
And a name revered both far and near,
Yet no hope beyond, no harbour waiting,
Where my storm-tossed vessel I could steer;
If I gained the world, but lost the Saviour,
Who endured the cross and died for me,
Could then all the world afford a refuge,
Whither, in my anguish, I might flee?

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: O the joy of having all in Jesus!
What a balm the broken heart to heal!
Ne'er a sin so great, but He'll forgive it,
Nor a sorrow that He does not feel!
If I have but Jesus, only Jesus,
Nothing else in all the world beside—
O then everything is mine in Jesus;
For my needs and more He will provide.

title: In Tenderness He Sought Me
author: W. Spencer Walton

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: And on His shoulders brought me
While angels in His presence sang
Until the courts of heaven rang.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: And poured in oil and wine;
I never heard a sweeter voice;
It made my aching heart rejoice!

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: O the love that sought me!
O the blood that bought me!
O the grace that brought me to the fold,
Wondrous grace that brought me to the fold!

title: In Times Like These
author: Ruth Caye Jones

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: In times like these you need a Saviour;
In times like these you need an anchor.
Be very sure, be very sure
Your anchor holds and grips the Solid Rock!

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: In times like these you need the Bible.
In times like these O be not idle.
Be very sure, be very sure
Your anchor holds and grips the Solid Rock!

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: In times like these I have a Saviour
In times like these I have an anchor;
I'm very sure, I'm very sure
My anchor holds and grips the solid Rock!

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: This Rock is Jesus, yes, He's the One.
This Rock is Jesus, the only One!
Be very sure, be very sure
Your anchor holds and grips the Solid Rock!

title: Isn't He Wonderful
author: Anonymous

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Eyes have seen, ears have heard,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Since that day on the cross,
When He died to save the lost,
Sinful men have turned Him down by the score.

title: Near the Cross
author: Fanny J. Crosby (1820-1915)

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus, keep me near the cross,
Free to all, a healing stream,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Near the cross! O lamb of God,
Help me walk from day to day

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Near the cross! I'll watch and wait,
Till I reach the golden strand,

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: In the cross, in the cross
Till my raptured soul shall find

title: Now I Belong to Jesus
author: Norman J. Clayton

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus, my Lord will love me forever,
From Him no power of evil can sever,
He gave His life to ransom my soul;

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Once I was lost in sin's degradation,
Jesus came down to bring me salvation,
Lifted me up from sorrow and shame,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Joy floods my soul for Jesus has saved me,
Freed me from sin that long had enslaved me
His precious blood, He gave to redeem,

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Not for the years of time alone,

title: Jesus Shall Reign
author: Isaac Watts

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus shall reign where'er the sun
His kingdom stretch from shore to shore,
Till moons shall wax and wane no more.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: To him shall endless prayer be made,
And praises throng to crown his head.
His name like sweet perfume shall rise

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: The prisoner leaps to lose his chains,
And all the sons of want are blest.

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Let every creature rise and bring
And earth repeat the loud Amen.

title: Jesus Calls Us
author: Cecil Frances Alexander

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus calls us; o'er the tumult
Of our life's wild, restless sea;
Day by day His sweet voice soundeth,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Jesus calls us from the worship
Of the vain world's golden store,
From each idol that would keep us,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: In our joys and in our sorrows,
Days of toil and hours of ease,
Still He calls, in cares and pleasures,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: Jesus calls us-- by Thy mercies,
Saviour, may we hear Thy call;
Give our hearts to Thy obedience,
Serve and love Thee best of all.

title: Kneel at the Cross
author: Charles E. Moody

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Kneel at the cross, Christ will meet you there
Come, while He waits for you;
List to His voice, leave with Him your care,

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Kneel at the cross, there is room for all
Bliss there awaits, harm can ne'er befall

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Kneel at the cross, give your idols up,
Turn not away to life's sparkling cup

title: Something worth living for
author: Dale Oldham

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Life was shattered and hope was gone;
Crushing the load that I bore;
Then out of the depths I cried,
"O God, give me something worth living for."

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: There, with life at its lowest ebb,
Then He came and mended my broken heart,
He gave me something worth living for.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Oh, the joy of sins forgiven,
There's nothing the same as before.
My life overflows since Jesus came
And gave me something worth living for.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Something more than wealth or fame,
He gave me something worth living for.

title: Where could I go?
author: James B. Coats

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Living below in this old sinful world,
Striving alone to face temptations sore,
Where could I go, but to the Lord?

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Life here is grand with friends I love so dear,
Comfort I get from God's own Word;
Yet when I face the chilling hand of death,
Where could I go, but to the Lord?

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Where could I go, O where could I go?
Seeking a refuge for my soul?
Needing a friend to save me in the end,
Where could I go, but to the Lord?

title: Love divine, all loves excelling
author: Singing Saints

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Joy of heaven, to earth come down;

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Let us all Thy grace receive.
Follow in Thy steps and never,
Then our hearts will yield their blessing,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Till in heaven we take our place,
Then to worship, and adore Thee,
Lost in wonder, love, and praise.

title: Lord Jesus I love Thee
author: Singing Saints

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: My Jesus, I love Thee, I know Thou art mine,
My Rock and my Fortress, my Surety divine;
My gracious Redeemer, my song shall be now,
'Tis Thou who art worthy, Lord Jesus 'tis Thou.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: I love Thee because Thou hast first loved me,
And purchased my pardon on Calvary's tree;
I love Thee for wearing the thorns on Thy brow;
'Tis Thou who art worthy, Lord Jesus 'tis Thou.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: And when the bright morn of Thy glory shall come,
And the children ascend to the Father's glad home,
I'll shout, with Thy likeness impressed on my brow,
'Tis Thou who art worthy, Lord Jesus, 'tis Thou.

title: He the pearly gates will open
author: Singing Saints

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Love divine, so great and wondrous,
Coming from the heart of Jesus,
Just the same through tests of time!.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: Like a dove, when hunted, frightened,
As a wounded fawn was I;
Broken hearted, yet He healed me,
He will heed the sinner's cry.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: Love divine, so great and wondrous,
All my sins He then forgave;
I will sing His praise forever,
For His blood, His power to save.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: He the pearly gates will open,
So that I may enter in;
And forgave me all my sins.

title: I'd Rather Live in Heaven
author: Luther G. Presley

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Men strive for the wealth of this wide, wicked world;
They seek after honor and fame;
So lavishly sporting their diamonds and pearls,
They put the dear Savior to shame.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: They seem not to know that their treasures will rust,
That thieves often break through and steal;
Contented with pleasure, they follow their lust,

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: What profit is found in earth's silver and gold?
How sad at the close of life's day
If, for the exchange one must lose his own soul,
From heaven's door be turned away.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: Than to own all earth's silver and gold;
Than the diamonds of a palace to hold;
Live in a shack by the road,
Than to own all earth's treasures,
With no title to a future abode.

title: More, more about Jesus
author: Eliza E. Hewitt

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: More about Jesus would I know,
More of His grace to others show;
More of His saving fullness see,
More of His love, who died for me.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: More about Jesus let me learn,
More of His holy will discern;
Spirit of God, my Teacher be,
Showing the things of Christ to me.

stanzas.label: Verse 3
lines: More about Jesus in His Word,
Hearing His voice in every line,

stanzas.label: Verse 4
lines: More about Jesus on His throne,
Riches in glory all His own;
More of His kingdom's sure increase,
More of His coming, Prince of Peace.

stanzas.label: Chorus
lines: More of His saving fulness see,
More of His love, who died for me.

title: My glorious Victor, Prince divine
author: Singing Saints

stanzas.label: Verse 1
lines: Clasp these surrendered hands in Thine;
At length my will is all Thine own,
Glad vassal of a Savior's throne.

stanzas.label: Verse 2
lines: My Master, lead me to Thy door;
Pierce this now willing ear once more;
Thy bonds are freedom; let me stay
